packages.name: box2d
packages.description: Box2D rigid-body physics: worlds of static, dynamic and kinematic bodies built from box, circle and polygon shapes

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new creates an empty world. Options: gravity ({x, y}, default {x: 0, y:
9.8}, so with y pointing down things fall down the screen).

functions.name: newWorld
functions.doc:
newWorld creates a world with the given gravity; anything that isn't a
vector means {x: 0, y: 9.8}.

Deprecated: use box2d.new({gravity: {x, y}}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use box2d.new({gravity: {x, y}}) instead.

functions.name: vec
functions.signature: box2d.vec(x: number, y: number) -> {x: number, y: number}
functions.doc: vec builds a vector {x, y}.

methods.name: advance
methods.signature: world.advance(ms: number, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
advance runs the simulation forward by ms milliseconds; call it once a
frame with the frame's duration. Options: velocityIterations (default 8)
and positionIterations (default 3), the solver's accuracy per step. Fails
with StateError when the world has been destroyed; throws ValueError for a
negative duration.

methods.name: bodyCount
methods.doc:
bodyCount returns how many bodies the world holds. Throws StateError when
the world has been destroyed.

methods.name: contactCount
methods.doc:
contactCount returns how many shape pairs are touching or close to it.
Throws StateError when the world has been destroyed.

methods.name: createBody
methods.doc:
createBody adds a body to the world and returns it. Options: type
("static" (default), "dynamic" or "kinematic"), position ({x, y}; or x and
y), angle (radians), velocity ({x, y} units per second), angularVelocity
(radians per second), linearDamping, angularDamping, gravityScale
(default 1), allowSleep (default true), awake (default true),
fixedRotation, bullet and active (default true). A body has no shape until
addBox, addCircle or addPolygon gives it one. Throws StateError when the
world has been destroyed.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc:
destroy frees the world and all its bodies. Destroying it again does
nothing; any other use of the world or its bodies afterwards is a
StateError.

methods.name: destroyBody
methods.doc:
destroyBody removes a body from the world and returns false when it was
already removed, belongs to another world, or the world is destroyed.

Deprecated: use body.destroy() instead.

methods.name: gravity
methods.doc:
gravity returns the world's gravity {x, y}. Throws StateError when the
world has been destroyed.

methods.name: isDestroyed
methods.doc: isDestroyed reports whether destroy has been called on the world.

methods.name: setGravity
methods.doc:
setGravity changes the world's gravity to a vector {x, y}. Fails with
StateError when the world has been destroyed.

methods.name: step
methods.doc:
step runs the simulation forward by dt seconds, with optional velocity and
position iteration counts, and returns false when the world has been
destroyed.

Deprecated: use world.advance(ms, {velocityIterations, positionIterations}) instead; it takes milliseconds.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use world.advance(ms, {velocityIterations, positionIterations}) instead; it takes milliseconds.

methods.name: addBox
methods.signature: body.addBox(width: number, height: number, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
addBox attaches a width by height rectangle centred on the body. Options:
density (default 1), friction (default 0.2), restitution (bounciness,
default 0) and sensor (detects contacts without colliding). Fails with
StateError when the body or its world has been destroyed; throws
ValueError for a size that isn't positive.

methods.name: addCircle
methods.signature: body.addCircle(radius: number, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
addCircle attaches a circle. Options: center ({x, y} relative to the body,
default {x: 0, y: 0}) and the shape options of addBox. Fails with
StateError when the body or its world has been destroyed; throws
ValueError for a radius that isn't positive.

methods.name: addPolygon
methods.signature: body.addPolygon(points: array, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
addPolygon attaches a convex polygon with 3 to 8 points {x, y} relative
to the body. Takes the shape options of addBox. Fails with StateError when
the body or its world has been destroyed; throws ValueError for too few or
too many points.

methods.name: angle
methods.doc:
angle returns the body's rotation in radians. Throws StateError when the
body or its world has been destroyed.

methods.name: applyForce
methods.doc:
applyForce pushes the body's centre with a force {x, y} for the next
advance, waking it. Fails with StateError when the body or its world has
been destroyed.

methods.name: applyImpulse
awake
methods.doc:
awake reports whether the body is awake, or false when it was destroyed.

Deprecated: use body.isAwake() instead.

methods.name: bodyType
methods.doc:
bodyType returns "static", "dynamic" or "kinematic". Throws StateError when
the body or its world has been destroyed.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc:
destroy removes the body from its world. Destroying it again, or after
the world was destroyed, does nothing.

methods.name: isAwake
methods.doc:
isAwake reports whether the body is being simulated rather than resting
asleep. A destroyed body is not awake.

methods.name: isDestroyed
methods.doc:
isDestroyed reports whether the body, or the world it belongs to, has been
destroyed.

methods.name: linearVelocity
methods.doc:
linearVelocity returns the body's velocity {x, y} in units per second.
Throws StateError when the body or its world has been destroyed.

methods.name: mass
methods.doc:
mass returns the body's mass, which its shapes' density and area decide.
Throws StateError when the body or its world has been destroyed.

methods.name: position
methods.doc:
position returns the body's position {x, y} in world units. Throws
StateError when the body or its world has been destroyed.

methods.name: setLinearVelocity
methods.doc:
setLinearVelocity sets the body's velocity {x, y} in units per second.
Fails with StateError when the body or its world has been destroyed.

methods.name: setTransform
methods.signature: body.setTransform(position: any, angle: number) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
setTransform moves the body to position {x, y} with rotation angle in
radians. Fails with StateError when the body or its world has been
destroyed.

packages.name: cache
packages.description: In-memory key-value caches that evict the least recently used entry and expire entries after a time to live.

functions.name: create
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use cache.new({capacity: capacity, ttl: milliseconds}) instead.

functions.name: createDefault
functions.doc:
createDefault makes a cache of 100 entries that live 300 seconds.

Deprecated: use cache.new() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use cache.new() instead.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new creates an empty cache. Options: capacity (the most entries it holds
before evicting the least recently used one, default 100) and ttl (how
long an entry lives after it is set, in milliseconds, default 300000, five
minutes). Throws ValueError for a capacity below 1 or a ttl that isn't
above 0.

methods.name: cleanupExpired
methods.doc:
cleanupExpired removes every expired entry now instead of when it is next
read, and returns how many it removed.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: clear removes every entry from the cache.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
delete removes key from the cache, returning true when it held a live
entry and false when there was nothing to remove.

methods.name: deleteMany
methods.doc:
deleteMany removes every key in keys, an array of strings, and returns how
many held a live entry.

methods.name: entries
methods.doc:
entries returns the live entries as an object of key to value, without
changing their recency.

methods.name: expire
methods.doc:
expire gives the live entry under key a new lifetime of ttl milliseconds
from now; a ttl of 0 removes it at once. Returns true when key held a live
entry and false when there was nothing to change. Throws ValueError for a
negative ttl.

methods.name: fetch
methods.doc:
fetch returns the live value under key, or calls loader() and stores and
returns what it gives back when key is missing or expired. Concurrent
fetches of one key wait for a single loader call. Throws StateError when
the loader fetches its own key, which would otherwise wait forever, and
lets an error the loader throws propagate without storing anything.

methods.name: filter
methods.doc:
filter returns an object of the live entries for which fn(key, value)
returns true. The cache is unchanged.

methods.name: forEach
methods.doc:
forEach calls fn(key, value) for each live entry, from most to least
recently used.

methods.name: get
getMany
methods.doc:
getMany returns an object holding the live entries among keys.

Deprecated: use cache.Cache.pick(keys) instead.

methods.name: getOrSet
methods.doc:
getOrSet returns the value under key, storing value first when key is
missing.

Deprecated: use cache.Cache.fetch(key, loader) instead, with a loader that
returns value.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use cache.Cache.fetch(key, loader) instead, with a loader that returns value.

methods.name: getOrSetFunc
methods.doc:
getOrSetFunc returns the value under key, storing fn() first when key is
missing.

Deprecated: use cache.Cache.fetch(key, loader) instead.

methods.name: getTTL
methods.doc:
getTTL returns the seconds the entry under key has left, 0 when it has
just expired and -1 when it is missing.

Deprecated: use cache.Cache.ttl(key) instead, which returns milliseconds
or null.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use cache.Cache.ttl(key) instead, which returns milliseconds or null.

methods.name: has
methods.doc:
has reports whether key holds a live (unexpired) entry, even one holding
null. It doesn't change the entry's recency.

methods.name: info
methods.signature: cache.info() -> {capacity: int, size: int, ttl: number}
methods.doc:
info describes the cache as a record with the keys size (live entries),
capacity and ttl (the default lifetime in milliseconds).

methods.name: keys
methods.doc: keys returns the keys of the live entries, in no particular order.

methods.name: mapValues
methods.doc:
mapValues returns an object of every live key with the value fn(key,
value) returns for it. The cache is unchanged.

methods.name: pick
methods.doc:
pick returns an object holding the live entries among keys, an array of
strings; missing and expired keys are left out. Each entry read becomes
most recently used.

methods.name: reduce
methods.doc:
reduce folds the live values, from most to least recently used, into one
result: it starts from initial and replaces it with fn(result, value) for
each value.

methods.name: set
methods.signature: cache.set(key: string, value: any, options?: object)
methods.doc:
set stores value under key, replacing any earlier value, and marks it most
recently used. When the cache is full the least recently used entry is
evicted. Option: ttl, this entry's lifetime in milliseconds (default: the
cache's ttl). Mutates the cache; throws ValueError for a negative ttl.

methods.name: setMany
methods.doc: setMany stores every key and value of entries, as set would one at a time.

methods.name: setTTL
methods.doc:
setTTL gives the entry under key a new lifetime in seconds.

Deprecated: use cache.Cache.expire(key, milliseconds) instead.

methods.name: size
methods.doc: size returns the number of live entries.

methods.name: stats
methods.doc:
stats describes the cache with the keys size, capacity, ttl (seconds) and
keys.

Deprecated: use cache.Cache.info() instead, whose ttl is in milliseconds,
and cache.Cache.keys() for the keys.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use cache.Cache.info() instead, whose ttl is in milliseconds, and cache.Cache.keys() for the keys.

methods.name: toArray
methods.signature: cache.toArray() -> {expiresAt: int64, key: string, value: any}[]
methods.doc:
toArray returns the live entries, from most to least recently used, as
records with the keys key, value and expiresAt (unix milliseconds).

methods.name: ttl
methods.doc:
ttl returns how long the entry under key has left to live, in whole
milliseconds, or null when key is missing or has expired.

methods.name: values
methods.doc:
values returns the values of the live entries, from most to least
recently used, without changing their recency.

packages.name: colors
packages.description: Parse CSS colors into OSL colors and convert, mix, lighten and darken them

functions.name: darken
functions.doc:
darken lowers color's HSL lightness by amount (0 to 1, where 1 is the
whole range, so darken(c, 1) is black). Returns "#rrggbb" or
"#rrggbbaa". Throws ValueError for an invalid color or amount.

functions.name: fromHSL
functions.doc:
fromHSL converts {h, s, l, a} (as toHSL returns it; a is optional and
defaults to 255) to a "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa" color. The hue wraps
around 360 degrees. Throws ValueError for a missing key, saturation or
lightness outside 0 to 1, or alpha outside 0-255.

functions.name: gray
functions.doc:
gray builds a grayscale {Y} from a channel that wraps modulo 256.

Deprecated: use {r: v, g: v, b: v} instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use {r: v, g: v, b: v} instead.

functions.name: hex
functions.doc:
hex parses "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa" into {R, G, B, A}, giving opaque black
for anything else.

Deprecated: use colors.parse(text) instead, which reports invalid input.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use colors.parse(text) instead, which reports invalid input.

functions.name: lighten
functions.doc:
lighten raises color's HSL lightness by amount (0 to 1, where 1 is the
whole range, so lighten(c, 1) is white). Returns "#rrggbb" or
"#rrggbbaa". Throws ValueError for an invalid color or amount.

functions.name: mix
functions.signature: colors.mix(a: any, b: any, amount: number) -> string
functions.doc:
mix blends two colors channel by channel, alpha included: amount 0 gives
a, 1 gives b and 0.5 the midpoint. Returns "#rrggbb" or "#rrggbbaa".
Throws ValueError for an invalid color or an amount outside 0 to 1.

functions.name: nrgba
functions.signature: colors.nrgba(r: any, g: any, b: any, a: any) -> object
functions.doc:
nrgba builds {R, G, B, A} from four channels, which wrap modulo 256.

Deprecated: use {r: r, g: g, b: b, a: a} instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use {r: r, g: g, b: b, a: a} instead.

functions.name: parse
functions.signature: colors.parse(text: string) -> result<{a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}, error>
functions.returns: result<{a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}, error>
functions.doc:
parse reads a CSS color and returns it as {r, g, b, a} with 0-255
channels, which every OSL color argument accepts. It understands
"#rgb", "#rgba", "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa", the CSS color names (such as
"red" and "rebeccapurple"), "transparent", rgb()/rgba() and
hsl()/hsla() with commas or spaces, percentages and an optional
"/ alpha", in any case. Fails with ParseError for anything else.

functions.name: rgb
functions.signature: colors.rgb(r: any, g: any, b: any) -> object
functions.doc:
rgb builds an opaque {R, G, B, A} from three channels, which wrap modulo
256.

Deprecated: use {r: r, g: g, b: b} or colors.stringify instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use {r: r, g: g, b: b} or colors.stringify instead.

functions.name: rgba
functions.signature: colors.rgba(r: any, g: any, b: any, a: any) -> object
functions.doc:
rgba builds {R, G, B, A} from four channels, which wrap modulo 256.

Deprecated: use {r: r, g: g, b: b, a: a} or colors.stringify instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use {r: r, g: g, b: b, a: a} or colors.stringify instead.

functions.name: stringify
functions.doc:
stringify returns color as "#rrggbb", or "#rrggbbaa" when it isn't fully
opaque. color is a CSS color string or {r, g, b, a}. Throws ValueError
for an invalid color.

functions.name: toHSL
functions.signature: colors.toHSL(color: any) -> {a: int, h: number, l: number, s: number}
functions.returns: {a: int, h: number, l: number, s: number}
functions.doc:
toHSL converts color to {h, s, l, a}: hue in degrees from 0 to 360,
saturation and lightness from 0 to 1, and alpha 0-255. Throws ValueError
for an invalid color.

packages.name: cron
packages.description: Run functions on five-field cron schedules from a background scheduler.
packages.about:
A schedule has five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of
week. Each is *, a value, a range, a step or a comma-separated list; when
both day fields are restricted, either can match. Times are local.

methods.name: add
methods.signature: scheduler.add(name: string, schedule: string, fn: any)
methods.doc:
add registers fn to run on schedule under name, enabled. Throws ValueError
when the schedule is invalid or never fires or a job already has that
name, and TypeError when fn isn't a function.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: clear removes every job.

methods.name: disable
methods.doc:
disable stops the job called name from running on its schedule; run can
still run it. Throws NotFoundError when there is no such job.

methods.name: enable
methods.doc:
enable lets the job called name run on its schedule again, from its next
matching time. Throws NotFoundError when there is no such job.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: has reports whether a job called name exists.

methods.name: isEnabled
methods.doc: isEnabled reports whether a job called name exists and is enabled.

methods.name: isRunning
methods.doc: isRunning reports whether start has been called without a later stop.

methods.name: job
methods.signature: scheduler.job(name: string) -> {enabled: boolean, lastRun: int?, name: string, nextRun: int?, runCount: int, running: boolean, schedule: string}?
methods.returns: {enabled: boolean, lastRun: int?, name: string, nextRun: int?, runCount: int, running: boolean, schedule: string}?
methods.doc:
job describes the job called name, or returns null when there is none.
Keys: name, schedule, enabled, running (a run is in progress), nextRun
(unix ms, null while disabled), lastRun (unix ms, null before the first
run) and runCount.

methods.name: jobs
methods.signature: scheduler.jobs() -> {enabled: boolean, lastRun: int?, name: string, nextRun: int?, runCount: int, running: boolean, schedule: string}[]
methods.returns: {enabled: boolean, lastRun: int?, name: string, nextRun: int?, runCount: int, running: boolean, schedule: string}[]
methods.doc: jobs describes every job, sorted by name, with the keys job returns.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
remove deletes the job called name; removing a job that doesn't exist
does nothing. A run already in progress finishes.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
run runs the job called name now, on the calling thread, even when it is
disabled, and returns when it finishes. An error the job throws
propagates. Throws NotFoundError when there is no such job.

methods.name: runAll
methods.doc:
runAll runs every enabled job now, one after another in name order, on
the calling thread. Every job runs even if an earlier one throws; then
the first error is rethrown.

methods.name: start
methods.doc:
start runs enabled jobs in the background whenever their schedule
matches, checking every second, until stop is called. Starting a running
scheduler does nothing. A job that is still running when it is due again
is skipped, and a job that throws has its error printed while the
scheduler keeps running. The program still exits when its main code
ends, so keep it alive (for example with a thread that waits) while jobs
should run.

methods.name: stop
methods.doc:
stop stops running jobs on their schedules; runs in progress finish.
Stopping a scheduler that isn't running does nothing.

packages.name: crypto
packages.description: Hashes, HMACs, password hashing, authenticated encryption, Ed25519 signatures and secure random values.

functions.name: aes256Decrypt
functions.signature: crypto.aes256Decrypt(data: string, key: byte[]) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
aes256Decrypt decrypts text from crypto.aes256Encrypt with the same
32-byte key. Fails with ValueError for a key that isn't 32 bytes,
ParseError when data isn't aes256Encrypt's output and PermissionError
for the wrong key or modified data.

functions.name: aes256Encrypt
functions.signature: crypto.aes256Encrypt(data: byte[], key: byte[]) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
aes256Encrypt encrypts data with AES-256-GCM under key and returns hex
text that crypto.aes256Decrypt reads. key is exactly 32 random bytes,
such as crypto.fromHex(crypto.randomHex(32)).unwrap(); to encrypt with a
password, use crypto.encrypt(data, password), which stretches it. Every
call uses a fresh random nonce, and the result is authenticated, so
tampering is detected. Fails with ValueError for a key that isn't 32
bytes.

functions.name: base64Decode
functions.doc:
base64Decode decodes standard base64, returning "" for invalid input.

Deprecated: use atob(text) instead.

functions.doc:
base64Encode encodes data as standard base64.

functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use btoa(data) instead.

functions.doc:
bcryptHash hashes a password with bcrypt at the given cost (default 10),
returning "" for a cost outside 4 to 31 or a password it can't hash.

Deprecated: use crypto.hashPassword(password, {algorithm: "bcrypt",
cost: n}) instead, or crypto.hashPassword(password) for Argon2id.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use crypto.hashPassword(password, {algorithm: "bcrypt", cost: n}) instead, or crypto.hashPassword(password) for Argon2id.

bcryptVerify reports whether password matches a bcrypt hash.

functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use crypto.verifyPassword(password, hash) instead, which checks bcrypt hashes too.

functions.doc:
binDecode reads space-separated binary bytes, returning "" for invalid

functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use text.decodeBin() instead, which fails with ParseError for invalid input.

functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use text.encodeBin() instead.

functions.name: constantTimeCompare
functions.doc:
constantTimeCompare reports whether a and b are equal, taking the same
time wherever they differ, so comparing a secret such as an HMAC doesn't
leak how much of it matched.

functions.name: decrypt
functions.signature: crypto.decrypt(data: string, password: string) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
decrypt decrypts text from crypto.encrypt with the same password,
including text from earlier versions of encrypt. Fails with ParseError
when data isn't encrypt's output and with PermissionError for the wrong
password or modified data.

functions.name: decryptFile
functions.signature: crypto.decryptFile(inputPath: string, outputPath: string, password: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
decryptFile decrypts a file written by crypto.encryptFile with the same
password and writes the original bytes to outputPath, readable only by
its owner when new. Fails like crypto.decrypt for the wrong password or
a file that isn't encrypted, and with NotFoundError, PermissionError or
IOError when a file can't be read or written.

functions.name: deriveKey
functions.signature: crypto.deriveKey(password: string, salt: byte[], options?: object) -> string
functions.doc:
deriveKey derives a key from a password and salt with PBKDF2 and returns
it as hex. Use a random salt of at least 16 bytes and store it with the
result. Options: iterations (default 600000), length in bytes (default
32) and hash (default "sha256", any name crypto.hash accepts). Throws
ValueError for iterations or a length below 1 or an unknown hash.

functions.name: ed25519GenerateKeyPair
functions.doc:
ed25519GenerateKeyPair returns a new Ed25519 key pair as {private,
public}: the 32-byte private seed and the public key, each as unpadded
base64url text. Keep private secret; share public so others can check
your signatures with crypto.ed25519Verify.

functions.name: ed25519Sign
functions.doc:
ed25519Sign signs data with an Ed25519 private key, given as base64url
or hex (the 32-byte seed or the 64-byte private key), and returns the
signature as unpadded base64url text. Throws ValueError for a key that
isn't one of those.

functions.name: ed25519Verify
functions.signature: crypto.ed25519Verify(publicKey: string, data: byte[], signature: string) -> boolean
functions.doc:
ed25519Verify reports whether signature, as base64url, is a valid
Ed25519 signature of data by the holder of publicKey, given as base64url
or hex. A malformed key or signature is false.

functions.name: encrypt
functions.doc:
encrypt encrypts data with a password and returns text that
crypto.decrypt turns back into data with the same password. The password
is stretched with Argon2id and a random salt, and the data is sealed with
AES-256-GCM, so the result reveals nothing but the data's length and any
change to it is detected.

functions.name: encryptFile
functions.signature: crypto.encryptFile(inputPath: string, outputPath: string, password: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
encryptFile encrypts the file at inputPath with a password, like
crypto.encrypt, and writes the text to outputPath. Fails with
NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when a file can't be read or
written.

functions.name: fromHex
functions.doc:
fromHex decodes hexadecimal text, in either case, to bytes. Fails with
ParseError for an odd length or a character that isn't a hex digit.

functions.name: generateKeyPair
functions.doc:
generateKeyPair returns a new Ed25519 key pair as hex text.

Deprecated: use crypto.ed25519GenerateKeyPair() instead, which encodes
the keys as base64url like the signatures; both encodings sign and
verify.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use crypto.ed25519GenerateKeyPair() instead, which encodes the keys as base64url like the signatures; both encodings sign and verify.

functions.name: hash
functions.doc:
hash returns the hex digest of data with the named algorithm: md5, sha1,
sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha3-224, sha3-256, sha3-384 or
sha3-512, in any case. A string is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes. Throws
ValueError for an unknown algorithm.

functions.name: hashDirectory
functions.signature: crypto.hashDirectory(path: string, options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
hashDirectory returns one hex digest for every file below a directory,
covering each file's path relative to it and its contents, so it changes
when a file is added, removed, renamed or edited. Option: algorithm
(default "sha256"). Fails with UnsupportedError when the tree contains a
symbolic link, and with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when it
can't be read.

functions.name: hashFile
functions.signature: crypto.hashFile(path: string, options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
hashFile returns the hex digest of a file's contents, reading it in
pieces so large files don't have to fit in memory. Option: algorithm
(default "sha256", any name crypto.hash accepts). Fails with
NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be read.

functions.name: hashPassword
functions.signature: crypto.hashPassword(password: string, options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
hashPassword hashes a password for storage, with a random salt, so it
can later be checked with crypto.verifyPassword. It uses Argon2id by
default, giving a "$argon2id$..." string. Options: algorithm ("argon2id"
or "bcrypt") and cost (bcrypt's work factor from 4 to 31, default 10).
Fails with ValueError when bcrypt is asked to hash a password longer than
its limit of 72 bytes; throws ValueError for a bad option.

functions.doc:
hexDecode decodes hex text, returning "" when it isn't valid hex.

functions.doc:

crypto.constantTimeCompare. Throws ValueError for an unknown algorithm.

functions.name: md5
functions.doc:
md5 returns the hex MD5 digest of data. MD5 is broken for security; use

functions.doc:

functions.doc:
needsRehash reports whether a stored password hash is weaker than what
crypto.hashPassword produces now: a bcrypt or old salted SHA-256 hash,

crypto.verifyPassword, store crypto.hashPassword(password) in its place.

functions.name: pbkdf2
functions.signature: crypto.pbkdf2(password: any, salt: any, iterations: any, keyLen: any, hashFunc: any) -> string
functions.doc:
pbkdf2 derives a PBKDF2 key as hex, returning "" for bad arguments.

functions.name: random
functions.doc:
random returns a random whole number from min up to but not including

functions.name: randomBetween
functions.doc:
randomBetween returns a cryptographically secure random whole number
from min to max, including both ends, like random.between. The bounds
may come in either order.

functions.doc:
randomBytes returns size random bytes as hex, or "" for a size of 0 or

functions.name: randomFloat
functions.doc:
randomFloat returns a cryptographically secure random number.
randomFloat() is from 0 up to but not including 1, randomFloat(max) from
0 up to max, and randomFloat(min, max) from min up to max, or min when
max isn't above it. Throws TypeError for more than two arguments or one
that isn't a number.

functions.name: randomHex
functions.doc:
randomHex returns size cryptographically secure random bytes as hex, so
the text is twice size characters long. Throws ValueError for a size
outside 0 to 16777216.

functions.name: randomInt
functions.doc:
randomInt returns a random whole number from 0 up to but not including
max, or from min up to but not including max. Throws TypeError without

Deprecated: use crypto.randomBetween(min, max) instead, whose bounds
are both included.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use crypto.randomBetween(min, max) instead, whose bounds are both included.

functions.name: randomString
functions.doc:
randomString returns length cryptographically secure random letters and
digits, or characters of alphabet when given, as in
crypto.randomString(6, "0123456789"). Throws ValueError for a length
outside 0 to 16777216 or an empty alphabet.

functions.name: randomUUID
functions.doc:
randomUUID returns a random version 4 UUID, such as
"3b241101-e2bb-4255-8caf-4136c566a962".

functions.name: secureErase
functions.doc:
secureErase overwrites a file's contents with random bytes three times,
flushing each pass to the device, and then deletes it. This is best
effort: on SSDs, copy-on-write or journaling filesystems, and wherever
backups or snapshots exist, copies of the old data can survive, so use
full-disk encryption when that matters. Fails with UnsupportedError for
anything but a regular file, and with NotFoundError, PermissionError or
IOError when it can't be written or removed.

functions.doc:
writeFileRows writes objects as a CSV file and reports success.

Deprecated: use fs.writeFile(path, csv.stringify(records)) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.writeFile(path, csv.stringify(records)) instead.

packages.name: date
packages.description: Dates, times and durations: date.DateTime instants in UTC, time zones, arithmetic, formatting and parsing.

functions.name: daysInMonth
functions.doc:
daysInMonth returns how many days month (1 to 12) of year has. Throws
ValueError for any other month.

functions.name: duration
functions.doc:
duration returns a duration of value microseconds.

Deprecated: use date.millis(ms) instead; it takes milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use date.millis(ms) instead; it takes milliseconds.

functions.name: fromUnix
functions.doc:
fromUnix returns the instant seconds after the Unix epoch (1970-01-01
UTC); negative values are before it.

functions.name: fromUnixMicros
functions.doc: fromUnixMicros returns the instant us microseconds after the Unix epoch.

functions.name: fromUnixMillis
functions.doc: fromUnixMillis returns the instant ms milliseconds after the Unix epoch.

functions.name: fromUnixMs
functions.doc:
fromUnixMs returns the instant ms milliseconds after the Unix epoch.

Deprecated: use date.fromUnixMillis(ms) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use date.fromUnixMillis(ms) instead.

functions.name: fromUnixUs
functions.doc:
fromUnixUs returns the instant us microseconds after the Unix epoch.

Deprecated: use date.fromUnixMicros(us) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use date.fromUnixMicros(us) instead.

functions.name: isLeap
functions.doc: isLeap reports whether year has a 29 February.

functions.name: millis
functions.doc:
millis returns a duration of ms milliseconds; fractions keep microsecond
precision. Throws ValueError for NaN or an infinite or out-of-range ms.

functions.name: now
functions.doc: now returns the current instant.

functions.name: nowUs
functions.doc:
nowUs returns the current time in microseconds since the Unix epoch.

Deprecated: use date.now().unixMicros() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use date.now().unixMicros() instead.

functions.name: parse
functions.signature: date.parse(text: string, options?: object) -> result<date.DateTime, error>
functions.doc:
parse reads a date or date-time from text. Without a format it accepts
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 forms: "2024-03-01", "2024-03-01T12:30",
"2024-03-01 12:30:05", "2024-03-01T12:30:05.250Z" and
"2024-03-01T12:30:05+02:00". Options: format (a layout using the same
tokens as dt.format, such as "DD/MM/YYYY HH:mm"; [text] and \x are
literal) and timezone (the IANA zone for text without an offset, default
"UTC"). Missing fields default to the start of the period. Fails with
ParseError when text doesn't match; throws ValueError for an unknown
time zone or a layout token that can't be parsed (z).

constants.name: day
constants.doc:
Day is one day in milliseconds, 86400000. A calendar day across a
daylight saving change can be an hour longer or shorter.

constants.name: hour
constants.doc: Hour is one hour in milliseconds, 3600000.

constants.name: minute
constants.doc: Minute is one minute in milliseconds, 60000.

constants.name: second
constants.doc: Second is one second in milliseconds, 1000.

constants.name: week
constants.doc: Week is seven days in milliseconds, 604800000.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
add returns the instant moved forward by value units, leaving dt alone.
unit is "us", "ms", "s", "m", "h", "d", "mo" or "y", or the long name
("minutes", "day", ...). Months and years move by calendar (31 January
plus a month is 2 or 3 March) and need whole numbers; days are 24 hours
in UTC. Throws ValueError for an unknown unit, a fractional month or
year, or a result out of range.

methods.name: addDuration
methods.doc:
addDuration returns the instant moved by duration. Throws ValueError
when the result is out of range.

methods.name: after
methods.doc: after reports whether dt is later than other.

methods.name: before
methods.doc: before reports whether dt is earlier than other.

methods.name: compare
methods.doc: compare returns -1, 0 or 1 as dt is before, equal to or after other.

methods.name: equals
methods.doc: equals reports whether dt and other are the same instant.

methods.name: format
methods.doc:
format writes the instant in UTC using layout tokens: YYYY YY (year),
MMMM MMM MM M (month), DD D (day), dddd ddd (weekday), HH H (24-hour),
hh h (12-hour), A a (AM/PM), mm m (minute), ss s (second), SSS SSSSSS
(fraction), Z ZZ (offset), z (zone name), X (unix seconds) and x (unix
microseconds). [text] and \x are written literally.

methods.name: inTimezone
methods.doc:
inTimezone returns a view of the instant in the IANA time zone tz, such
as "Europe/London", for formatting local times. Fails with ValueError
for an unknown zone.

methods.name: iso
methods.doc:
iso writes the instant as RFC 3339 text in UTC, such as
"2024-03-01T12:30:00Z".

methods.name: round
methods.doc:
round returns the start of the UTC period that dt falls in; despite the
name it never rounds up.

Deprecated: use dt.truncate(unit) instead.

methods.name: since
methods.doc: since returns the time from other to dt, negative when other is later.

methods.name: subtract
methods.doc: subtract returns the instant moved back by value units; see dt.add.

methods.name: truncate
methods.doc:
truncate returns the start of the UTC day, hour, minute, second or
millisecond ("d", "h", "m", "s", "ms" or their long names) that dt falls
in, leaving dt alone. Throws ValueError for any other unit.

methods.name: unix
methods.doc:
unix returns the instant in whole seconds since the Unix epoch, rounded
down.

methods.name: unixMicros
methods.doc: unixMicros returns the instant in microseconds since the Unix epoch.

methods.name: unixMillis
methods.doc:
unixMillis returns the instant in whole milliseconds since the Unix
epoch, rounded down.

methods.name: unixMs
methods.doc:
unixMs returns the instant in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

Deprecated: use dt.unixMillis() instead.

methods.name: unixUs
methods.doc:
unixUs returns the instant in microseconds since the Unix epoch.

Deprecated: use dt.unixMicros() instead.

methods.name: until
methods.doc: until returns the time from dt to other, negative when other is earlier.

methods.name: with
methods.doc:
with returns the instant with one UTC calendar field replaced, leaving dt
alone. field is "year", "month" (1 to 12), "day", "hour", "minute" or
"second", or the short unit name ("y", "mo", "d", "h", "m", "s").
Out-of-range values roll over, as 31 February becomes 2 or 3 March.
Throws ValueError for an unknown field or a result out of range.

methods.name: days
methods.doc: days returns the duration in 24-hour days.

methods.name: hours
methods.doc: hours returns the duration in hours.

methods.name: micros
methods.doc: micros returns the duration in whole microseconds.

methods.name: millis
methods.doc: millis returns the duration in whole milliseconds, rounded toward zero.

methods.name: minutes
methods.doc: minutes returns the duration in minutes.

methods.name: seconds
methods.doc: seconds returns the duration in seconds.

methods.name: format
methods.doc:
format writes the instant in the zone using the layout tokens of
dt.format.

methods.name: iso
methods.doc:
iso writes the instant as RFC 3339 text in the zone, with its offset,
such as "2024-03-01T07:30:00-05:00".

methods.name: timezone
methods.doc: timezone returns the zone's IANA name, such as "Europe/London".

methods.name: toDateTime
methods.doc: toDateTime returns the instant without its zone.

packages.name: db
packages.description: SQLite databases with SQL queries and JSON document collections.

functions.name: open
functions.doc:
open opens the SQLite database file at path, creating it when it doesn't
exist; ":memory:" opens a private in-memory database. Fails with
NotFoundError when path's directory doesn't exist, ParseError when the
file isn't an SQLite database, and PermissionError or IOError when it
can't be opened. Close the handle with db.close() when done.

functions.name: openMemory
functions.doc:
openMemory opens a private in-memory database, or returns null on
failure.

Deprecated: use db.open(":memory:") instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use db.open(":memory:") instead.

constants.name: asc
constants.doc: Asc is the "asc" sort direction, for query.sort(field, db.asc).
constants.deprecated: write the direction as the string "asc" instead

constants.name: contains
constants.doc: Contains is the $contains query operator, for query.where(field, db.contains, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "contains" instead

constants.name: desc
constants.doc: Desc is the "desc" sort direction, for query.sort(field, db.desc).
constants.deprecated: write the direction as the string "desc" instead

constants.name: eq
constants.doc: Eq is the $eq query operator, for query.where(field, db.eq, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "==" instead

constants.name: equal
constants.doc: Equal is the $eq query operator, for query.where(field, db.equal, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "==" instead

constants.name: greater
constants.doc: Greater is the $gt query operator, for query.where(field, db.greater, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string ">" instead

constants.name: greaterEqual
constants.doc: GreaterEqual is the $gte query operator, for query.where(field, db.greaterEqual, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string ">=" instead

constants.name: gt
constants.doc: Gt is the $gt query operator, for query.where(field, db.gt, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string ">" instead

constants.name: gte
constants.doc: Gte is the $gte query operator, for query.where(field, db.gte, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string ">=" instead

constants.name: in
constants.doc: In is the $in query operator, for query.where(field, db.in, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "in" instead

constants.name: less
constants.doc: Less is the $lt query operator, for query.where(field, db.less, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "<" instead

constants.name: lessEqual
constants.doc: LessEqual is the $lte query operator, for query.where(field, db.lessEqual, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "<=" instead

constants.name: lt
constants.doc: Lt is the $lt query operator, for query.where(field, db.lt, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "<" instead

constants.name: lte
constants.doc: Lte is the $lte query operator, for query.where(field, db.lte, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "<=" instead

constants.name: matches
constants.doc: Matches is the $regex query operator, for query.where(field, db.matches, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "matches" instead

constants.name: ne
constants.doc: Ne is the $ne query operator, for query.where(field, db.ne, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "!=" instead

constants.name: nin
constants.doc: Nin is the $nin query operator, for query.where(field, db.nin, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "notIn" instead

constants.name: notEqual
constants.doc: NotEqual is the $ne query operator, for query.where(field, db.notEqual, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "!=" instead

constants.name: notOneOf
constants.doc: NotOneOf is the $nin query operator, for query.where(field, db.notOneOf, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "notIn" instead

constants.name: oneOf
constants.doc: OneOf is the $in query operator, for query.where(field, db.oneOf, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "in" instead

constants.name: present
constants.doc: Present is the $exists query operator, for query.where(field, db.present, value).
constants.deprecated: write the operator as the string "exists" instead

methods.name: begin
methods.doc:
begin starts a transaction: every statement on this database runs in it
until commit or rollback. Throws StateError when a transaction is already
open or the database is closed; fails like db.exec.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close closes the database, rolling back a transaction that is still
open. Closing twice does nothing; any other method on a closed database
throws StateError.

methods.name: collection
methods.doc:
collection returns the document collection name, creating its table
(coll_<name>) when it doesn't exist. Throws ValueError unless name is
letters, digits, _ and -; fails like db.exec.

methods.name: collections
methods.doc:
collections returns the names of the database's collections in
alphabetical order. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: columns
commit
methods.doc:
commit saves the open transaction's changes. Throws StateError when no
transaction is open; fails like db.exec, for example with ValueError for
a deferred constraint, and the transaction is then rolled back.

methods.name: count
methods.signature: dB.count(table: string, where: string, ...whereArgs: any) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
count returns how many rows of table match the SQL condition where (with
? placeholders bound to whereArgs); an empty where counts every row.
Throws ValueError for an invalid table name; fails like db.exec.

methods.name: createTable
methods.signature: dB.createTable(table: string, columns: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
createTable creates table, unless it already exists, with one column per
key of columns, whose value is the column's SQL type and constraints
(such as "INTEGER PRIMARY KEY"). Columns are created in alphabetical
order; use db.exec with CREATE TABLE to choose the order. Throws
ValueError for an invalid name or no columns and TypeError for a type
that isn't a string; fails like db.exec.

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: dB.delete(table: string, where: string, ...whereArgs: any) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
delete removes every row of table matching the SQL condition where (with
? placeholders bound to whereArgs) and returns how many it removed.
Throws ValueError for an invalid table name or an empty where; pass "1" to
delete every row. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: dropTable
methods.doc:
dropTable deletes table and its rows; a table that doesn't exist is not
an error. Throws ValueError for an invalid name; fails like db.exec.

methods.name: exec
methods.doc:
exec runs one SQL statement, binding args to its ? placeholders. Use
db.run when you need the number of changed rows or the inserted rowid.
Used as a boolean (as in `if d.exec(...)`) it is true when the statement
succeeded. Fails with ParseError for invalid SQL, NotFoundError for a
missing table or column, ValueError for a constraint violation or the
wrong number of args, TypeError for an arg SQLite can't store, and
TimeoutError when the database is locked.

methods.name: exists
methods.signature: dB.exists(table: string, where: string, ...whereArgs: any) -> result<boolean, error>
methods.doc:
exists reports whether any row of table matches the SQL condition where,
like count. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: getColumns
methods.doc:
getColumns returns the column names of table, or [] on failure.

Deprecated: use db.columns(table) instead.

methods.name: getTables
methods.doc:
getTables returns the table names, or [] on failure.

Deprecated: use db.tables() instead.

methods.name: insert
methods.signature: dB.insert(table: string, data: object) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
insert adds a row to table with the columns and values of data and
returns its rowid. Throws ValueError for an invalid table or column name
or empty data; fails like db.exec.

methods.name: lastInsertID
methods.doc:
lastInsertID returns the rowid of the most recent successful INSERT on
this database, or 0. Prefer the lastInsertID of db.exec or the result of
db.insert, which belong to one statement. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: query
methods.doc:
query runs an SQL query, binding args to its ? placeholders, and returns
its rows as *db.Row handles (use db.queryMap for objects). Fails like
db.exec.

methods.name: queryMap
methods.doc:
queryMap runs an SQL query and returns its rows as objects keyed by
column name. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: queryMapOne
methods.doc:
queryMapOne runs an SQL query and returns its first row as an object
keyed by column name, or null when it returns no rows. Fails like
db.exec.

methods.name: queryOne
methods.doc:
queryOne runs an SQL query and returns its first row as a *db.Row, or
null when it returns no rows. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: rollback
methods.doc:
rollback discards the open transaction's changes. Throws StateError when
no transaction is open.

methods.name: rowsAffected
methods.doc:
rowsAffected runs a statement and returns how many rows it changed, or 0
on failure.

Deprecated: use db.run(query, args...).rowsAffected instead.

methods.name: run
methods.signature: dB.run(query: string, ...args: any) -> result<{lastInsertID: int, rowsAffected: int}, error>
methods.doc:
run runs one SQL statement like exec, binding args to its ? placeholders,
and returns a record with the keys rowsAffected and lastInsertID (the
rowid of the last inserted row, or 0). Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: tables
methods.doc:
tables returns the names of the database's tables in alphabetical order,
including the coll_ tables behind collections. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: transaction
methods.doc:
transaction runs fn(db) inside a transaction and commits it when fn
returns. When fn throws, the transaction is rolled back and the error
propagates; when fn returns an error or a failed result, the transaction
is rolled back and that error is this call's result. Throws StateError
when a transaction is already open or fn commits or rolls back itself;
fails like db.exec when the commit fails.

methods.name: update
methods.signature: dB.update(table: string, data: object, where: string, ...whereArgs: any) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
update sets the columns in data on every row of table matching the SQL
condition where (with ? placeholders bound to whereArgs) and returns how
many rows changed. Throws ValueError for an invalid name, empty data or an
empty where; pass "1" to update every row. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: columns
methods.doc: columns returns the row's column names in order.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: count returns the number of columns in the row.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get returns a column's value: column is a 1-based position or a column
name (matched ignoring case). Returns null when there is no such column.
Throws TypeError when column is neither a number nor a string.

methods.name: getByName
methods.doc:
getByName returns the value of the column named name, ignoring case.

Deprecated: use row.get(name) instead.

methods.name: isEmpty
methods.doc: isEmpty reports whether the row has no columns.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: toArray returns the row's values in column order.

methods.name: toMap
methods.doc:
toMap returns the row as an object keyed by column name. When two columns
share a name the later one wins.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: all returns every document in the collection. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: count returns how many documents match filter. Fails like find.

methods.name: deleteMany
methods.doc:
deleteMany removes every document matching filter and returns how many
it removed. Fails like find.

methods.name: deleteOne
methods.doc:
deleteOne removes the first document matching filter and returns how
many it removed, 0 or 1. Fails like find.

methods.name: drop
methods.doc: drop deletes the collection's table and documents. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc: exists reports whether any document matches filter. Fails like find.

methods.name: fields
methods.doc:
fields starts a query that returns only the named fields; see
db.Query.fields.

methods.name: find
methods.signature: collection.find(filter: object, options?: object) -> result<object[], error>
methods.doc:
find returns the documents matching filter, an object such as
{age: {$gte: 18}, role: "admin"} (see db.Collection.where for the
operators). Options: sort (an object of field to "asc" or "desc", applied
in key order), skip and limit. Throws ValueError for an unknown operator
or a negative skip or limit; fails with ParseError for an invalid $regex
and otherwise like db.exec.

methods.name: findByID
methods.doc:
findByID returns the document whose _id is id, or null when there is
none. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: findOne
methods.doc:
findOne returns the first document matching filter, or null when none
does. Fails like find.

methods.name: insertMany
methods.doc:
insertMany stores each object in docs like insertOne and returns their
_ids in order. Throws TypeError when an item isn't an object, before
storing anything; when an insert fails, the documents before it stay
stored.

methods.name: insertOne
methods.doc:
insertOne stores doc as a new document and returns its _id. doc's own _id
is used when it has one; otherwise a random id is generated and written
into doc. Fails with ValueError when a document with that _id exists, and
otherwise like db.exec.

methods.name: query
methods.doc: query starts an empty query over the whole collection.

methods.name: replaceOne
methods.signature: collection.replaceOne(filter: object, doc: object) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
replaceOne replaces the first document matching filter with doc, keeping
its _id, and returns how many documents changed, 0 or 1. Fails like find.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
save writes doc under its _id, replacing the stored document with that
id or inserting doc when there is none (generating an _id and writing it
into doc when it has none), and returns the _id. Fails like db.exec.

methods.name: sort
methods.doc: sort starts a query ordered by field; see db.Query.sort.

methods.name: updateMany
methods.signature: collection.updateMany(filter: object, changes: object) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
updateMany sets each field of changes on every document matching filter
and returns how many changed. Fails like find.

methods.name: updateOne
methods.signature: collection.updateOne(filter: object, changes: object) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
updateOne sets each field of changes (dot paths such as "address.city"
reach into nested objects) on the first document matching filter and
returns how many documents changed, 0 or 1. Fails like find.

methods.name: where
methods.signature: collection.where(field: string, op: string, value: any) -> *db.Query
methods.doc: where starts a query with one condition; see db.Query.where.

methods.name: all
methods.doc:
all runs the query and returns the matching documents. Fails with
ParseError for an invalid "matches" pattern and otherwise like db.exec.

methods.name: and
methods.signature: query.and(field: string, op: string, value: any) -> *db.Query
methods.doc:
and adds a condition like where.

Deprecated: use query.where(field, op, value) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use query.where(field, op, value) instead.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc:
apply runs the queued updates on every document matching the query's
conditions and returns how many documents it updated; with no queued
updates it changes nothing and returns 0. Fails like all.

methods.name: count
methods.doc:
count returns how many documents match the query's conditions, ignoring
skip and limit. Fails like all.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
delete removes every document matching the query's conditions (ignoring
sort, skip and limit) and returns how many it removed. Fails like all.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc:
exists reports whether any document matches the query's conditions.
Fails like all.

methods.name: fields
methods.doc:
fields makes this query return only the named fields (dot paths allowed)
plus _id, and returns the query. Throws TypeError for a name that isn't
a string.

methods.name: first
methods.doc:
first runs the query and returns the first matching document, or null
when none matches. Fails like all.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get runs the query like all.

Deprecated: use query.all() instead.

methods.name: inc
methods.doc:
inc queues adding amount to the number in field (missing counts as 0)
for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: limit
methods.doc:
limit makes this query return at most n documents and returns the query.
Throws ValueError for a negative n.

methods.name: max
methods.doc:
max queues raising field to value when value is larger (or field is
missing) for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: min
methods.doc:
min queues lowering field to value when value is smaller (or field is
missing) for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: mul
methods.doc:
mul queues multiplying the number in field by factor for apply and
returns the query.

methods.name: pull
methods.doc:
pull queues removing every element equal to value from the array in
field for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: push
methods.doc:
push queues appending value to the array in field (creating it) for
apply and returns the query.

methods.name: rename
methods.doc: rename queues moving field to newField for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: set queues setting field to value for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: skip
methods.doc:
skip makes this query leave out its first n documents and returns the
query. Throws ValueError for a negative n.

methods.name: sort
methods.doc:
sort orders this query's results by field, "asc" or "desc", after any
earlier sort fields, and returns the query. Values of different types
order null, booleans, numbers, strings, objects, arrays. Throws
ValueError for another direction.

methods.name: unset
methods.doc: unset queues removing field for apply and returns the query.

methods.name: where
methods.signature: query.where(field: string, op: string, value: any) -> *db.Query
methods.doc:
where adds the condition "field op value" to this query and returns the
query, so calls chain; conditions combine with AND. field may be a dot
path such as "address.city". op is one of "==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<",
"<=", "in" and "notIn" (value is an array), "contains" (a substring of a
string or a member of an array), "matches" (value is a regular
expression) and "exists" (value is true or false); the filter forms
"$eq", "$gt" and so on work too. Throws ValueError for any other op.

packages.name: diff
packages.description: Compare texts line by line, word by word or character by character and format the differences.

functions.name: chars
functions.signature: diff.chars(oldText: string, newText: string, options?: object) -> *diff.Diff
functions.doc:
chars compares two texts character by character. Options: context
(unchanged characters kept around each change, default 0).

functions.name: compareLines
functions.doc:
compareLines compares two arrays of lines.

Deprecated: use diff.text(oldLines.join("\n"), newLines.join("\n")) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use diff.text(oldLines.join("\n"), newLines.join("\n")) instead.

functions.name: compareWords
functions.doc:
compareWords compares two texts word by word.

Deprecated: use diff.words(oldText, newText) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use diff.words(oldText, newText) instead.

functions.name: html
functions.doc:

found" message for equal texts.

packages.name: utf16
packages.description: Measures, indexes, orders and case-maps strings like JavaScript does, counting UTF-16 code units with 1-based positions.

functions.name: at
functions.doc:
at returns the UTF-16 code unit at a 1-based index as a string, like
text[index] for code units: half of a surrogate pair comes back as a lone
surrogate. Returns "" when index is outside the string, as text[index]
does.

functions.name: compare
functions.doc:
compare orders a and b by UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript's < does, and
returns -1 when a sorts first, 0 when they are equal and 1 when b sorts
first.

functions.name: compareLower
functions.doc:
compareLower orders a and b as compare(lower(a), lower(b)) does, which is
JavaScript's a.toLowerCase() < b.toLowerCase(), without building either
lowered copy when both are ASCII.

functions.name: containsLower
functions.doc:
containsLower reports whether lower(text) contains lower(part), as
JavaScript's text.toLowerCase().includes(part.toLowerCase()) does, without
building either lowered copy when both are ASCII.

functions.name: index
functions.doc:
index returns the 1-based code unit position where part first occurs in
text, or 0 when it doesn't occur, as text.index does. An empty part is
found at 1.

functions.name: isSameLower
functions.doc:
isSameLower reports whether utf16.lower(text) equals lowered, which is
JavaScript's text.toLowerCase() === lowered, without building the lowered
copy for ASCII text.

functions.name: join
functions.doc:
join concatenates a and b like JavaScript's +: a lone high surrogate at
the end of a and a lone low surrogate at the start of b become one
character again.

functions.name: length
functions.doc:
length returns the length of text in UTF-16 code units, which is
JavaScript's string.length: an emoji outside the Basic Multilingual Plane
counts as 2.

functions.name: lower
functions.doc:
lower returns text in lower case like JavaScript's toLowerCase, with full
Unicode case mapping (final sigma included). Lone surrogates are kept.

functions.name: sameLower
functions.doc:
sameLower reports whether utf16.lower(s) equals lowered.

Deprecated: use utf16.isSameLower(text, lowered) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use utf16.isSameLower(text, lowered) instead.

functions.name: trim
functions.signature: utf16.trim(text: string, start: int, end: int) -> string
functions.doc:
trim returns the code units of text from start to end, both 1-based and
inclusive, like string.trim(start, end) counted in UTF-16 code units. A
negative position counts back from the end (-1 is the last code unit),
positions past either end are clamped, and reversed positions are
swapped, so trim never fails.

functions.name: upper
functions.doc:
upper returns text in upper case like JavaScript's toUpperCase, with full
Unicode case mapping ("ß" becomes "SS"). Lone surrogates are kept.

it returns fallback, or "" without one; use env.has to tell unset from
empty.

values.

functions.doc:
int reads an environment variable as a whole number, returning fallback
when it is unset or blank. Fails with ParseError when it is set to
something else, such as PORT=abc.

functions.name: isDev
functions.doc: isDev reports whether env.mode() is "dev" or "development".

functions.name: isProd
functions.doc: isProd reports whether env.mode() is "prod" or "production".

functions.name: isTest
functions.doc: isTest reports whether env.mode() is "test" or "testing".

functions.name: keys
functions.doc: keys returns the names of every environment variable, sorted.

functions.name: load
functions.doc:
load reads .env files (".env" when none are given) and sets their
variables, keeping any that are already set. Use
env.parseFile(path).apply({override: true}) to replace them. Every file
that can be read is applied, in order, even when an earlier one is
missing; then load fails with the first error: NotFoundError for a
missing file, PermissionError or IOError for an unreadable one, and
ValueError for a key the OS rejects.

functions.name: local
functions.doc:
local loads .env and reports whether it was read.

Deprecated: use env.load() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use env.load() instead.

functions.name: localOverload
functions.doc:
localOverload loads .env, replacing set variables, and reports whether
it was read.

Deprecated: use env.parseFile(".env").apply({override: true}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use env.parseFile(".env").apply({override: true}) instead.

functions.name: missing
functions.doc:
missing returns the listed environment variables that are unset or
empty, in the order given.

functions.name: mode
functions.doc:
mode returns the app's mode from APP_ENV, OSL_ENV or NODE_ENV (the first
that is set), lowercased, or "development".

functions.name: number
functions.signature: env.number(key: string, fallback: number) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
number reads an environment variable as a number, returning fallback
when it is unset or blank. Fails with ParseError when it isn't a number.

functions.name: overload
functions.doc:
overload loads .env files, replacing variables that are already set,
and reports whether every file was read.

Deprecated: use env.parseFile(path).apply({override: true}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use env.parseFile(path).apply({override: true}) instead.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc: parse reads .env text into a File handle with no path.

functions.name: parseFile
functions.doc:
parseFile reads a .env file into a File handle that remembers its path,
so file.save() writes back to it. Fails with NotFoundError when the file
doesn't exist, PermissionError or IOError.

functions.name: read
functions.doc:
read reads a .env file into a File handle, which is empty when the file
can't be read.

Deprecated: use env.parseFile(path) instead, which fails when the file
can't be read.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use env.parseFile(path) instead, which fails when the file can't be read.

functions.name: require
functions.doc:
require returns an environment variable that must be set. Fails with
NotFoundError when it is unset or empty.

functions.name: required
functions.doc:
required checks that every listed environment variable is set and not
empty. Fails with NotFoundError naming all the missing ones.

functions.name: set
functions.signature: env.set(key: string, value: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
set sets an environment variable for this program and the processes it
starts. Spaces around key are ignored. Throws ValueError for an empty
name or one containing "=".

functions.name: stringify
functions.doc:
stringify formats an object as .env text, one KEY=value line per key in
sorted order, quoting values that need it.

functions.name: unset
functions.doc:
unset removes an environment variable. Removing one that isn't set does
nothing. Throws ValueError for an empty name or one containing "=".

functions.name: value
functions.doc:
value returns a Value handle for a variable.

instead.

methods.name: clear

methods.name: expand
methods.doc:
expand returns a value with $NAME and ${NAME} references replaced, first
from the file's own values (recursively, ignoring cycles) and then from
the environment; \$ stays a literal $.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get returns a value. When it is missing or empty it returns fallback,
or "" without one.

methods.name: getBool

getBool reads a boolean, or def when missing or malformed.

methods.name: getDefault

getDefault returns a value, or def when it is missing or empty.

Deprecated: use file.get(key, def) instead.

methods.name: getFloat
methods.doc:
getFloat reads a number, or def when missing or malformed.

Deprecated: use file.number(key, def) instead.

methods.name: getInt
methods.doc:
getInt reads a whole number, or def when missing or malformed.

Deprecated: use file.int(key, def) instead.

methods.name: has

methods.name: int
methods.signature: file.int(key: string, fallback: int) -> result<int, error>

methods.name: keys

load re-reads the file and sets its values as environment variables,
keeping set ones, and reports whether it was read.

read.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc:
merge sets every key of an object. It mutates the file and returns it,
so calls can chain. Blank keys are skipped.

methods.name: number

methods.doc: number reads a value as a number, like env.number.

methods.doc: path returns the file's path, or "" when it has none.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
read replaces the values with the contents of the file at file.path().
Fails with NotFoundError when it doesn't exist, PermissionError or
IOError, leaving the values unchanged. Throws StateError when the file
has no path.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
save writes the values to file.path() as .env text (see env.stringify).
Fails with NotFoundError when the directory doesn't exist, PermissionError
or IOError. Throws StateError when the file has no path.

methods.name: set
methods.doc:
set sets a value. It mutates the file and returns it, so calls can
chain. Non-string values are stored as their string form.
Throws ValueError for an empty key.

methods.name: setPath
methods.doc:
setPath sets the path file.read() and file.save() use. It mutates the
file and returns it, so calls can chain. An empty path means ".env".

methods.name: text
methods.doc: text formats the values as .env text (see env.stringify).

methods.name: unset
methods.doc:
unset removes a key. It mutates the file and returns it, so calls can
chain.

methods.name: value
