packages.name: events
packages.description: Named in-process events whose listeners can be added, removed and emitted from any thread.

functions.name: count
functions.doc: count returns how many listeners event has.

functions.name: emit
functions.doc:
emit calls every listener of event with args, in the order they were
added, on the calling thread, and returns when they have all run.
Listeners added or removed during the emit take effect from the next one.
An error a listener throws propagates to the caller of emit and the
remaining listeners are not called.

functions.name: off
functions.doc:
off removes the earliest registration of fn for event, whether added with
on or once, and reports whether there was one to remove. Throws TypeError
when fn isn't a function.

functions.name: on
functions.doc:
on adds fn as a listener for event. Every registration is called, in the
order added, each time the event is emitted, so adding a function twice
calls it twice. Throws TypeError when fn isn't a function.

functions.name: once
functions.doc:
once adds fn as a listener that is removed just before its first call.
Throws TypeError when fn isn't a function.

packages.name: exif
packages.description: Read the EXIF orientation of JPEG, PNG, WebP and TIFF images and remove their EXIF metadata without re-encoding

functions.name: has
orientation
functions.doc:
orientation reads the EXIF orientation of an image: 1 to 8, where 1 is
upright and 6 means "rotate 90 degrees clockwise to display" (see
pic.orient). It reads JPEG, PNG, WebP and TIFF images and raw EXIF
blocks, and is 1 when the image has no EXIF or no orientation tag,
including for GIF, BMP, ICO and QOI images, which can't carry EXIF.

Fails with ParseError for corrupt image or EXIF data or data that isn't an
image, and UnsupportedError for HEIF, AVIF and JPEG XL images.

functions.name: orientationFile
functions.doc:
orientationFile reads the EXIF orientation of the image file at path, as
exif.orientation does. Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or
IOError when the file can't be read, and otherwise as exif.orientation
does.

functions.name: strip
functions.doc:
strip returns a copy of a JPEG, PNG or WebP image with its EXIF metadata
removed and every other byte unchanged; the pixels aren't re-encoded. An
image without EXIF comes back as an identical copy, as do GIF, BMP, ICO
and QOI images, which can't carry EXIF.

Fails with ParseError for corrupt image data or data that isn't an image,
and UnsupportedError for TIFF, HEIF, AVIF and JPEG XL images and raw EXIF
blocks.

functions.name: stripFile
functions.doc:
stripFile reads the image file at path and returns it with its EXIF
metadata removed, as exif.strip does; the file itself isn't changed.
Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't
be read, and otherwise as exif.strip does.

packages.name: fs
packages.description: Read, write and manage files and directories, and work with path strings.

functions.name: absPath
functions.doc:
absPath returns path as an absolute, cleaned path, resolved against the
working directory. Fails with IOError when the working directory can't
be read.

functions.name: append
functions.doc:
append opens a file for appending, or returns null.

Deprecated: use fs.open(path, {mode: "a"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.open(path, {mode: "a"}) instead.

functions.name: appendFile
functions.signature: fs.appendFile(path: string, text: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
appendFile adds text to the end of a file, creating it if needed. Fails
with NotFoundError when the parent directory doesn't exist,
PermissionError, or IOError.

functions.name: appendFileBytes
functions.signature: fs.appendFileBytes(path: string, data: any) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
appendFileBytes adds bytes to the end of a file, creating it if needed.
data is read like fs.writeFileBytes data. Fails like fs.appendFile.

functions.name: appendToFile
functions.doc:
appendToFile appends text and reports whether it worked.

Deprecated: use fs.appendFile(path, text) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.appendFile(path, text) instead.

functions.name: base
functions.doc:
base returns the last element of a path: fs.base("a/b/c.txt") is
"c.txt". It only reads the string.

functions.name: chdir
functions.doc:
chdir changes the working directory and reports whether it worked.

Deprecated: use process.chdir(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use process.chdir(path) instead.

functions.name: cleanPath
functions.doc:
cleanPath returns the shortest equivalent path, resolving "." and ".."
and repeated separators: fs.cleanPath("/a//b/./c") is "/a/b/c".

functions.name: copy
functions.signature: fs.copy(from: string, to: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
copy copies a file, or a directory and everything in it, to a new path,
keeping permissions. Options: overwrite (boolean, default false) replaces
files that already exist at the destination; without it, an existing
destination file fails with IOError. Fails with NotFoundError when from
doesn't exist. Throws ValueError when copying a directory into itself.

functions.name: copyDir
functions.doc:
copyDir copies a directory tree into dstPath and reports whether it
worked.

Deprecated: use fs.copy(from, to) instead, which copies files and
directories.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.copy(from, to) instead, which copies files and directories.

functions.name: create
functions.doc:
create opens a file for writing, truncating it, or returns null.

Deprecated: use fs.open(path, {mode: "w"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.open(path, {mode: "w"}) instead.

functions.name: dir
functions.doc:
dir returns everything but the last element of a path:
fs.dir("a/b/c.txt") is "a/b". It only reads the string.

functions.name: eachLine
functions.doc:
eachLine calls fn with every line of a file; a missing file calls it
never.

Deprecated: use `for line in fs.lines(path)` instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use `for line in fs.lines(path)` instead.

functions.name: entries
functions.signature: fs.entries(path: string) -> result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}[], error>
functions.returns: result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}[], error>
functions.doc:
entries lists a directory's entries, sorted by name. Each entry has the
keys name, path (path joined with name), ext, isDir, isSymlink, size
(bytes), modTime (unix milliseconds) and mode (such as "-rw-r--r--").
Fails like fs.readDir.

functions.name: evalSymlinks
functions.doc:
evalSymlinks resolves every symlink in a path. Fails with NotFoundError
when the path or a link target doesn't exist.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc:
exists reports whether something exists at path. A broken symlink
counts as missing.

functions.name: ext
functions.doc:
ext returns the extension of a path's last element, with its dot:
fs.ext("a/b/c.txt") is ".txt", and "" when there is none.

functions.name: getBase
functions.doc:
getBase returns the last element of a path.

Deprecated: use fs.base(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.base(path) instead.

functions.name: getDir
functions.doc:
getDir returns a path's directory.

Deprecated: use fs.dir(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.dir(path) instead.

functions.name: getExt
functions.doc:
getExt returns a path's extension.

Deprecated: use fs.ext(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.ext(path) instead.

functions.name: getModTime
functions.doc:
getModTime returns a file's modification time in unix milliseconds, or 0
when it can't be read.

Deprecated: use fs.modTime(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.modTime(path) instead.

functions.name: getParts
functions.doc:
getParts returns [base, dir, ext] of a path.

Deprecated: use fs.base(path), fs.dir(path) and fs.ext(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.base(path), fs.dir(path) and fs.ext(path) instead.

functions.name: getSize
functions.doc:
getSize returns a file's size in bytes, or 0 when it can't be read.

Deprecated: use fs.size(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.size(path) instead.

functions.name: getStat
functions.doc:
getStat describes a file, with success false when it can't be read.

Deprecated: use fs.stat(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.stat(path) instead.

functions.name: getStem
functions.doc:
getStem returns a path's last element without its extension.

Deprecated: use fs.stem(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.stem(path) instead.

functions.name: getwd
functions.doc:
getwd returns the working directory, or "" when it can't be read.

Deprecated: use process.cwd() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use process.cwd() instead.

functions.name: glob
functions.doc:
glob lists the paths matching a shell pattern such as "src/*.osl", in
lexical order. * and ? match within one path element and [a-z] matches a
range; ** is not special. Fails with ParseError for a malformed pattern.

functions.name: grep
functions.signature: fs.grep(path: string, pattern: string) -> result<string[], error>
functions.doc:
grep returns the lines of a file that match a regular expression. Fails
with NotFoundError when the file doesn't exist and ParseError for an
invalid pattern.

functions.name: head
functions.doc:
head returns up to the first count lines (default 10) of a file. Fails with
NotFoundError when the file doesn't exist; throws ValueError for a
negative count.

functions.name: isAbs
functions.doc: isAbs reports whether a path is absolute.

functions.name: isDir
functions.doc: isDir reports whether path is a directory, following symlinks.

functions.name: isFile
functions.doc: isFile reports whether path is a regular file, following symlinks.

functions.name: joinPath
functions.doc:
joinPath joins path elements with the OS separator and cleans the
result: fs.joinPath("a", "b", "c.txt") is "a/b/c.txt".

functions.name: lines
functions.doc:
lines iterates over a file's lines, without line endings, reading as it
goes; the file closes when the loop finishes. Fails with NotFoundError
when the file doesn't exist; a read error throws IOError from the loop.

functions.name: mkdir
functions.signature: fs.mkdir(path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
mkdir creates a directory. Options: recursive (boolean, default false)
also creates missing parents and succeeds when the directory already
exists. Fails with NotFoundError when a parent is missing (without
recursive), IOError when path already exists, or PermissionError.

functions.name: mkdirAll
functions.doc:
mkdirAll creates a directory and any missing parents and reports whether
it worked.

Deprecated: use fs.mkdir(path, {recursive: true}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.mkdir(path, {recursive: true}) instead.

functions.name: modTime
functions.doc:
modTime returns when a file was last modified, in unix milliseconds,
following symlinks. Fails with NotFoundError when the file doesn't exist.

functions.name: open
functions.signature: fs.open(path: string, options?: object) -> result<*fs.File, error>
functions.doc:
open opens a file and returns a handle; close it when done. Options:
mode is "r" (default) to read, "w" to write from the start, creating or
truncating the file, or "a" to append, creating it if needed. Fails with
NotFoundError when a file opened for reading (or the parent directory)
doesn't exist, PermissionError, or IOError. Throws ValueError for an
unknown mode.

functions.name: openText
functions.doc:
openText returns a readable handle over text, for reading it the way a
file is read.

functions.name: pathStartsWith
functions.doc:
pathStartsWith reports whether path is prefix or lies below it, comparing
whole elements: "/a/bc" does not start with "/a/b".

functions.name: readDir
functions.doc:
readDir lists the names of the entries in a directory, sorted by name.
Fails with NotFoundError when the directory doesn't exist,
PermissionError, or IOError when path isn't a directory.

functions.name: readDirAll
functions.signature: fs.readDirAll(path: any) -> {ext: string, isDir: boolean, name: string, path: string, type: any}[]
functions.returns: {ext: string, isDir: boolean, name: string, path: string, type: any}[]
functions.doc:
readDirAll lists a directory's entries, or [] when it can't be read.

Deprecated: use fs.entries(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.entries(path) instead.

functions.name: readFile
functions.doc:
readFile reads a whole file as text. Fails with NotFoundError when the
file doesn't exist, PermissionError when it can't be read, and IOError
for anything else, such as path being a directory.

functions.name: readFileBytes
functions.doc: readFileBytes reads a whole file as bytes. Fails like fs.readFile.

functions.name: relPath
functions.doc:
relPath returns target relative to base, with forward slashes:
fs.relPath("/a/b", "/a/b/c") is "c". Throws ValueError when one path is
absolute and the other isn't.

functions.name: remove
functions.signature: fs.remove(path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
remove deletes a file, or a directory and everything in it. A symlink is
removed, not its target. Fails with NotFoundError when path doesn't exist,
so used as a boolean it is true only when something was removed, and
PermissionError or IOError when something can't be deleted. Option: force
(boolean, default false) succeeds without doing anything when path
doesn't exist, like rm -rf, for cleanup of a path that may already be
gone.

functions.name: rename
functions.signature: fs.rename(from: string, to: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
rename moves or renames a file or directory, replacing an existing file
at to. Fails with NotFoundError when from doesn't exist, PermissionError,
or IOError (for example when to is on another device).

functions.name: segments
functions.doc:
segments lists a cleaned path's elements without separators:
fs.segments("/usr/local/bin") is ["usr", "local", "bin"].

functions.name: size
functions.doc:
size returns a file's size in bytes, following symlinks. Fails with
NotFoundError when the file doesn't exist.

functions.name: splitExt
functions.doc:
splitExt splits a path into [path without extension, extension]:
fs.splitExt("a/b.txt") is ["a/b", ".txt"].

functions.name: splitPath
functions.doc:
splitPath splits a path after its last separator into [directory, name]:
fs.splitPath("a/b/c.txt") is ["a/b/", "c.txt"].

functions.name: stat
functions.signature: fs.stat(path: string) -> result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}, error>
functions.returns: result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}, error>
functions.doc:
stat describes the file, directory or symlink at path, with the same
keys as an fs.entries entry. A symlink describes its target, with
isSymlink true. Fails with NotFoundError when nothing exists at path.

functions.name: stem
functions.doc:
stem returns the last element of a path without its extension:
fs.stem("a/b/c.txt") is "c".

functions.name: syncFile
functions.doc:
syncFile flushes a file's written data to disk. Fails with NotFoundError
when the file doesn't exist; it never creates one.

functions.name: syncLater
functions.doc:
syncLater queues a file to be flushed to disk in the background, merging
repeated requests for the same file; fs.syncPending waits for the queue.
A file removed before its flush is skipped. Throws ValueError for an
empty path.

functions.name: syncPending
functions.doc:
syncPending waits until every file queued with fs.syncLater before the
call is flushed. Fails with the first flush error, usually an IOError,
including one from a flush that finished before the call. Every call
waiting on a flush reports its failure, and a failure no call was
waiting on is reported once, by the next call.

functions.name: tail

backwards from the end. Fails with NotFoundError when the file doesn't

functions.signature: fs.walk(path: any) -> {ext: string, isDir: boolean, name: string, path: string, type: any}[]
functions.returns: {ext: string, isDir: boolean, name: string, path: string, type: any}[]
functions.doc:
walk lists everything below path, or [] when it can't be read.

functions.doc:
walkDir calls fn(path, file, control) for every entry under path,
including path itself; setting control.skip skips a directory.

functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use `for entry in fs.walkTree(path)` instead.

functions.name: walkTree
functions.signature: fs.walkTree(path: string) -> iter<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}>
functions.returns: iter<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}>
functions.doc:
walkTree visits everything below a directory, depth first in lexical
order, without following symlinks; the root itself is not included. It
yields entries shaped like fs.entries ones. A missing or unreadable root
or subdirectory throws NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError from
the loop that is iterating.

functions.name: withExt
functions.doc:
withExt replaces a path's extension; the dot is optional and "" removes
it: fs.withExt("a/b.txt", "md") is "a/b.md".

functions.name: withName
functions.doc:
withName replaces a path's last element: fs.withName("a/b/c.txt",
"d.md") is "a/b/d.md".

functions.name: writeFile
functions.signature: fs.writeFile(path: string, text: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
writeFile replaces a file's contents with text, creating it if needed.
The write is atomic: readers see the old or the new contents, never a
mix, even after a crash, and an existing file keeps its permissions.
Writing through a symlink replaces its target. Fails with NotFoundError
when the parent directory doesn't exist, PermissionError, or IOError.
Options: durable (boolean, default true) returns only once the new
contents are on stable storage; false keeps the write atomic but may
return first, so a crash right after can leave the old contents. On
macOS false uses a write barrier, and on Linux with ext4, XFS or btrfs
it waits for the data to reach the disk without flushing its cache;
elsewhere it flushes in full, like a durable write.

functions.name: writeFileBytes
functions.signature: fs.writeFileBytes(path: string, data: any, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
writeFileBytes replaces a file's contents with bytes, atomically like
fs.writeFile and with the same options. data is a byte[]; a string
writes its UTF-8 bytes and an array of whole numbers from 0 to 255
writes those bytes. Throws ValueError for a number outside that range.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close flushes buffered writes and closes the file. Closing again does
nothing. Fails with IOError when the final flush fails.

methods.name: eof
methods.doc:
eof reports whether there is nothing left to read. A closed or
write-only handle has nothing to read.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc:
flush writes buffered data to the file. Throws StateError on a closed or
read-only handle; fails with IOError.

methods.name: grep
methods.doc:
grep reads the remaining lines and returns those matching a regular
expression. Fails with ParseError for an invalid pattern and IOError when
reading fails. Throws StateError on a closed or write-only handle.

methods.name: head
methods.doc:
head reads up to count lines (default 10) from the current position. Throws
StateError on a closed or write-only handle and ValueError for a negative
count; fails with IOError when reading fails.

methods.name: lines
methods.doc:
lines iterates over the remaining lines, without line endings. A read
error throws IOError from the loop. Throws StateError on a closed or
write-only handle.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
read reads text from the current position: everything that is left, or
at most count bytes when count is given. At the end of the file it returns "".
Throws StateError on a closed or write-only handle and ValueError for a
negative count; fails with IOError when reading fails.

methods.name: readBytes
methods.doc:
readBytes reads bytes from the current position: everything that is
left, or at most count bytes when count is given. Fails like file.read.

methods.name: readLine
methods.doc:
readLine reads the next line, without its line ending ("\n" or "\r\n").
Fails with IOError at the end of the file, so check file.eof() first or
loop with `for line in file.lines()`. Throws StateError on a closed or
write-only handle.

methods.name: seek
methods.doc:
seek moves the read and write cursor offset bytes from "start" (the
default), "current" or "end", and returns its new offset from the start:
the number of bytes before it, so 0 is the start of the file. Offsets are
distances, not 1-based positions. Buffered writes are flushed first.
Throws StateError on a closed handle and ValueError for another origin;
fails with IOError.

methods.name: tail
methods.doc:
tail reads the last count lines (default 10) of the whole file, without
moving the read position. Throws StateError on a closed or write-only
handle and ValueError for a negative count; fails with IOError.

methods.name: write
methods.doc:
write writes data at the current position: a string, a byte[] or an
array of whole numbers from 0 to 255; other values are written as their
string form. Writes are buffered until file.flush() or file.close().
Throws StateError on a closed or read-only handle; fails with IOError.

packages.name: ftp
packages.description: Connects to FTP servers to list, upload, download, rename and delete remote files and directories.

functions.name: connect
functions.doc:
connect opens and logs in to an FTP server. Options: username (default
"anonymous"), password, timeout (milliseconds, default 10000) and tls,
as in std:email: "auto" (the default) switches to TLS with AUTH TLS when
the server offers it, "starttls" requires that, "implicit" speaks TLS
from the start (port 990 unless address names one) and "none" never uses
TLS. A password is never sent unencrypted to another machine: without
TLS, a login to a host that isn't localhost or a loopback address fails
with UnsupportedError before the password is sent, unless it is the
anonymous login (user "anonymous" with no password or the default one). Also fails with PermissionError, NetworkError or TimeoutError. The
deprecated four-argument form returns a disconnected client instead of
failing.

changeDirectory changes the remote working directory, returning false on

methods.name: chdir

chdir changes the remote working directory, which relative paths start
from. Fails with NotFoundError when path doesn't exist.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close logs out and closes the connection. Closing twice is a no-op. Fails
with NetworkError when the server can't be told, but the connection is
closed either way.

methods.name: connectEx
methods.signature: fTP.connectEx(host: any, port: any, user: any, ...rest: any) -> *ftp.FTP
methods.doc:
connectEx connects to another server, or returns null on failure.

methods.name: createDirectory

createDirectory creates a remote directory, returning false on failure.

Deprecated: use client.mkdir(path) instead.

currentDirectory returns the remote working directory, or "" on failure.

methods.name: download
methods.signature: fTP.download(remotePath: string, localPath: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
download copies the remote file at remotePath to localPath, creating
missing local directories. A partly written file is removed. Fails with
NotFoundError when the remote file doesn't exist, IOError when the
transfer breaks off, and PermissionError or IOError when localPath can't
be written.

methods.name: downloadDir
methods.signature: fTP.downloadDir(remoteDir: string, localDir: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
downloadDir copies the remote directory remoteDir and everything in it to
localDir. Fails like download, and with IOError when the server lists an
unsafe name or a symlink.

Deprecated: use client.downloadDir(remoteDir, localDir) instead.

methods.returns: result<{isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int?, name: string, path: string, size: int, target: string?}[], error>
methods.doc:
entries lists the directory at path ("" for the current directory). Each
entry has the keys name, path, isDir, isSymlink, size (bytes), modTime
(unix milliseconds, null when the server doesn't say) and target (where a
symlink points, null otherwise). "." and ".." are left out. Fails with
NotFoundError when the directory doesn't exist.

mkdir creates the remote directory path. Its parent must exist. Fails
with PermissionError when the server refuses, which most servers also do

passiveMode succeeds for true, since transfers always use passive mode,
and fails with UnsupportedError for false.

removeDir deletes the remote directory path, which must be empty.

setModTime sets the modification time of the remote file at path to
modTime (unix milliseconds; servers keep whole seconds). Fails with

functions.signature: img.linearGradient(from: object, to: object, stops: array, options?: object) -> *img.Gradient
functions.doc:
linearGradient returns a gradient along the line from one point {x, y}
to another, in image pixels, to use as a fill, stroke or color.

stops is an array of colors spread evenly along the line, or of
{offset, color} objects with offsets from 0 (at from) to 1 (at to).
Colors blend premultiplied, so fading to "transparent" keeps the color.
Options: spread, what the gradient does past its ends: "pad" (the
default; the end colors continue), "repeat" or "reflect". Throws
ValueError for no stops, an invalid color or offset, or a malformed
point.

functions.name: measureText
functions.signature: img.measureText(text: string, options?: object) -> {ascent: number, descent: number, height: number, lineHeight: number, lines: string[], width: number}
functions.returns: {ascent: number, descent: number, height: number, lineHeight: number, lines: string[], width: number}
functions.doc:
measureText lays text out as pic.text would and measures it, without
drawing. Options: font, size, maxWidth and lineHeight, as for pic.text.

The record's keys, all in pixels: width, of the widest line; height,
from the top of the first line to the bottom of the last; ascent and
descent, how far the font reaches above and below a baseline;
lineHeight, the distance between baselines; and lines, the text of each
line after wrapping. Throws ValueError for an invalid option.

functions.name: new
functions.signature: img.new(width: int, height: int, options?: object) -> *img.Image
functions.doc:
new creates a width x height image, transparent unless the fill option
gives a color ("#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa", a CSS name such as "white", or
{r, g, b, a}), an *img.Gradient or an *img.Pattern to start it with.
Throws ValueError unless both sides are 1 to 100000 pixels and the image
is at most 100 megapixels, or for an invalid fill.

functions.name: normalizeOrientationBytes
functions.doc:
normalizeOrientationBytes turns an image upright using the EXIF orientation
in data, the bytes it was decoded from. It returns the image itself when no
change is needed and null for a closed image.

Deprecated: use img.decode(data, {autoOrient: true}) or
pic.orient(img.info(data).orientation) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use img.decode(data, {autoOrient: true}) or pic.orient(img.info(data).orientation) instead.

functions.name: open
functions.doc:
open decodes the image file at path, or returns null when it can't.

Deprecated: use img.decodeFile(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use img.decodeFile(path) instead.

functions.name: openSize
functions.doc:
openSize returns the [width, height] of the image file at path, or [0, 0]
when it can't be read.

Deprecated: use img.infoFile(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use img.infoFile(path) instead.

functions.name: orient
functions.doc:
orient applies an EXIF orientation, or returns null for one outside 1-8 or
a closed image.

Deprecated: use pic.orient(orientation) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.orient(orientation) instead.

functions.name: parsePath
functions.doc:
parsePath reads SVG path data, the d attribute of an SVG <path>, such as
"M 10 10 L 90 10 Q 50 60 10 10 Z": the M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A and Z
commands, in absolute (upper case) and relative (lower case) forms. The
numbers are SVG coordinates, which put the image's top-left corner at
0, 0, so the data draws where an SVG renderer would draw it: SVG's 0 to 1
is pixel 1. Fails with ParseError, naming the character where the data
goes wrong.

functions.name: path
functions.doc:
path returns a new empty path to build with moveTo, lineTo, quadTo,
cubicTo, arc, arcTo, rect, circle, ellipse and close, and to draw with
pic.drawPath. Building methods change the path and return it, so calls
chain: img.path().moveTo(a).lineTo(b).close().

functions.name: pattern
functions.doc:
pattern returns image repeated in tiles across the whole plane, one
tile's top-left pixel at pixel 1, 1, to use as a fill, stroke or color.
The pattern copies the image, so later changes to it don't show. Throws
StateError when the image is closed.

functions.name: radialGradient
functions.signature: img.radialGradient(center: object, radius: number, stops: array, options?: object) -> *img.Gradient
functions.doc:
radialGradient returns a gradient in circles around center, {x, y},
reaching the last stop at radius pixels, to use as a fill, stroke or
color. stops and the spread option are as for img.linearGradient, with
offset 0 at the center and 1 at radius. Throws ValueError for a negative
radius, no stops or an invalid stop.

functions.name: resize
functions.doc:
resize scales an image with Lanczos filtering, where 0 for one side keeps
the aspect ratio, or returns null for invalid sizes or a closed image.

Deprecated: use pic.resize(w, h) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.resize(w, h) instead.

functions.name: resizeFast
functions.doc:
resizeFast scales an image with bilinear filtering, or returns null for
invalid sizes or a closed image.

Deprecated: use pic.resize(w, h, {filter: "bilinear"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.resize(w, h, {filter: "bilinear"}) instead.

functions.name: resizeFit
functions.doc:
resizeFit scales an image to fit inside maxW x maxH, keeping the aspect
ratio, or returns null for invalid sizes or a closed image.

Deprecated: use pic.resize(maxW, maxH, {fit: "contain"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.resize(maxW, maxH, {fit: "contain"}) instead.

functions.name: resizeHeight
functions.doc:
resizeHeight scales an image to height h, keeping the aspect ratio.

Deprecated: use pic.resize(0, h) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.resize(0, h) instead.

functions.name: resizeWidth
functions.doc:
resizeWidth scales an image to width w, keeping the aspect ratio.

Deprecated: use pic.resize(w, 0) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.resize(w, 0) instead.

functions.name: rgb
functions.signature: img.rgb(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> img.Color
functions.doc:
rgb returns an opaque img.Color from red, green and blue channels, each
0 to 255. Throws ValueError for a channel outside that range.

functions.name: rgba
functions.signature: img.rgba(r: int, g: int, b: int, a: int) -> img.Color
functions.doc:
rgba returns an img.Color from red, green, blue and alpha channels, each
0 to 255; alpha 0 is fully transparent. Throws ValueError for a channel
outside that range.

functions.name: rotate
functions.doc:
rotate turns an image clockwise by angle degrees, or returns null for a
non-finite angle or a closed image.

Deprecated: use pic.rotate(degrees) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.rotate(degrees) instead.

functions.name: saveJPEG
functions.signature: img.saveJPEG(i: *img.Image, path: string, quality: int) -> boolean
functions.doc:
saveJPEG writes an image to path as JPEG with quality clamped to 1-100,
returning false on failure.

Deprecated: use pic.save(path, {quality: q}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.save(path, {quality: q}) instead.

functions.name: savePNG
functions.doc:
savePNG writes an image to path as PNG, returning false on failure.

Deprecated: use pic.save(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.save(path) instead.

functions.name: setColorProfile
functions.doc:
setColorProfile sets an image's ICC profile from bytes, a string or an array
of byte numbers, without checking it; empty input clears it. Returns false
for a closed image or invalid input.

Deprecated: use pic.setColorProfile(profile) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pic.setColorProfile(profile) instead.

functions.name: sizeBytes
functions.doc:
sizeBytes returns {w, h} for image bytes, or {} when they can't be read.

Deprecated: use img.info(data) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use img.info(data) instead.

methods.name: blur
methods.doc:
blur returns a copy blurred like a Gaussian blur with a standard
deviation of radius pixels, as CSS blur() is; 0 leaves it as it is.
Pixels past the edges repeat the edge, so edges don't fade, and
transparency blurs without dark fringes. It takes the same time for any
radius. Throws ValueError for a radius outside 0-1000.

methods.name: bounds
methods.signature: image.bounds() -> {height: int, width: int, x: int, y: int}
methods.returns: {height: int, width: int, x: int, y: int}
methods.doc:
bounds returns the region {x, y, width, height} this frame of an animation
changed, with x, y its top-left pixel (1, 1 is the image's top-left
corner). For any other image it is the whole image, {x: 1, y: 1, width,
height}, so pic.crop(pic.bounds()) is always valid.

methods.name: brightness
methods.doc:
brightness returns a copy with every color multiplied by amount: 1
leaves it as it is, 0 is black and 2 twice as bright (clipped at
white). Throws ValueError for an amount outside 0-1000.

methods.name: circle
methods.signature: image.circle(center: object, radius: number, options?: object)
methods.doc:
circle draws a circle around center, {x, y}, with radius in pixels, in
place. It takes rectangle's options except radius. Throws ValueError for
a malformed center, a negative radius or an invalid option.

methods.name: clone
methods.doc:
clone returns an independent copy, keeping the color profile and frame
details.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close releases the image's pixels. Closing twice does nothing; any other
method of a closed image throws StateError.

methods.name: colorProfile
methods.doc:
colorProfile returns the embedded ICC color profile, or null when the image
has none.

methods.name: contrast
methods.doc:
contrast returns a copy with every color moved away from middle gray by
amount: 1 leaves it as it is, 0 is solid gray and 2 doubles the
contrast. Throws ValueError for an amount outside 0-1000.

methods.name: crop
methods.doc:
crop returns a copy of the rectangle {x, y, width, height} of this image,
in pixels with x, y its top-left pixel (1, 1 is the image's top-left
corner); the image itself is unchanged. pic.crop(pic.bounds()) is the
whole image, or for an animation frame the part that frame changed.
Throws ValueError when a key is missing or not a whole number, or the
rectangle is empty or reaches outside the image.

methods.name: delay
methods.doc:
delay returns how long this frame of an animation is shown, in
milliseconds. It is 0 for a still image and for a frame whose file sets no
delay.

methods.name: draw
methods.signature: image.draw(source: *img.Image, x: int, y: int, options?: object)
methods.doc:
draw paints source onto this image with source's top-left pixel at pixel
x, y, in place: at 1, 1 their corners line up, and 0 or less puts part of
source off the left or top edge. Options: blend (default "over"),
opacity, width, height and filter. Throws ValueError
for an invalid option, TypeError for a null source and StateError when
either image is closed.

methods.name: drawPath
methods.doc:
drawPath draws path, from img.path or img.parsePath, in place. Each
subpath is filled as if closed, by the nonzero rule; the outline
follows the path as drawn, closing only subpaths that path.close()
closed. It takes rectangle's options except radius. Throws ValueError for
an invalid option and TypeError for a null path.

methods.name: ellipse
methods.signature: image.ellipse(center: object, radii: object, options?: object)
methods.doc:
ellipse draws an ellipse around center, {x, y}, with radii {x, y} in
pixels, in place. It takes rectangle's options except radius. Throws
ValueError for a malformed center or radii, or an invalid option.

methods.name: encode
methods.signature: image.encode(format: string, options?: object) -> result<byte[], error>
methods.doc:
encode returns the image encoded as format: "png", "jpeg" (or "jpg"),
"gif", "bmp" or "tiff" (or "tif"). PNG and JPEG embed the color profile.
GIF keeps the exact colors of images with up to 256 of them, and otherwise
dithers to a fixed palette; pixels under 50% opacity become transparent.
Options: quality (JPEG only, 1-100, default 90).

Fails with UnsupportedError for WebP, AVIF, HEIC, JPEG XL, ICO and QOI,
which can't be encoded. Throws ValueError for an unknown format or a
quality outside 1-100.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc:
fill sets every pixel to color, in place, replacing what was there
(transparency included) rather than blending. color is "#rrggbb",
"#rrggbbaa", a CSS name such as "white", {r, g, b, a}, an *img.Gradient
or an *img.Pattern. Throws ValueError for an invalid color.

methods.name: flipX
methods.doc: flipX returns a copy mirrored left to right.

methods.name: flipY
methods.doc: flipY returns a copy mirrored top to bottom.

methods.name: grayscale
methods.doc:
grayscale returns a gray copy, each pixel's luminance as CSS
grayscale(1) computes it; alpha is kept.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: height returns the height in pixels.

methods.name: hueRotate
methods.doc:
hueRotate returns a copy with every color's hue turned by degrees around
the color wheel, as CSS hue-rotate() does; 0 and 360 leave it as it is.
Throws ValueError for a non-finite angle.

methods.name: index
methods.doc:
index returns this frame's position in its file, counting from 1. It is 1
for an image that isn't one of several.

methods.name: invert
methods.doc:
invert returns a copy with every color inverted (255 - channel); alpha
is kept.

methods.name: line
methods.signature: image.line(from: object, to: object, options?: object)
methods.doc:
line draws a straight line from {x, y} to {x, y}, in place. Options:
color, lineWidth, lineCap, dash, dashOffset, opacity, blend and antialias.
Throws ValueError for a malformed point or option and StateError when
the image is closed.

methods.name: mapPixels
methods.doc:
mapPixels returns a copy where each pixel is fn(color, x, y): color is
the pixel as {r, g, b, a} with 0-255 channels and x, y its position, 1, 1
for the top-left pixel as in pixel and setPixel. fn returns the new
color, in any form a color can take, or null to keep the pixel. It calls
fn once per pixel, so it suits small images and per-pixel effects the
filters don't cover; it takes about a second per megapixel. Throws ValueError when fn returns an
invalid color and TypeError when fn is null.

methods.name: mask
methods.doc:
mask multiplies this image's alpha by mask's, in place, so the image
shows only where mask is opaque. Options: channel is "alpha" (the
default) or "luminance", which uses mask's brightness times its alpha,
so white shows and black hides. Throws ValueError unless mask is the
same size as this image, and StateError when either is closed.

methods.name: opacity
methods.doc:
opacity returns a copy with every pixel's alpha multiplied by amount: 1
leaves it as it is and 0 makes it transparent. Throws ValueError for an
amount outside 0-1.

methods.name: orient
methods.doc:
orient returns a copy turned and flipped so that an image stored with EXIF
orientation 1-8 displays upright; the image itself is unchanged. Use it
with img.info(data).orientation, or decode with {autoOrient: true}. Throws
ValueError for an orientation outside 1-8.

methods.name: pixel
methods.doc:
pixel returns the color at pixel x, y (1, 1 is the top-left one) as
"#rrggbb" when it is opaque and "#rrggbbaa" otherwise, the form
colors.stringify uses; every fully transparent pixel is "#00000000".
Throws ValueError when the point is outside the image.

methods.name: pixelate
methods.doc:
pixelate returns a copy made of size x size pixel blocks, each the
average color of the pixels under it, counting from the top-left
corner; 1 leaves the image as it is. Throws ValueError for a size below
1.

methods.name: pixels
methods.doc:
pixels returns a copy of every pixel as bytes, four per pixel (red,
green, blue, alpha, each 0-255, not premultiplied), row by row from the
top-left corner, so pixel x, y starts at byte
((y - 1) * width + x - 1) * 4 + 1 of the 1-based array.

methods.name: polygon
methods.doc:
polygon draws the closed shape through points (an array of {x, y}), in
place; it may cross itself, and where it overlaps itself is inside
(the nonzero rule). It takes rectangle's options except radius. Throws
ValueError for a malformed point or option.

methods.name: polyline
methods.doc:
polyline draws connected straight lines through points (an array of
{x, y}), in place, with lineJoin ("miter", the default, "round" or
"bevel") and miterLimit (default 10) shaping the corners; it takes
line's other options. Throws ValueError for a malformed point or option.

methods.name: rectangle
methods.doc:
rectangle draws {x, y, width, height} in place. Options: fill, stroke,
radius and the outline options line uses. Throws ValueError for a
malformed rectangle, a negative size or an invalid option.

methods.name: resize
methods.signature: image.resize(width: int, height: int, options?: object) -> *img.Image
methods.doc:
resize returns a copy scaled to width x height pixels; the image itself
is unchanged. Pass 0 for one side to keep the aspect ratio. Options:
filter is "lanczos" (the default, sharpest), "bicubic", "mitchell",
"bilinear" (faster) or "nearest" (blocky, for pixel art); fit is "fill"
(the default: exactly width x height), "contain" (as large as fits inside
width x height, keeping the aspect ratio) or "cover" (fills width x height
exactly, keeping the aspect ratio and cropping the overflow evenly).
Throws ValueError for negative sizes, both sides 0, a result over 100
megapixels, or an unknown option value.

methods.name: rotate
methods.doc:
rotate returns a copy turned clockwise by degrees; the image itself is
unchanged. Multiples of 90 are exact; other angles enlarge the copy to fit
the turned image and leave its corners transparent. Throws ValueError for
a non-finite angle.

methods.name: saturate
methods.doc:
saturate returns a copy with its colors' saturation scaled by amount, as
CSS saturate() does: 1 leaves it as it is, 0 is gray and 2 is twice as
vivid. Throws ValueError for an amount outside 0-1000.

methods.name: save
methods.signature: image.save(path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
save encodes the image and writes it to path, choosing the format from the
file extension (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .bmp, .tif or .tiff) unless the
format option names one. Options: format, and quality (JPEG only, 1-100,
default 90).

Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't
be written, and UnsupportedError as encode does. Throws ValueError when
the format can't be told from path or is unknown.

methods.name: setColorProfile
methods.doc:
setColorProfile replaces the ICC color profile that encode and save embed,
in place; empty bytes remove it. Throws ValueError when profile isn't an
ICC profile or is over 8 MB.

methods.name: setPixel
methods.signature: image.setPixel(x: int, y: int, color: any)
methods.doc:
setPixel sets pixel x, y (1, 1 is the top-left one) to color
("#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa", a CSS name such as "red", or {r, g, b, a}), in
place, replacing it rather than blending. Throws ValueError for a point
outside the image or an invalid color.

methods.name: setPixels
methods.doc:
setPixels replaces every pixel, in place, with data laid out as pixels()
returns it. Throws ValueError unless data is exactly width * height * 4
bytes.

methods.name: sharpen
methods.doc:
sharpen returns a copy sharpened with an unsharp mask: each color moves
away from its blurred neighbourhood by amount, so 0 leaves the image as
it is and 1 is a strong sharpen. Options: radius, the blur's standard
deviation in pixels (default 1); larger radii sharpen coarser detail.
Alpha is kept. Throws ValueError for an amount outside 0-100 or a radius
outside 0-1000.

methods.name: size
methods.signature: image.size() -> {h: int (deprecated), height: int, w: int (deprecated), width: int}
methods.returns: {h: int (deprecated), height: int, w: int (deprecated), width: int}
methods.doc:
size returns the image's {width, height} in pixels. The record also
carries the deprecated keys w and h, the same values under the names
img.Image.size used before.

methods.name: text
methods.signature: image.text(text: string, point: object, options?: object)
methods.doc:
text draws text with its top-left corner at {x, y}, in place. "\n" starts
a new line. Options: font (default "sans"), size (default 16), color,
align, baseline, maxWidth, lineHeight, opacity, blend and antialias.
Throws ValueError for a malformed point or option.

methods.name: threshold
methods.doc:
threshold returns a black and white copy: white where a pixel's
luminance is at least level (0-1), black elsewhere. Alpha is kept.
Throws ValueError for a level outside 0-1.

methods.name: tint
methods.doc:
tint returns a copy with every color mixed toward color by amount: 0
leaves it as it is and 1 gives every pixel color's red, green and blue
(scaled by color's own alpha). Alpha is kept. Throws ValueError for an
invalid color or an amount outside 0-1.

methods.name: toDataURL
methods.doc: toDataURL returns the image encoded as a data URL such as "data:image/png;base64,...", for HTML, CSS or an tag. Options: format ("png", the default, "jpeg", "gif", "bmp" or "tiff") and quality (JPEG only, 1-100, default 90). Fails and throws as encode does.

methods.name: width
methods.doc: width returns the width in pixels.

methods.name: arc
methods.signature: path.arc(center: object, radius: number, options?: object) -> *img.Path
methods.doc:
arc adds an arc of the circle around center, {x, y}, with radius in
pixels, joined to the current point by a straight line, as a canvas
arc() does. Angles are degrees, with 0 pointing right and 90 pointing
down (clockwise on screen). Options: start (default 0), end (default
360) and counterclockwise (default false, sweeping clockwise from start
to end). A sweep of 360 degrees or more draws the whole circle. Throws
ValueError for a negative radius or a non-finite angle. Returns the
path.

methods.name: arcTo
methods.signature: path.arcTo(control: object, point: object, radius: number) -> *img.Path
methods.doc:
arcTo adds an arc with radius (pixels) that rounds the corner at
control: it is tangent to the line from the current point to control
and to the line from control to point (both {x, y}), joined to the
current point by a straight line, as a canvas arcTo() does. The path
then continues from where the arc ends, not from point. Throws
ValueError for a negative radius. Returns the path.

methods.name: bounds
methods.signature: path.bounds() -> {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}?
methods.returns: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}?
methods.doc:
bounds returns the smallest rectangle {x, y, width, height} holding the
path's lines and curves, or null when the path draws nothing.

methods.name: circle
methods.doc:
circle adds a circle around center, {x, y}, with radius in pixels, as a
closed subpath. Throws ValueError for a negative radius. Returns the
path.

methods.name: clone
methods.doc: clone returns an independent copy of the path.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close joins the current point back to the start of the subpath with a
straight line, so an outline turns the corner there instead of ending
in caps. Returns the path.

methods.name: cubicTo
methods.signature: path.cubicTo(control1: object, control2: object, point: object) -> *img.Path
methods.doc:
cubicTo adds a cubic Bézier curve from the current point, pulled toward
control1 and then control2, to point (all {x, y}). Returns the path.

methods.name: ellipse
methods.doc:
ellipse adds an ellipse around center, {x, y}, with radii {x, y} in
pixels, as a closed subpath. Throws ValueError for negative radii.
Returns the path.

methods.name: lineTo
methods.doc:
lineTo adds a straight line from the current point to point, {x, y}
(starting the subpath there when the path is empty). Returns the path.

methods.name: moveTo
methods.doc: moveTo starts a new subpath at point, {x, y}. Returns the path.

methods.name: quadTo
methods.doc:
quadTo adds a quadratic Bézier curve from the current point, pulled
toward control, to point (both {x, y}). Returns the path.

methods.name: rect
methods.doc:
rect adds the rectangle rect, {x, y, width, height}, as a closed
subpath. Options: radius rounds the corners (pixels, default 0). Throws
ValueError for a malformed rectangle or a negative size. Returns the
path.

methods.name: rotate
methods.doc:
rotate turns everything already in the path clockwise by degrees around
1, 1 (the image's top-left corner), or around the center option, {x, y}.
Throws ValueError for a non-finite angle. Returns the path.

methods.name: scale
methods.signature: path.scale(x: number, y: number, options?: object) -> *img.Path
methods.doc:
scale stretches everything already in the path by x horizontally and y
vertically, away from 1, 1 (the image's top-left corner) or from the
center option, {x, y}; negative factors mirror it. Throws ValueError for
a non-finite factor. Returns the path.

methods.name: translate
methods.doc:
translate moves everything already in the path by x, y pixels. Throws
ValueError for a non-finite distance. Returns the path.

methods.name: colorAt
methods.doc:
colorAt returns the gradient's color at offset (0-1 between its first
and last stop, outside that range as spread says) as "#rrggbb", or
"#rrggbbaa" when it isn't opaque, for picking colors from a scale.
Throws ValueError for a non-finite offset.

methods.name: name
methods.doc:
name returns the font's full name from its name table, such as
"Go Regular" or "DejaVu Sans Bold".

methods.name: a
methods.doc: a returns the color's alpha channel, 0 (transparent) to 255 (opaque).

methods.name: b
methods.doc: b returns the color's blue channel, 0 to 255.

methods.name: g
methods.doc: g returns the color's green channel, 0 to 255.

methods.name: r
methods.doc: r returns the color's red channel, 0 to 255.

methods.name: withAlpha
methods.doc:
withAlpha returns a copy of the color with alpha a, from 0 (fully
transparent) to 255 (opaque): img.rgb(255, 0, 0).withAlpha(128) is a
half-transparent red. Throws ValueError for an alpha outside that range.

packages.name: js
packages.description: Run JavaScript in a sandboxed QuickJS runtime with a hard timeout, a memory cap and no access to the host.

functions.name: eval
functions.doc:
eval runs JavaScript with a timeout in milliseconds (0 or less is 60000,
and at most 300000) and returns {success: true, result} with the value
as a string, or {success: false, error}.

Deprecated: use js.evaluate(code, {timeout: ms}) instead, which returns
the value itself and fails with a typed error.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use js.evaluate(code, {timeout: ms}) instead, which returns the value itself and fails with a typed error.

functions.name: evaluate
functions.signature: js.evaluate(code: string, options?: object) -> result<any, error>
functions.doc:
evaluate runs JavaScript in a fresh sandboxed QuickJS runtime and
returns the value of its last expression, converted through JSON:
objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null keep their shape,
undefined becomes null, and a promise is awaited. The code can't reach
files, the network or the program. Options: timeout in milliseconds
(default 60000) and memoryLimit in bytes (default 1048576). Fails with
ParseError for a syntax error, TimeoutError when the code runs too long,
and RuntimeError for an exception it throws or running out of memory.
Throws ValueError for a timeout or memoryLimit of 0 or less.

packages.name: json
packages.description: Parse, stringify and stream JSON text.

functions.name: format
functions.doc:
format encodes data as JSON indented by two spaces, or "" when it can't
be encoded.

Deprecated: use json.stringify(value, {indent: 2}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use json.stringify(value, {indent: 2}) instead.

functions.name: isArray
functions.doc: isArray reports whether text is a JSON document whose root is an array.

functions.name: isObject
functions.doc: isObject reports whether text is a JSON document whose root is an object.

functions.name: isValid
functions.doc: isValid reports whether text is a JSON document json.parse accepts.

functions.name: open
functions.doc:
open opens the JSON file at path for reading one token at a time, so a
large document never has to fit in memory. Read it with stream.events(),
stream.skip() and stream.readObject(), and close it when done. Options:
maxBytes (refuse files larger than this many bytes; no limit by default).
Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't
be opened, and ValueError when it is larger than maxBytes. Passing a
number instead of options is the deprecated form of {maxBytes: n}.

functions.name: parse
functions.signature: json.parse(text: any, options?: object) -> result<any, error>
functions.doc:
parse reads a JSON document from text: objects, arrays, strings, numbers,
booleans and null. Fails with ParseError, naming the line and column, for
malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, numbers out of range and trailing
data. Options: type ("object", "array" or "any", the default) also fails
with ParseError when the document is a different kind of value. Use
json.parse<T>(text) to check the result against an OSL type.

functions.name: parseArray
functions.doc:
parseArray parses text and requires a JSON array.

Deprecated: use json.parse(text, {type: "array"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use json.parse(text, {type: "array"}) instead.

functions.name: parseFile
functions.signature: json.parseFile(path: string, options?: object) -> result<any, error>
functions.doc:
parseFile reads and parses the JSON file at path, with the same options
as json.parse. Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when
the file can't be read and ParseError when it isn't valid JSON.

functions.name: parseObject
functions.doc:
parseObject parses text and requires a JSON object.

Deprecated: use json.parse(text, {type: "object"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use json.parse(text, {type: "object"}) instead.

functions.name: stringify
functions.doc:
stringify encodes value as JSON text, with object keys in sorted order.
Options: indent (spaces per nesting level, default 0 for compact output).
Throws ValueError for NaN, infinite numbers and cyclic values, and
TypeError for values JSON can't represent, such as functions.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close closes the file. Closing twice is a no-op, and every other method
throws StateError afterwards. Fails with IOError if the file can't be
closed cleanly.

methods.name: error
methods.doc:
error returns the stream's failure message, or "".

Deprecated: errors are now thrown by stream.events() and returned by
stream.skip() and stream.readObject().
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: errors are now thrown by stream.events() and returned by stream.skip() and stream.readObject().

methods.name: events
methods.signature: stream.events() -> iter<{depth: int, type: string, value: any}>
methods.returns: iter<{depth: int, type: string, value: any}>
methods.doc:
events iterates over the rest of the document one token at a time, as
records {type, value, depth} (see json.Event). The loop shares the
stream's position, so calling skip() or readObject() inside it consumes
those tokens. Throws ParseError, naming the line and column, when the
file turns out to be malformed; wrap the loop in try() to handle it.
Throws StateError once the stream is closed.

methods.name: more
methods.doc:
more reports whether another event can be read.

Deprecated: use for event in stream.events() instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use for event in stream.events() instead.

methods.name: next
methods.doc:
next reads the next event, or {type: "eof"} at the end.

Deprecated: use for event in stream.events() instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use for event in stream.events() instead.

methods.name: ok
methods.doc:
ok reports whether the stream has not failed.

Deprecated: errors are now thrown by stream.events() and returned by
stream.skip() and stream.readObject().
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: errors are now thrown by stream.events() and returned by stream.skip() and stream.readObject().

methods.name: readObject
methods.doc:
readObject reads the next value, which must be an object whose values
are all strings, numbers, booleans or null, and returns it. Options:
maxKeys (fail when the object has more keys; no limit by default) and
stringsOnly (require every value to be a string; default false). Fails
with ParseError when the next value is not such an object or the JSON is
malformed, and ValueError when it has more than maxKeys keys. Throws
StateError once the stream is closed.

methods.name: readScalarMap
methods.doc:
readScalarMap reads the next value as an object of at most maxValues
scalar values.

Deprecated: use stream.readObject({maxKeys: n}) instead.

methods.name: readStringMap
methods.doc:
readStringMap reads the next value as an object of at most maxValues
string values.

Deprecated: use stream.readObject({maxKeys: n, stringsOnly: true}) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use stream.readObject({maxKeys: n, stringsOnly: true}) instead.

methods.name: skip
methods.doc:
skip skips the next value, however deeply nested, without decoding it,
and reports whether there was one: false at the end of the document or
when the next token closes the enclosing object or array. After a "key"
event it skips that key's value. Fails with ParseError for malformed
JSON and throws StateError once the stream is closed.

packages.name: jwt
packages.description: Create and check HMAC-signed JSON Web Tokens (HS256, HS384, HS512).

functions.name: check
functions.signature: jwt.check(token: string, secret: byte[], options?: object) -> result<object, error>
functions.doc:
check verifies a token signed with secret and returns its claims. It
accepts HS256, and HS384 and HS512 when secret is long enough for them
(48 and 64 bytes), never an unsigned token, and rejects a token past its
exp time or before its nbf time. Options: algorithm, the one algorithm
to accept ("HS256", "HS384" or "HS512"); leeway, the clock difference to
allow in milliseconds (default 0); audience, a string or an array of
strings, one of which the token's aud claim must hold; and issuer, a
string or an array of strings, one of which its iss claim must be. Fails
with ParseError for a malformed token, ExpiredError for an expired
token, PermissionError for a wrong signature, an unsigned token, one not
valid yet, another algorithm than the option names or one that needs a
longer secret, or the wrong audience or issuer, UnsupportedError for an
algorithm other than HS256, HS384 and HS512, and ValueError for a secret
under 32 bytes, or shorter than the algorithm option needs.

functions.name: create
functions.signature: jwt.create(claims: object, secret: byte[], options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
create signs claims into a token with secret. It adds iat, the time it
was issued in unix seconds, unless claims has one, and leaves claims
itself unchanged. Options: expiresIn, the token's lifetime in
milliseconds, which sets exp; and algorithm, "HS256" (the default),
"HS384" or "HS512". secret is at least as long as the algorithm's hash:
32 bytes for HS256, 48 for HS384 and 64 for HS512, such as
crypto.randomHex(32); a shorter one fails with ValueError. Throws
ValueError for a bad option or claims that can't be written as JSON.

functions.name: decode
functions.signature: jwt.decode(token: string) -> result<{error: string? (deprecated), header: object, payload: object}, error>
functions.returns: result<{error: string? (deprecated), header: object, payload: object}, error>
functions.doc:
decode reads a token's header and claims without checking its
signature, as {header, payload}; the deprecated key error is always
null. Never trust the result: use jwt.check for that. Fails with
ParseError for a malformed token.

functions.name: encode
functions.signature: jwt.encode(header: any, payload: any, secret: any) -> string
functions.doc:
encode signs a raw JSON header and payload with HS256, whatever alg the
header names.

Deprecated: use jwt.create(claims, secret, options) instead, which
writes a header that matches the signature.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use jwt.create(claims, secret, options) instead, which writes a header that matches the signature.

functions.name: getClaim
functions.doc:
getClaim returns one claim of a token without checking its signature, or
null when it is missing or the token is malformed.

Deprecated: use jwt.check(token, secret)[name] for a claim you can
trust, or jwt.decode(token).payload[name].
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use jwt.check(token, secret)[name] for a claim you can trust, or jwt.decode(token).payload[name].

functions.name: isExpired
functions.doc:
isExpired reports whether a token's exp time has passed, without
checking its signature. A token without exp never expires; a malformed
token, or one whose exp isn't a number, counts as expired.

functions.name: refresh
functions.signature: jwt.refresh(token: any, secret: any, expiresIn: any) -> string
functions.doc:
refresh verifies a token like jwt.verify and signs its claims again,
expiring expiresIn seconds from now, or returns "" when it isn't valid.

Deprecated: use jwt.renew(token, secret, {expiresIn: ms}) instead; note
that expiresIn there is in milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use jwt.renew(token, secret, {expiresIn: ms}) instead; note that expiresIn there is in milliseconds.

functions.name: renew
functions.signature: jwt.renew(token: string, secret: byte[], options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
renew checks a token like jwt.check and returns a new one with the same
claims, a fresh iat and, with the option expiresIn (ms), a new lifetime;
without it, the old lifetime from iat to exp carries over. Option:
algorithm, by default the old token's. Fails like jwt.check, and with
ValueError when secret is too short for the new algorithm.

functions.name: sign
functions.signature: jwt.sign(claims: object, secret: any, ...expiresIn: any) -> string
functions.doc:
sign signs claims with HS256, adding exp and iat when expiresIn, in
seconds, is above 0. Returns "" when claims can't be written as JSON.

Deprecated: use jwt.create(claims, secret, {expiresIn: ms}) instead;
note that expiresIn there is in milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use jwt.create(claims, secret, {expiresIn: ms}) instead; note that expiresIn there is in milliseconds.

functions.name: signWithExpiry
functions.signature: jwt.signWithExpiry(claims: object, secret: any, expiresIn: any) -> string
functions.doc:
signWithExpiry signs a copy of claims with iat and exp added, expiring
expiresIn seconds from now, rounded up to the next whole second.

Deprecated: use jwt.create(claims, secret, {expiresIn: ms}) instead;
note that expiresIn there is in milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use jwt.create(claims, secret, {expiresIn: ms}) instead; note that expiresIn there is in milliseconds.

functions.name: verify
functions.doc:
verify checks an HS256 token and returns {valid: true, header, payload},
or {valid: false, error} with error one of "token_too_large",
"invalid_token_format", "invalid_signature", "invalid_payload",
"invalid_exp", "token_expired", "invalid_header" or
"unsupported_algorithm".

Deprecated: use jwt.check(token, secret) instead, which returns the
claims and fails with a typed error.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use jwt.check(token, secret) instead, which returns the claims and fails with a typed error.

packages.name: layout
packages.description: Lay out std:ui tags in boxes without a screen: build nodes, measure them, find what sits at a point, and inspect and change a tree.
packages.about:
osl:go ui_text

Tags compile to ui.node values, and std:window draws them with this
package's layout, which follows the same rules as a web page: hug, fill
and fixed sizes, gap, pad and nine-point align. Text is shaped with the
UI's own font, built in, so a layout measures the same on every machine.

functions.name: absolute
functions.doc:
absolute builds an <absolute>: children outside the parent's layout, at
its pad values from the parent's edges.

functions.name: at
functions.signature: layout.at(node: ui.Node, x: number, y: number, options?: object) -> {height: number, key: string, tag: string, text: string, width: number, x: number, y: number}?
functions.returns: {height: number, key: string, tag: string, text: string, width: number, x: number, y: number}?
functions.doc:
at is the innermost element at x, y, counted from 1, when node is laid
out in a screen of opts.width by opts.height (800 by 600), as boxes
lists it, or null when nothing is there.

functions.name: box
functions.doc: box builds a <box>: a column that only groups its children.

functions.name: boxes
functions.signature: layout.boxes(node: ui.Node, options?: object) -> {height: number, key: string, tag: string, text: string, width: number, x: number, y: number}[]
functions.returns: {height: number, key: string, tag: string, text: string, width: number, x: number, y: number}[]
functions.doc:
boxes lays node out in a screen of opts.width by opts.height (800 by 600
when left out) and lists where every element lands, parents before
their children: {tag, x, y, width, height, text, key}, with x and y
counting from 1 at the screen's top-left corner. Text is measured with
the UI's own font, as a window draws it. Hidden elements are left out.
Throws ValueError for a size that isn't above 0.

functions.name: button
functions.doc:
button builds a <button> labelled text; its on:click prop is what it
runs.

functions.name: checkbox
functions.doc: checkbox builds a <checkbox>, with a bind or checked prop.

functions.name: column
functions.doc:
column builds a <column>: children stacked top to bottom.

	layout.column({gap: 8, pad: 16}, [layout.text({size: 20}, "Hi")])

functions.name: find
functions.doc:
find is the first node in node's tree, node itself included, for which
test returns true, going depth first, or null.

functions.name: findAll
functions.doc:
findAll lists the nodes in node's tree, node itself included, for which
test returns true, depth first.

functions.name: grid
functions.doc: grid builds a <grid>: children in rows of equal columns.

functions.name: image
functions.doc: image builds an <image> of the file or URL in its src prop.

functions.name: input
functions.doc: input builds an <input>, usually with a bind prop.

functions.name: link
functions.doc:
link builds a <link> labelled text, to its href prop or running its
on:click prop.

functions.name: measure
functions.signature: layout.measure(node: ui.Node, options?: object) -> {height: number, width: number}
functions.doc:
measure is how big node is when it hugs its content: {width, height},
with text wrapped at opts.maxWidth when given. A fixed size is its size.

functions.name: replace
functions.signature: layout.replace(root: ui.Node, old: ui.Node, replacement: ui.Node) -> ui.Node
functions.doc:
replace returns a copy of root with the node old, found by identity,
swapped for replacement, everywhere it appears. root itself is
unchanged.

functions.name: row
functions.doc: row builds a <row>: children side by side.

functions.name: scroll
functions.doc:
scroll builds a <scroll>: a column whose children scroll when they
don't fit.

functions.name: spacer
functions.doc: spacer builds a <spacer>, which takes the room left along its parent.

functions.name: stack
functions.doc: stack builds a <stack>: children on top of each other.

functions.name: text
functions.doc: text builds a <text> showing text.

packages.name: log
packages.description: Levelled, timestamped console logging with a history of recent entries and progress output.
packages.about:
Levels are DEBUG, INFO, SUCCESS, WARN and ERROR. Entries below the current
level (INFO by default) are dropped. The last 1000 entries are kept for
log.history().

functions.name: assert
functions.doc:
assert logs message at ERROR level ("Assertion failed" without one) when
condition is false, and does nothing otherwise. It never throws; use
std:testing to stop on a failed check.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: clear clears the terminal screen.

functions.name: clearHistory
functions.doc: clearHistory removes every recorded entry.

functions.name: countByLevel
functions.doc:
countByLevel returns how many recorded entries each level has, keyed by
level name; levels with no entries are absent.

functions.name: countdown
functions.doc:
countdown counts down from from to 1 on one line, one number per second,
then prints message followed by Done!. Blocks for from seconds. Throws
ValueError when from is negative.

functions.name: debug
functions.doc:
debug prints message at DEBUG level, formatted like log.info. DEBUG is
below the default level, so call log.setLevel("DEBUG") to see it.

functions.name: disableHistory
functions.doc: disableHistory clears the history and stops recording entries.

functions.name: enableHistory
functions.doc:
enableHistory clears the history and starts recording entries again.
History is on by default.

functions.name: error
functions.doc: error prints message at ERROR level, formatted like log.info.

functions.name: exportHistory
functions.doc:
exportHistory writes the recorded entries to the file at path, one per
line as "[HH:MM:SS] [LEVEL] message", replacing the file. Fails with
NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be written.

functions.name: fatal
functions.doc:
fatal logs message at ERROR level, prefixed with [FATAL], and exits the
program with status 1 at once: deferred code doesn't run and running
threads stop. Throw an error instead when callers should be able to
recover.

functions.name: flush
functions.doc: flush writes any output that setBuffer is holding back.

functions.name: getHistory
functions.doc:
getHistory returns the recorded entries as objects with timestamp
(HH:MM:SS text), level and message keys.

Deprecated: use log.history(), whose entries have a unix-ms time, instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use log.history(), whose entries have a unix-ms time, instead.

functions.name: getLevel
functions.doc:
getLevel returns the current level's name.

Deprecated: use log.level() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use log.level() instead.

functions.name: group
functions.doc: group prints a heading that starts a group of related output.

functions.name: groupEnd
functions.doc: groupEnd prints the line that ends a group started with log.group.

functions.name: history
functions.signature: log.history() -> {level: string, message: string, time: number}[]
functions.doc:
history returns the recorded entries, oldest first: at most the most
recent 1000 at or above the level in force when they were logged. Each
entry has keys time (unix ms), level and message (formatted, without the
time or level).

functions.name: info
functions.doc:
info prints message at INFO level with the time, applying printf-style
verbs (%s, %d, %f, ...) to args; leftover args are appended with spaces.

functions.name: json
functions.doc: json prints data as JSON on one line.

functions.name: level
functions.doc: level returns the current level's name, such as "INFO".

functions.name: log
functions.doc:
log prints message at the named level, formatted like log.info. Throws
ValueError for an unknown level name.

functions.name: plain
functions.doc:
plain prints message without a level, time or colour, formatted like
log.info. It ignores the level and isn't recorded in the history.

functions.name: progress
functions.signature: log.progress(current: number, total: number, options?: object)
functions.doc:
progress draws a progress bar for current out of total on the current
line, redrawing in place on each call and ending the line once current
reaches total. Options: width (characters, default 30) and label (text
before the bar, default ""). Throws ValueError when total isn't above 0
or width is negative.

functions.name: progressBar
functions.doc:
progressBar draws a progress bar; it takes current, total, width and
label and draws nothing when total is 0.

Deprecated: use log.progress(current, total, {width, label}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use log.progress(current, total, {width, label}) instead.

functions.name: separator
functions.doc: separator prints a line of 80 dashes.

functions.name: setBuffer
functions.doc:
setBuffer batches output from log and print, writing it at most
milliseconds later or once 64 KB is waiting, so a program that writes many
lines makes few system calls. Zero or less writes every line straight
through again, which is the default.

functions.name: setLevel
functions.doc:
setLevel sets the least severe level that is printed and recorded:
"DEBUG", "INFO" (the default), "SUCCESS", "WARN" or "ERROR". Throws
ValueError for any other name.

functions.name: spinner
functions.doc:
spinner prints the current frame of a spinner before message on the
current line; call it repeatedly to animate it, and with done true to
replace it with a check mark and end the line.

functions.name: success
functions.doc:
success prints message at SUCCESS level, which ranks with INFO, formatted
like log.info.

functions.name: table
functions.doc: table prints rows (arrays of cells) under headers as a text table.

functions.name: time
functions.doc:
time prints message prefixed with the current time of day to the
millisecond, such as [14:03:07.123].

functions.name: timestamp
functions.doc:
timestamp prints message prefixed with the current time in unix
microseconds, such as [1760000000123456].

functions.name: trace
functions.doc: trace prints message at DEBUG level, prefixed with [TRACE].

functions.name: warn
functions.doc: warn prints message at WARN level, formatted like log.info.

functions.name: withTimestamp
functions.doc:
withTimestamp prints message at the named level, prefixed with the date
and time. Throws ValueError for an unknown level name.
