methods.name: loadString
methods.doc:
loadString reports whether code compiles, without running it.

Deprecated: use state.run(code), which fails with ParseError for a
syntax error.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use state.run(code), which fails with ParseError for a syntax error.

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
register makes fn callable from Lua as the global function name. Lua
arguments are converted to OSL values and fn's result back to Lua; an
error fn throws becomes a Lua error, which Lua's pcall can catch and
which otherwise fails the run with the error's own kind. Throws
StateError after close.

methods.name: run
methods.signature: state.run(code: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
run runs Lua code in this state, so the globals it sets stay for later
calls. Option: timeout in milliseconds, by default the state's. Fails
with ParseError, TimeoutError, ValueError or RuntimeError like
lua.run; an error thrown by a registered OSL function keeps its kind.
Throws StateError after close.

methods.name: runFile
methods.signature: state.runFile(path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
runFile runs a Lua file in this state. Option: timeout in milliseconds,
by default the state's. Fails with NotFoundError or IOError when the
file can't be read, and otherwise like state.run. Throws StateError
after close.

methods.name: set
methods.doc:
set sets a global to a copy of value: arrays become tables with keys 1
to n and objects tables with string keys. Throws StateError after
close.

methods.name: setGlobal
methods.doc:
setGlobal sets a global's value.

Deprecated: use state.set(name, value) instead.

packages.name: math
packages.description: Math functions and constants beyond the built-ins: trigonometry, number theory, statistics and binary64 primitives.
packages.about:
Angles are in radians; use math.radians(degrees) and math.degrees(radians)
to convert. Statistics of an empty array fail with a ValueError result,
and factorial, fibonacci and lcm fail with an OverflowError result when the
answer doesn't fit an int. pi, e, phi and tau are constants: math.pi.

functions.name: abs
functions.doc: abs returns the absolute value of x.

functions.name: acos
functions.doc: acos returns the arccosine of x in radians, or NaN outside -1 to 1.

functions.name: asin
functions.doc: asin returns the arcsine of x in radians, or NaN outside -1 to 1.

functions.name: atan
functions.doc: atan returns the arctangent of x in radians.

functions.name: atan2
functions.doc:
atan2 returns the angle in radians from the positive x axis to the point
(x, y), from -pi to pi. Note that y comes first.

functions.name: avg
functions.doc:
avg returns the arithmetic mean of numbers. Fails with ValueError for an
empty array.

functions.name: bits
functions.doc:
bits returns the IEEE 754 binary64 encoding of x, reinterpreted as a signed
64-bit integer. fromBits(bits(x)) is x, including NaN payloads and -0.

functions.name: cbrt
functions.doc: cbrt returns the cube root of x.

functions.name: ceil
functions.doc: ceil rounds x up to the nearest whole number.

functions.name: clamp
functions.signature: math.clamp(value: number, min: number, max: number) -> number
functions.doc:
clamp limits value to the range from min to max. The bounds may come in
either order.

functions.name: correlation
functions.signature: math.correlation(a: number[], b: number[]) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
correlation returns the Pearson correlation of two equally long arrays
of paired values, from -1 to 1. Fails with ValueError for empty arrays,
arrays of different lengths, or an array whose values are all equal,
which has no correlation.

functions.name: cos
functions.doc: cos returns the cosine of x radians.

functions.name: cosh
functions.doc: cosh returns the hyperbolic cosine of x.

functions.name: covariance
functions.signature: math.covariance(a: number[], b: number[]) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
covariance returns the population covariance of two equally long arrays
of paired values. Fails with ValueError for empty arrays or arrays of
different lengths.

functions.name: degrees
functions.doc: degrees converts radians to degrees.

functions.name: exp
functions.doc: exp returns e raised to the power x.

functions.name: factorial
functions.doc:
factorial returns n! (1 * 2 * ... * n). Fails with ValueError for a
negative n, and with OverflowError for one above 20, whose factorial
doesn't fit an int.

functions.name: fibonacci
functions.doc:
fibonacci returns the nth Fibonacci number, counting fibonacci(0) as 0
and fibonacci(1) as 1. Fails with ValueError for a negative n, and with
OverflowError for one above 92, whose result doesn't fit an int.

functions.name: floor
functions.doc: floor rounds x down to the nearest whole number.

functions.name: fma
functions.signature: math.fma(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> number
functions.doc: fma returns x * y + z rounded once, as IEEE 754 fusedMultiplyAdd does.

functions.name: fromBits
functions.doc: fromBits returns the number whose IEEE 754 binary64 encoding is bits.

functions.name: fround
functions.doc: fround matches JavaScript's Math.fround: the nearest float32 value, as a number.

functions.name: gcd
functions.doc:
gcd returns the greatest common divisor of a and b, which is never
negative; math.gcd(0, 0) is 0. The one result an int can't hold, 2^63
from the smallest int, wraps as int arithmetic does.

functions.name: geometricMean
functions.doc:
geometricMean returns the nth root of the product of n numbers, which
must all be above 0. Fails with ValueError for an empty array or a
number that is 0 or less.

functions.name: harmonicMean
functions.doc:
harmonicMean returns the count of numbers divided by the sum of their
reciprocals; they must all be above 0. Fails with ValueError for an
empty array or a number that is 0 or less.

functions.name: hypot
functions.doc:
hypot returns the length of the hypotenuse, sqrt(x*x + y*y), without
overflowing for large values.

functions.name: iqr
functions.doc:
iqr returns the interquartile range of numbers, q3 minus q1. Fails with
ValueError for an empty array.

functions.name: isFinite
functions.doc: isFinite reports whether x is neither infinite nor NaN.

functions.name: isInfinite
functions.doc:
isInfinite reports whether x is positive or negative infinity; use
math.sign(x) for which one.

functions.name: isNaN
functions.doc: isNaN reports whether x is NaN (not a number).

functions.name: isPrime
functions.doc:
isPrime reports whether n is a prime number. Numbers below 2 and numbers
with a fractional part are not prime.

functions.name: lcm
functions.signature: math.lcm(a: int, b: int) -> result<int, error>
functions.doc:
lcm returns the least common multiple of a and b, which is never
negative, or 0 when either is 0. Fails with OverflowError when the
result doesn't fit an int.

functions.name: ldexp
functions.doc: ldexp returns x * 2^exp, rounding once even when the result is subnormal.

functions.name: lerp
functions.signature: math.lerp(start: number, end: number, t: number) -> number
functions.doc:
lerp interpolates linearly from start to end: t of 0 gives start, 1 gives
end, and values outside 0 to 1 extrapolate.

functions.name: log
functions.doc:
log returns the natural logarithm of x: NaN when x is negative and
-Infinity when it is 0.

functions.name: log10
functions.doc: log10 returns the base-10 logarithm of x.

functions.name: log2
functions.doc: log2 returns the base-2 logarithm of x.

functions.name: max
functions.doc: max returns the larger of a and b.

functions.name: maxOf
functions.doc:
maxOf returns the largest of numbers. Fails with ValueError for an empty
array.

functions.name: median
functions.doc:
median returns the middle value of numbers, or the mean of the two
middle values for an even count. Fails with ValueError for an empty
array.

functions.name: min
functions.doc: min returns the smaller of a and b.

functions.name: minOf
functions.doc:
minOf returns the smallest of numbers. Fails with ValueError for an
empty array.

functions.name: mod
functions.doc:
mod returns the remainder of a divided by b, with the sign of a:
math.mod(-7, 3) is -1. Throws ValueError when b is 0.

functions.name: mode
functions.doc:
mode returns the most frequent values in numbers, in ascending order:
one value usually, several on a tie, and none for an empty array.

functions.name: normalize
functions.doc:
normalize rescales numbers to the range 0 to 1, mapping the smallest to
0 and the largest to 1. When the numbers are all equal, each becomes 0.

functions.name: percentile
functions.signature: math.percentile(numbers: number[], p: number) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
percentile returns the pth percentile of numbers, for p from 0 to 100,
interpolating between the closest values: the 50th is the median. Throws
ValueError for p outside 0 to 100, and fails with ValueError for an empty
array.

functions.name: pow
functions.doc: pow returns base raised to the power exponent.

functions.name: primes
functions.doc:
primes returns the first count prime numbers, starting at 2. Throws
ValueError for a negative count.

functions.name: product
functions.doc: product returns numbers multiplied together, or 1 for an empty array.

functions.name: quantile
functions.signature: math.quantile(numbers: number[], q: number) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
quantile returns the qth quantile of numbers, for q from 0 to 1, the
same as math.percentile(numbers, q * 100). Throws ValueError for q
outside 0 to 1, and fails with ValueError for an empty array.

functions.name: quartiles
functions.signature: math.quartiles(numbers: number[]) -> result<{q1: number, q2: number, q3: number}, error>
functions.returns: result<{q1: number, q2: number, q3: number}, error>
functions.doc:
quartiles returns the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of numbers as
{q1, q2, q3}. Fails with ValueError for an empty array.

functions.name: radians
functions.doc: radians converts degrees to radians.

functions.name: rangeOf
functions.doc:
rangeOf returns the largest of numbers minus the smallest. Fails with
ValueError for an empty array.

functions.name: round
functions.doc:
round rounds x to the nearest whole number, with halves rounded away from
zero: 2.5 is 3 and -2.5 is -3.

functions.name: sign
functions.doc: sign returns 1 for a positive x, -1 for a negative one and 0 for 0 or NaN.

functions.name: sin
functions.doc: sin returns the sine of x radians.

functions.name: sinh
functions.doc: sinh returns the hyperbolic sine of x.

functions.name: sqrt
functions.doc: sqrt returns the square root of x, or NaN when x is negative.

functions.name: standardDeviation
functions.signature: math.standardDeviation(numbers: number[], options?: object) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
standardDeviation returns the population standard deviation of numbers,
the square root of math.variance. With the option sample: true it returns
the sample standard deviation instead. Fails with ValueError for an
empty array, or fewer than 2 numbers for a sample.

functions.name: sum
functions.doc: sum returns the total of numbers, or 0 for an empty array.

functions.name: tan
functions.doc: tan returns the tangent of x radians.

functions.name: tanh
functions.doc: tanh returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.

functions.name: toFixed
functions.doc:
toFixed formats x with exactly digits digits after the decimal point,
as C's printf("%.*f") does: the exact binary value of x is rounded to
the nearest, with exact halves rounded to even, so math.toFixed(2.5, 0)
is "2" and math.toFixed(0.125, 2) is "0.12". NaN and the infinities format as "NaN", "+Inf"
and "-Inf". Throws ValueError for digits outside 0 to 100.

functions.name: toPercent
functions.doc:
toPercent returns x as a percentage of total: math.toPercent(25, 200) is
12.5. Throws ValueError when total is 0.

functions.name: trunc
functions.doc: trunc drops the fractional part of x, rounding toward zero.

functions.name: variance
functions.signature: math.variance(numbers: number[], options?: object) -> result<number, error>
functions.doc:
variance returns the population variance of numbers: the mean squared
difference from their mean. With the option sample: true it returns the
sample variance instead, dividing by one less than the count. Fails with
ValueError for an empty array, or fewer than 2 numbers for a sample.

functions.name: zScores
functions.doc:
zScores returns how many population standard deviations each of numbers
is from their mean. When the numbers are all equal, every score is 0.

constants.name: e
constants.doc:
E is Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm,
2.718281828459045.

constants.name: phi
constants.doc: Phi is the golden ratio, 1.618033988749895.

constants.name: pi
constants.doc:
Pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter,
3.141592653589793.

constants.name: tau
constants.doc: Tau is a full turn in radians, 2 * pi.

packages.name: md
packages.description: Converts Markdown (with GitHub tables, task lists and strikethrough) to HTML and HTML back to Markdown.

functions.name: fromHTML
functions.doc:
fromHTML converts HTML to Markdown. Fails with ParseError when the HTML
can't be converted.

functions.name: sanitize
functions.doc:
sanitize returns Markdown text with raw HTML and unsafe links removed, by
rendering it to safe HTML and converting that back to Markdown. Fails
with ParseError when the rendered HTML can't be converted back.

functions.name: toHTML
functions.doc:
toHTML renders Markdown text as HTML, with GitHub Flavored Markdown
(tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks) and an id on every
heading. Raw HTML in the text and javascript: links are dropped unless
the unsafe option is true; only set it for text you trust. Options:
unsafe (boolean, default false).

functions.name: toHTMLUnsafe
functions.doc:
toHTMLUnsafe renders Markdown text as HTML and keeps any raw HTML in it.

Deprecated: use md.toHTML(text, {unsafe: true}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use md.toHTML(text, {unsafe: true}) instead.

packages.name: mem
packages.description: Inspect the program's memory use, write pprof profiles and serve live profiling data.

functions.name: address
functions.doc:
address returns the deprecated package-level server's address, or "".

Deprecated: use the Server from mem.serve(address) and server.address()
instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use the Server from mem.serve(address) and server.address() instead.

functions.name: dump
functions.signature: mem.dump(path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
dump writes a pprof profile to path, replacing the file atomically, for
`go tool pprof`. Options: profile (default "heap") names the profile:
"heap", "allocs", "goroutine", "threadcreate", "block" or "mutex". A heap
or allocs profile runs a garbage collection first. Fails with
NotFoundError when the directory doesn't exist, PermissionError or
IOError. Throws ValueError for an unknown profile.

functions.name: dumpProfile
functions.doc:
dumpProfile writes a named pprof profile and reports whether it worked.

Deprecated: use mem.dump(path, {profile: name}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use mem.dump(path, {profile: name}) instead.

functions.name: gc
functions.signature: mem.gc() -> {alloc: int, frees: int, gcCPUFraction: number, gcSys: int, goroutines: int, heapAlloc: int, heapIdle: int, heapInuse: int, heapObjects: int, heapReleased: int, heapSys: int, liveObjects: int, mallocs: int, mcacheInuse: int, mspanInuse: int, nextGC: int, numGC: int, otherSys: int, pauseTotalNs: int, profileRate: int, stackInuse: int, stackSys: int, sys: int, totalAlloc: int}
functions.returns: {alloc: int, frees: int, gcCPUFraction: number, gcSys: int, goroutines: int, heapAlloc: int, heapIdle: int, heapInuse: int, heapObjects: int, heapReleased: int, heapSys: int, liveObjects: int, mallocs: int, mcacheInuse: int, mspanInuse: int, nextGC: int, numGC: int, otherSys: int, pauseTotalNs: int, profileRate: int, stackInuse: int, stackSys: int, sys: int, totalAlloc: int}
functions.doc: gc runs a garbage collection and then returns mem.stats().

functions.name: profileRate
functions.doc:
profileRate returns how many bytes are allocated, on average, between
samples in the heap profile; 0 means heap profiling is off.

functions.name: serve
functions.doc:
serve starts a pprof HTTP server in the background on address (such as
"127.0.0.1:6060", or ":0" for any free port) and returns its Server
handle; profiles are under /debug/pprof/. Anyone who can reach the
address can read them, so prefer a loopback address. Fails with
NetworkError when the address can't be listened on.

functions.name: setGCPercent
functions.doc:
setGCPercent sets how much the heap may grow past the live data from the
last garbage collection before the next one starts, as a percentage
(Go's GOGC), and returns the previous setting. The default is 100, or
the GOGC environment variable. A larger value collects less often and
uses more memory, which suits a program with a small live heap that
allocates a lot. A negative value turns garbage collection off, though
mem.setMemoryLimit can still trigger it.

functions.name: setMemoryLimit
functions.doc:
setMemoryLimit sets a soft limit in bytes on the memory the Go runtime
uses (Go's GOMEMLIMIT), collecting garbage more often as it nears the
limit, and returns the previous limit. Pass 0 for no limit; a previous
value of 0 means there was none, so the result can be passed back to
restore it. Throws ValueError for a negative limit.

functions.name: setProfileRate
functions.doc:
setProfileRate sets the heap profile sampling rate in bytes (0 turns it
off; 1 records every allocation) and returns the previous rate. Set it
early, before the allocations to profile. Throws ValueError for a
negative rate.

functions.name: stats
functions.signature: mem.stats() -> {alloc: int, frees: int, gcCPUFraction: number, gcSys: int, goroutines: int, heapAlloc: int, heapIdle: int, heapInuse: int, heapObjects: int, heapReleased: int, heapSys: int, liveObjects: int, mallocs: int, mcacheInuse: int, mspanInuse: int, nextGC: int, numGC: int, otherSys: int, pauseTotalNs: int, profileRate: int, stackInuse: int, stackSys: int, sys: int, totalAlloc: int}
functions.returns: {alloc: int, frees: int, gcCPUFraction: number, gcSys: int, goroutines: int, heapAlloc: int, heapIdle: int, heapInuse: int, heapObjects: int, heapReleased: int, heapSys: int, liveObjects: int, mallocs: int, mcacheInuse: int, mspanInuse: int, nextGC: int, numGC: int, otherSys: int, pauseTotalNs: int, profileRate: int, stackInuse: int, stackSys: int, sys: int, totalAlloc: int}
functions.doc:
stats returns a snapshot of memory statistics with the keys alloc,
totalAlloc, sys, mallocs, frees, liveObjects, heapAlloc, heapSys,
heapIdle, heapInuse, heapReleased, heapObjects, stackInuse, stackSys,
mspanInuse, mcacheInuse, gcSys, otherSys, nextGC (sizes in bytes),
numGC, pauseTotalNs (nanoseconds), gcCPUFraction (0 to 1), goroutines
and profileRate.

functions.name: stop
functions.doc:
stop stops the server started by the deprecated package-level serve and
reports whether one was running.

Deprecated: use the Server from mem.serve(address) and server.close()
instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use the Server from mem.serve(address) and server.close() instead.

methods.name: address
methods.doc:
address returns the address the server listens on, with the real port
when it was started on port 0.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: close stops the server and frees its port. Closing again does nothing.

packages.name: mime
packages.description: Looks up media types by file extension and parses and formats Content-Type values.

functions.name: byFilename
functions.doc:
byFilename returns the media type for a file name, or "" when unknown.

Deprecated: use mime.typeByFilename(path) instead, which returns null for
unknown extensions.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use mime.typeByFilename(path) instead, which returns null for unknown extensions.

functions.name: extByType
functions.doc:
extByType returns the conventional file extension for a media type, with
its leading dot (".png" for "image/png", ".jpg" for "image/jpeg"), or null
when the type is unknown. Parameters such as "; charset=utf-8" are ignored.

functions.name: format
functions.doc:
format builds a Content-Type value from a media type and its parameters,
quoting values where needed: mime.format("text/plain", {charset: "utf-8"})
is "text/plain; charset=utf-8". Throws ValueError when mediaType or a
parameter name is not a valid token.

functions.name: isAudio
functions.doc:
isAudio reports whether a media type is an audio/* type. Case and
parameters are ignored. A value without "/" is checked as a file name or
extension ("clip.mp3", "mp3"), as before; for paths, use mime.isAudioFile.

functions.name: isAudioFile
functions.doc:
isAudioFile reports whether a file name or path has the extension of an
audio type. The file is not opened.

functions.name: isImage
functions.doc:
isImage reports whether a media type is an image/* type. Case and
parameters are ignored. A value without "/" is checked as a file name or
extension ("cat.png", "png"), as before; for paths, use mime.isImageFile.

functions.name: isImageFile
functions.doc:
isImageFile reports whether a file name or path has the extension of an
image type. The file is not opened.

functions.name: isText
functions.doc:
isText reports whether a media type holds text: text/*, JSON, XML,
JavaScript and the +json and +xml suffix types. Case and parameters are
ignored. A value without "/" is checked as a file name or extension
("notes.txt", "txt"), as before; for paths, use mime.isTextFile.

functions.name: isTextFile
functions.doc:
isTextFile reports whether a file name or path has the extension of a
text type, by the same rules as mime.isText. The file is not opened.

functions.name: isVideo
functions.doc:
isVideo reports whether a media type is a video/* type. Case and
parameters are ignored. A value without "/" is checked as a file name or
extension ("movie.mp4", "mp4"), as before; for paths, use
mime.isVideoFile.

functions.name: isVideoFile
functions.doc:
isVideoFile reports whether a file name or path has the extension of a
video type. The file is not opened.

functions.name: parse
functions.signature: mime.parse(text: string) -> result<{params: string[string], type: string, valid: boolean (deprecated)}, error>
functions.returns: result<{params: string[string], type: string, valid: boolean (deprecated)}, error>
functions.doc:
parse splits a Content-Type value into its lowercased media type and its
parameters, returning {type, params} where params maps each parameter name
(lowercased) to its unquoted value; the deprecated key valid is always
true. Fails with ParseError when text is not a type/subtype pair or
repeats a parameter.

functions.name: resolve
functions.doc:
resolve returns the bare lowercase media type of a media type string, or of
a file name or extension when input has no "/"; "" when unknown.

Deprecated: use mime.parse(text).type for a media type, or
mime.typeByFilename(path) / mime.typeByExt(ext) for a file name.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use mime.parse(text).type for a media type, or mime.typeByFilename(path) / mime.typeByExt(ext) for a file name.

functions.name: typeByExt
functions.doc:
typeByExt returns the media type registered for a file extension, such as
"application/json" for "json" or ".json", or null when the extension is
unknown. Text types carry a charset parameter ("text/html; charset=utf-8").

functions.name: typeByFilename
functions.doc:
typeByFilename returns the media type for a file name or path from its
extension, such as "image/png" for "photos/cat.png", or null when the name
has no known extension.

packages.name: net
packages.description: Opens TCP, Unix and UDP sockets and resolves host names; use std:requests for HTTP and std:url for URLs.

functions.name: addressInfo
functions.signature: net.addressInfo(hostname: string) -> result<{hostname: string, hosts: string[], ips: string[]}, error>
functions.returns: result<{hostname: string, hosts: string[], ips: string[]}, error>
functions.doc:
addressInfo resolves hostname and returns {hostname, hosts, ips}: the
name asked for, its addresses as net.lookupHost returns them, and its IP
addresses as net.lookupIP returns them. Fails like net.lookupHost.

functions.name: connect
functions.signature: net.connect(network: string, address: string, options?: object) -> result<*net.TCPConn, error>
functions.doc:
connect opens a stream connection to address, such as "example.com:80"
or "127.0.0.1:8080" (a socket path for "unix"). network is "tcp", "tcp4",
"tcp6" or "unix". Options: timeout (milliseconds to wait for the
connection, default 5000). Fails with NetworkError when the connection is
refused or unreachable, NotFoundError when the host doesn't resolve,
TimeoutError when it takes too long and ValueError for a malformed address
or unknown network.

functions.name: dial
functions.doc:
dial opens a stream connection, or returns null when it fails.

Deprecated: use net.connect(network, address) instead, which reports why
the connection failed.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use net.connect(network, address) instead, which reports why the connection failed.

functions.name: getAddressInfo
functions.doc:
getAddressInfo resolves hostname into {hostname, hosts, ips}, with empty
arrays when it fails.

Deprecated: use net.addressInfo(hostname) instead, which fails with a
typed error.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use net.addressInfo(hostname) instead, which fails with a typed error.

functions.name: listen
functions.signature: net.listen(network: string, address: string) -> result<*net.Listener, error>
functions.doc:
listen starts accepting stream connections on address, such as
"127.0.0.1:0" (port 0 picks a free port; read it back with localAddr()).
network is "tcp", "tcp4", "tcp6" or "unix". Fails with NetworkError when
the address is in use or can't be bound and ValueError for a malformed
address or unknown network.

functions.name: listenUDP
functions.signature: net.listenUDP(network: string, address: string) -> result<*net.UDPConn, error>
functions.doc:
listenUDP binds a UDP socket to address, such as "127.0.0.1:0". network
is "udp", "udp4" or "udp6". Fails with NetworkError when the address can't
be bound and ValueError for a malformed address or unknown network.

functions.name: lookupHost
functions.doc:
lookupHost resolves hostname to its addresses, as strings such as
"93.184.216.34". Fails with NotFoundError when the host doesn't exist,
TimeoutError when the resolver doesn't answer and NetworkError otherwise.

functions.name: lookupIP
functions.doc:
lookupIP resolves hostname to its IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. Fails like
net.lookupHost.

functions.name: lookupPort
functions.signature: net.lookupPort(service: string, network: string) -> result<int, error>
functions.doc:
lookupPort returns the port number of a service name such as "https" on
network ("tcp" or "udp"); a numeric service is returned as a number.
Fails with NotFoundError for an unknown service.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close closes the connection; a read waiting in another thread then fails
with StateError. Closing twice is a no-op.

methods.name: localAddr
methods.doc: localAddr returns this end's address, such as "127.0.0.1:51514".

methods.name: read
methods.signature: tCPConn.read(maxBytes: int, options?: object) -> result<string, error>
methods.doc:
read waits for data and returns up to maxBytes bytes of it as a string.
Once the peer has closed the connection and everything it sent has been
read, it fails with StateError, so a read loop ends with
`string chunk = conn.read(4096) catch (err) ( break )`. Options: timeout
(milliseconds to wait for data; by default it waits indefinitely). Fails
with TimeoutError when the timeout passes and NetworkError when the
connection breaks. Throws ValueError when maxBytes is less than 1 and
StateError on a connection closed with close(). Reads are capped at 16 MiB.

methods.doc:

methods.name: read
methods.signature: uDPConn.read(maxBytes: int, options?: object) -> result<{addr: string, data: string}, error>
methods.doc:
read waits for the next datagram and returns {data, addr}: its payload as

Throws TypeError for other data types and StateError on a closed socket.

uploadFile uploads the file at path; see uploadBytes. Options: name
(default the file's name), mimeType (default guessed from the
extension). Fails with NotFoundError when the file doesn't exist.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: url is the websocket address the client connects to.

methods.name: userID

methods.name: userRoles
methods.doc: userRoles returns the role names username has.

methods.name: username

methods.name: users
methods.doc: users returns every member.

methods.name: usersBanned
methods.doc: usersBanned returns the banned users.

methods.name: usersOnline
methods.doc: usersOnline returns the members who are online.

methods.name: vote
methods.doc: vote votes in the poll pollID for one or more option ids (strings).

methods.name: ack
methods.doc:
ack marks the channel read: ack(messageID?).

Deprecated: use channel.markRead({messageID}) instead.

methods.name: archive
methods.doc:
archive archives (true) or unarchives (false) the thread. Throws
StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: client
methods.doc: client is the client this handle belongs to.

methods.name: createThread
methods.doc: createThread starts a thread called name in the channel and returns it.

methods.name: createWebhook
methods.doc:
createWebhook creates a webhook called name in the channel and returns it
(with its token).

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
delete deletes the message id.

Deprecated: use (channel.get(id)).delete() instead.

methods.name: edit
methods.doc:
edit edits the message id.

Deprecated: use (channel.get(id)).edit(content) instead.

methods.name: editWith
methods.doc:
editWith edits the message id with a raw payload.

Deprecated: use (channel.get(id)).edit(content, options) instead.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get fetches the message id as a handle. Fails with NotFoundError when it
doesn't exist.

methods.name: info
methods.doc: info returns the channel's or thread's info object.

methods.name: isThread
methods.doc: isThread reports whether the handle is a thread.

methods.name: join
methods.doc: join joins the thread. Throws StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: leave
methods.doc: leave leaves the thread. Throws StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: listThreads
methods.doc: listThreads returns the channel's threads. Options: limit (number).

methods.name: lock
methods.doc:
lock locks (true) or unlocks (false) the thread. Throws StateError on a
channel handle.

methods.name: markRead
methods.doc: markRead marks the channel read. Options: messageID (string, read up to it).

methods.name: message
methods.doc:
message returns the message id as an object, or {}.

Deprecated: use channel.get(id) instead.

methods.name: messages
methods.doc: messages returns up to limit of the newest messages as objects, oldest first.

methods.name: messagesAround
methods.signature: channel.messagesAround(id: string, above: int, below: int) -> result<array, error>
methods.doc:
messagesAround returns the message id with up to above older and below
newer messages.

methods.name: messagesBatch
methods.doc: messagesBatch returns the messages with these ids.

methods.name: messagesBefore
methods.signature: channel.messagesBefore(id: string, limit: int) -> result<array, error>
methods.doc: messagesBefore returns up to limit messages older than the message id.

methods.name: name
methods.doc: name is the channel name ("" for a thread handle made with client.thread).

methods.name: pin
methods.doc:
pin pins the message id.

Deprecated: use message.pin() instead.

methods.name: pinThread
methods.doc: pinThread pins the thread in its channel. Throws StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: pinned
methods.doc: pinned returns the pinned messages.

methods.name: react
methods.doc:
react reacts to the message id.

Deprecated: use message.react(emoji) instead.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: remove deletes the thread. Throws StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: rename
methods.doc: rename renames the thread. Throws StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: replies
methods.doc:
replies returns the replies to the message id, or [].

Deprecated: use message.replies() instead.

methods.name: search
methods.signature: channel.search(query: string, options?: object) -> result<object, error>
methods.doc:
search searches messages for query and returns {results, total,
has_more}. filters is passed to the server as-is (such as {pinned: true}).

methods.name: send
methods.signature: channel.send(content: string, options?: object) -> result<*originchats.Message, error>
methods.doc:
send posts content (text, may be "") and returns the sent message.
Options: embeds (array of embeds or objects), attachments (array of
objects from client.upload), alias ({name, avatar, color}: post under
another name), replyTo (message id), ping (boolean, default true: notify
the replied-to author). Signed when the client is signing.

methods.name: sendAs
methods.doc:
sendAs posts under another name: sendAs(name, content, avatar?, color?).

Deprecated: use channel.send(content, {alias: {name, avatar, color}}) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use channel.send(content, {alias: {name, avatar, color}}) instead.

methods.name: sendAttachment
methods.doc:
sendAttachment posts content with an attachment.

Deprecated: use channel.send(content, {attachments: [attachment]}) instead.

methods.name: sendEmbed
methods.doc:
sendEmbed posts content with an embed.

Deprecated: use channel.send(content, {embeds: [embed]}) instead.

methods.name: sendWith
methods.doc:
sendWith posts a raw payload here.

Deprecated: use channel.send(content, options) instead.

methods.name: threadID
methods.doc: threadID is the thread id, or null for a channel.

methods.name: threads
methods.doc:
threads lists the channel's threads: threads(limit?).

Deprecated: use channel.listThreads({limit}) instead.

methods.name: typing
methods.doc: typing shows the bot as typing here for a few seconds.

methods.name: unpin
methods.doc:
unpin unpins the message id.

Deprecated: use message.unpin() instead.

methods.name: unpinThread
methods.doc: unpinThread unpins the thread. Throws StateError on a channel handle.

methods.name: unreact
methods.doc:
unreact removes a reaction from the message id.

Deprecated: use message.unreact(emoji) instead.

methods.name: webhooks
methods.doc: webhooks returns the channel's webhooks.

methods.name: alias
methods.doc: alias is the {name, avatar, usercolor} the message was posted under, or null.

methods.name: arg
methods.doc:
arg is the index-th word of content (1 for the first), or null when there
are fewer words.

methods.name: args
methods.doc: args splits content on whitespace, handy inside prefix commands.

methods.name: attachments
methods.doc: attachments lists the message's attachment objects.

methods.name: authorID
methods.doc: authorID is the author's rotur user id ("" when the server didn't send one).

methods.name: channel
methods.doc: channel is the name of the channel the message is in.

methods.name: client
methods.doc: client is the client that received or sent the message.

methods.name: content
methods.doc:
content is the message text. Inside a prefix command it is the text after
the prefix.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: data is the message object as the server sent it.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: delete deletes the message.

methods.name: edit
methods.signature: message.edit(content: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
edit replaces the message's text. Options: embeds, attachments (as for
channel.send). Only the bot's own messages can be edited.

methods.name: editWith
methods.doc:
editWith edits the message with a raw payload.

Deprecated: use message.edit(content, options) instead.

methods.name: embeds
methods.doc: embeds lists the message's embed objects.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: id is the message id.

methods.name: interaction
methods.doc: interaction is the slash command call the message answers, or null.

methods.name: isAutomated
methods.doc: isAutomated reports whether a webhook or slash command posted the message.

methods.name: isEdited
methods.doc: isEdited reports whether the message was edited.

methods.name: isEphemeral
methods.doc: isEphemeral reports whether only the bot can see the message.

methods.name: isPinned
methods.doc: isPinned reports whether the message is pinned.

methods.name: isReply
methods.doc: isReply reports whether the message replies to another.

methods.name: isSigned
methods.doc:
isSigned reports whether the message carries a rotur signature (verify
checks it).

methods.name: isThread
methods.doc: isThread reports whether the message is in a thread.

methods.name: mentions
methods.doc:
mentions reports whether the message pings name or contains @name
(ignoring case).

methods.name: mentionsMe
methods.doc: mentionsMe reports whether the message mentions the bot.

methods.name: pin
methods.doc: pin pins the message.

methods.name: pings
methods.doc: pings is the message's mentions as {users, roles, replies}.

methods.name: poll
methods.doc: poll is the poll in the message's embeds ({question, options, ...}), or null.

methods.name: raw
methods.doc: raw is the whole server packet the message arrived in.

methods.name: react
methods.doc: react adds the reaction emoji.

methods.name: reactions
methods.doc: reactions is an object of emoji to the usernames who reacted.

methods.name: replies
methods.doc: replies returns the replies to the message as objects.

methods.name: reply
methods.signature: message.reply(content: string, options?: object) -> result<*originchats.Message, error>
methods.doc:
reply replies to the message in its channel or thread and returns the
reply. Options: ping (boolean, default true: notify the author), embeds,
attachments, alias (as for channel.send).

methods.name: replyEmbed
methods.doc:
replyEmbed replies with content and an embed.

Deprecated: use message.reply(content, {embeds: [embed]}) instead.

methods.name: replyNoPing
methods.doc:
replyNoPing replies without notifying the author.

Deprecated: use message.reply(content, {ping: false}) instead.

methods.name: replyTo
methods.doc: replyTo is the replied-to message summary ({id, user, ...}), or null.

methods.name: replyWith
methods.doc:
replyWith replies with a raw payload.

Deprecated: use message.reply(content, options) instead.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
send posts content in the message's channel.

Deprecated: use message.target().send(content) instead.

methods.name: sendEmbed
methods.doc:
sendEmbed posts content with an embed in the message's channel.

Deprecated: use message.target().send(content, {embeds: [embed]}) instead.

methods.name: sendWith
methods.doc:
sendWith posts a raw payload in the message's channel.

Deprecated: use message.target().send(content, options) instead.

methods.name: sentAt
methods.doc: sentAt is when the message was sent, in unix ms.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: target is a handle for the channel or thread the message is in.

methods.name: threadID
methods.doc: threadID is the thread the message is in, or null outside threads.

methods.name: timestamp
methods.doc:
timestamp is when the message was sent, in unix seconds.

Deprecated: use message.sentAt() instead, which is in unix ms.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use message.sentAt() instead, which is in unix ms.

methods.name: typing
methods.doc:
typing shows typing in the message's channel.

Deprecated: use message.target().typing() instead.

methods.name: unpin
methods.doc: unpin unpins the message.

methods.name: unreact
methods.doc: unreact removes the bot's reaction emoji.

methods.name: user
methods.doc: user is the author's username.

methods.name: verify
methods.doc:
verify reports whether the message's rotur signature is valid for its
author. Unsigned messages, signatures more than 5 minutes off the message
time and unknown keys are false. Fails only when the author's key can't
be fetched (NetworkError and the like).

methods.name: verifyEmbeds
methods.doc:
verifyEmbeds reports whether the message has embeds and every one carries
a valid author signature. Fails like verify.

methods.name: webhook
methods.doc: webhook is the webhook that posted the message, or null.

methods.name: arg
methods.doc: arg is the argument called name, or null when it wasn't given.

methods.name: argBool
methods.doc:
argBool is the argument called name as a boolean, false when it wasn't
given (see has).

methods.name: argNum
methods.doc:
argNum is the argument called name as a number, 0 when it wasn't given
(see has).

methods.name: argStr
methods.doc: argStr is the argument called name as text, "" when it wasn't given (see has).

methods.name: args
methods.doc: args is an object of every argument given, by input name.

methods.name: channel
methods.doc: channel is the channel name the command was called in.

methods.name: client
methods.doc: client is the client the command was called on.

methods.name: command
methods.doc: command is the command name, without "/".

methods.name: has
methods.doc: has reports whether the argument called name was given.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: id is the call id.

methods.name: invoker
methods.doc: invoker is the caller's user id.

methods.name: isEphemeral
methods.doc: isEphemeral reports whether only the caller sees the response.

methods.name: isSigned
methods.doc: isSigned reports whether the call carries the caller's rotur signature.

methods.name: raw
methods.doc: raw is the whole slash_call packet.

methods.name: respond
methods.doc:
respond answers the call with text (signed when the client is signing).
Fails with StateError when the client isn't connected.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
send posts content in the command's channel.

Deprecated: use call.target().send(content) instead.

methods.name: sendEmbed
methods.doc:
sendEmbed posts content with an embed in the command's channel.

Deprecated: use call.target().send(content, {embeds: [embed]}) instead.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: target is a handle for the channel or thread the command was called in.

methods.name: threadID
methods.doc: threadID is the thread the command was called in, or null.

methods.name: user
methods.doc: user is the caller's username (the id when the server sent no username).

methods.name: verify
methods.doc:
verify reports whether the call's rotur signature is valid for the
caller. Unsigned calls and unknown keys are false. Fails only when the
caller's key can't be fetched.

methods.name: addBoolean
methods.doc:
addBoolean adds a true/false input; it mutates the command and returns
it. Options as for addString.

methods.name: addChoice
methods.doc:
addChoice adds an enum input in place: addChoice(name, choices, description?, required?).

Deprecated: use slashCommand.addChoices(name, choices, {description, required}) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use slashCommand.addChoices(name, choices, {description, required}) instead.

methods.name: addChoices
methods.signature: slashCommand.addChoices(name: string, choices: array, options?: object) -> *originchats.SlashCommand
methods.doc:
addChoices adds an input limited to choices (strings); it mutates the
command and returns it. Options as for addString.

methods.name: addInput
methods.doc:
addInput adds an input of kind ("str", "int", "float", "bool", "user" or
"enum") in place: addInput(kind, name, description?, required?).

Deprecated: use slashCommand.addString, addInteger, addNumber, addBoolean or addUser instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use slashCommand.addString, addInteger, addNumber, addBoolean or addUser instead.

methods.name: addInteger
methods.doc:
addInteger adds a whole-number input; it mutates the command and returns
it. Options as for addString.

methods.name: addNumber
methods.doc:
addNumber adds a number input; it mutates the command and returns it.
Options as for addString.

methods.name: addOption
methods.doc:
addOption adds a raw option object in the server's format; it mutates
the command and returns it.

methods.name: addString
methods.doc:
addString adds a text input called name; it mutates the command and
returns it. Options: description (string, default name), required
(boolean, default true).

methods.name: addUser
methods.doc:
addUser adds a user input; it mutates the command and returns it.
Options as for addString.

methods.name: blacklistRoles
methods.doc:
blacklistRoles stops members with one of roles using the command; it
mutates the command and returns it.

methods.name: description
methods.doc:
description sets the command's description; it mutates the command and
returns it.

methods.name: ephemeral
methods.doc:
ephemeral makes responses visible only to the caller (on true); it
mutates the command and returns it.

methods.name: fn
methods.doc: fn registers the command with handler(call); see client.slash.

methods.name: whitelistRoles
methods.doc:
whitelistRoles lets only members with one of roles use the command; it
mutates the command and returns it.

methods.name: addField
methods.signature: embed.addField(name: string, value: string, options?: object) -> *originchats.Embed
methods.doc:
addField adds a name/value field; it mutates the embed and returns it.
Options: inline (boolean, show next to other inline fields).

methods.name: asPoll
methods.signature: embed.asPoll(question: string, choices: array, options?: object) -> *originchats.Embed
methods.doc:
asPoll turns the embed into a poll asking question; it mutates the embed
and returns it. choices are strings or {text, emoji} objects. Options:
multiselect (boolean).

methods.name: audio
methods.doc: audio sets audio from link; it mutates the embed and returns it.

methods.name: author
methods.doc:
author sets the author line in place: author(name, url?, iconURL?).

Deprecated: use embed.withAuthor(name, {url, iconURL}) instead.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: build returns the embed as the object the server receives.

methods.name: color
methods.doc:
color sets the accent color value: "#rrggbb", {r, g, b} or a 0xRRGGBB
number; it mutates the embed and returns it. Throws ValueError for a
malformed color.

methods.name: description
methods.doc: description sets the description; it mutates the embed and returns it.

methods.name: field
methods.doc:
field adds a field in place: field(name, value, inline?).

Deprecated: use embed.addField(name, value, {inline}) instead.

methods.name: footer
methods.doc:
footer sets the footer in place: footer(text, iconURL?).

Deprecated: use embed.withFooter(text, {iconURL}) instead.

methods.name: image
methods.doc: image sets a large image from link; it mutates the embed and returns it.

methods.name: markdown
methods.doc:
markdown turns markdown rendering on (true) or off; it mutates the embed
and returns it.

methods.name: poll
methods.doc:
poll turns the embed into a poll in place: poll(question, options, multiselect?).

Deprecated: use embed.asPoll(question, choices, {multiselect}) instead.

methods.name: thumbnail
methods.doc:
thumbnail sets a small image from link; it mutates the embed and returns
it.

methods.name: timestamp
methods.doc:
timestamp shows value, an ISO 8601 time; it mutates the embed and
returns it.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: title sets the title; it mutates the embed and returns it.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: url makes the title link to link; it mutates the embed and returns it.

methods.name: video
methods.doc: video sets a video from link; it mutates the embed and returns it.

methods.name: withAuthor
methods.doc:
withAuthor sets the author line; it mutates the embed and returns it.
Options: url (string), iconURL (string).

methods.name: withFooter
methods.doc:
withFooter sets the footer line; it mutates the embed and returns it.
Options: iconURL (string).

packages.name: pdf
packages.description: Creates PDF documents with text, shapes, images, tables, bookmarks and watermarks, and merges and splits PDFs it wrote.

functions.name: create
functions.doc:
create returns an empty US Letter document.

Deprecated: use pdf.new() instead, which returns a *pdf.Document.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pdf.new() instead, which returns a *pdf.Document.

functions.name: createCustom
functions.doc:
createCustom returns an empty document width x height points, or US
Letter when the size is invalid.

Deprecated: use pdf.new({width: width, height: height}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pdf.new({width: width, height: height}) instead.

functions.name: decode
functions.doc:
decode reads a PDF this package wrote back into a document, so it can be
inspected, added to and saved again. Text written to it flows onto a new
page; bookmarks are not kept. Fails with ParseError when data isn't a PDF
and UnsupportedError for a PDF written by other software.

functions.name: decodeFile
functions.doc:
decodeFile reads the PDF at path like pdf.decode. Fails with
NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be read.

functions.name: getInfo
functions.doc:
getInfo returns the name, size, dates and extension of the file at path,
or {} when it doesn't exist.

Deprecated: use fs.stat(path) for file details, or pdf.decodeFile(path) to read the PDF.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.stat(path) for file details, or pdf.decodeFile(path) to read the PDF.

functions.name: merge
functions.doc:
merge builds a document from the pages of PDF files this package wrote,
skipping files it can't read.

Deprecated: use pdf.mergeFiles(paths) instead, which fails for a file it
can't read.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pdf.mergeFiles(paths) instead, which fails for a file it can't read.

functions.name: mergeFiles
functions.doc:
mergeFiles returns a new document with the pages of each PDF at paths in
order, keeping each page's size. The files must have been written by this
package. Fails, naming the file, with the errors of pdf.decodeFile. Throws
ValueError when paths is empty.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new returns an empty document with one blank page. Options: pageSize
("letter", the default, "legal", "tabloid", "a3", "a4" or "a5", in any
case); landscape (boolean) turns the page sideways; width and height
(points, both or neither, up to 14400) set a custom page size instead of
pageSize; margin (points, default 72, or a quarter of the shorter side on
smaller pages) and fontSize (points, default 12);
title, author and subject (strings) for the document's properties.
Throws ValueError for an unknown page size or an invalid number.

functions.name: split
functions.doc:
split writes each page of a PDF this package wrote to outputDir/page_N.pdf,
returning false on failure.

Deprecated: use pdf.splitFile(path, dir) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use pdf.splitFile(path, dir) instead.

functions.name: splitFile
functions.signature: pdf.splitFile(path: string, dir: string) -> result<string[], error>
functions.doc:
splitFile writes each page of the PDF at path, which must have been
written by this package, to its own file dir/page_N.pdf (N from 1),
creating dir if needed, and returns the paths written. Fails with the
errors of pdf.decodeFile, or with PermissionError or IOError when a file
can't be written.

methods.name: addBookmark
methods.signature: document.addBookmark(title: string, page: int, options?: object)
methods.doc:
addBookmark adds an entry titled title to the viewer's bookmarks panel
that opens page (1-based). Options: level (whole number, default 0) nests
it: 0 is top level and level n goes under the closest earlier entry of
level n-1 (a deeper jump is treated as one level). Throws ValueError for
a page that doesn't exist or a negative level.

methods.name: addPage
methods.doc:
addPage finishes the current page and starts a new blank one the size of
the document's pages; flowing text continues at its top margin.

methods.name: author
methods.doc: author returns the document's author property, or "" when it has none.

methods.name: circle
methods.signature: document.circle(center: object, radius: number, options?: object)
methods.doc:
circle draws a circle around center, {x, y} in points from the top-left
corner ({x: 1, y: 1}), with radius in points. Options: fill, stroke and lineWidth as for
rectangle. Throws ValueError for a malformed center, a negative radius or
an invalid option.

methods.name: drawImage
methods.doc:
drawImage draws an img.Image from std:img stretched to fill rect, {x,
y, width, height} in points with x and y its top-left corner, so
anything drawn or filtered with img can go in the document as it is,
without encoding it first. Translucent pixels are blended onto white, the
page's color. Later changes to the image don't change the document.
Throws ValueError for a malformed rectangle, TypeError for null and
StateError when the image is closed.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
encode returns the document as PDF file bytes; the document is unchanged
and can still be added to.

methods.name: fontSize
methods.doc: fontSize returns the font size in points for text written from now on.

methods.name: image
methods.signature: document.image(data: byte[], rect: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
image draws PNG, JPEG or GIF image bytes stretched to fill rect, {x, y,
width, height} in points with x and y its top-left corner, {x: 1, y: 1}
for the page's. Transparent
pixels are drawn without their transparency. Fails with ParseError when
data isn't an image it can decode. Throws ValueError for a malformed
rectangle.

methods.name: imageFile
methods.signature: document.imageFile(path: string, rect: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
imageFile draws the image file at path like image. Fails with
NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be read
and ParseError when it isn't an image.

methods.name: line
methods.signature: document.line(from: object, to: object, options?: object)
methods.doc:
line draws a straight line between the points from and to, each {x, y} in
points from the top-left corner, which is {x: 1, y: 1}. Options: color (an OSL colour, default
black) and lineWidth (points, default 1). Throws ValueError for a
malformed point or option.

methods.name: margin
methods.doc: margin returns the page margin in points.

methods.name: newLine
methods.doc: newLine moves the flowing text down one line, leaving a blank line.

methods.name: pageCount
methods.doc:
pageCount returns the number of pages, the current one included; a new
document has 1.

methods.name: pageSize
methods.doc:
pageSize returns the size in points of the current page, which new pages
share, as {width, height}.

methods.name: pageText
methods.doc:
pageText returns the text written to page (1-based), one line per text
line, each ending in a newline. Throws ValueError for a page that doesn't
exist.

methods.name: rectangle
methods.doc:
rectangle draws the rectangle rect, {x, y, width, height} in points with
x and y its top-left corner ({x: 1, y: 1} starts at the page's). Options: fill and stroke (OSL colours)
fill it and outline it; without either it is outlined in black;
lineWidth (points, default 1). Throws ValueError for a malformed
rectangle, a negative size or an invalid option.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
save writes the document to path as a PDF file; the document is
unchanged and can still be added to. Fails with NotFoundError,
PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be written.

methods.name: setAuthor
methods.doc: setAuthor sets the document's author property; "" removes it.

methods.name: setFontSize
setMargin
methods.doc:
setMargin sets the margin in points that flowing text, wrapping and
tables keep from the page edges, from the next page (or this one, if
nothing is on it yet). Throws ValueError for a negative margin or one
that leaves no room on the page.

methods.name: setSubject
methods.doc: setSubject sets the document's subject property; "" removes it.

methods.name: setTitle

(fail with RuntimeError on a non-zero exit). Fails with NotFoundError
when the command doesn't exist, PermissionError when it can't be run and
TimeoutError when the timeout passes (the process is killed).

packages.name: ptr
packages.description: Shared mutable cells and low-level identity, address and memory-layout queries.
packages.about:
ptr.new(value) makes a shared mutable cell, so a function can update a
value its caller owns: p.value() reads it and p.set(v) replaces it.
@variable points at an existing variable instead; ptr.deref(p) and
ptr.set(p, v) read and write through either kind. == compares what two
pointers hold and === whether they are the same. Address and layout
queries are for debugging and interop; addresses are not stable across
runs.

functions.name: addressOf
functions.doc:
addressOf returns the address of value as a number: for an object, array,
function or handle, the address of the data it refers to, which every
reference to it shares; for null, 0; for other values, the address of a
temporary copy.

functions.name: alignOf
functions.doc:
alignOf returns the alignment in bytes of value's Go representation.
Throws ValueError for null.

functions.name: deref
functions.doc:

what a ptr.new Pointer holds. Throws ValueError for a null pointer and
TypeError for a value that isn't a pointer.

functions.name: equalPointers
functions.doc:
equalPointers reports whether a and b are the same object, array, function
or handle rather than equal copies. Two nulls are the same.

functions.name: isNull
functions.doc: isNull reports whether value is null or a null Go pointer.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new returns a Pointer holding value. Copies of the Pointer share the cell,
so p.set(v) is seen by every holder.

functions.name: offsetOf
functions.doc:
offsetOf returns the byte offset of the Go field named field
within a Go struct value, such as a package handle. Throws ValueError when
value isn't a struct or has no such field; OSL objects are maps, not
structs.

functions.name: set
functions.doc:
set stores value where pointer points, in place: in the variable behind
@value, or in a ptr.new Pointer. Returns true. Throws ValueError for a
null pointer and TypeError for a value that isn't a pointer or a value
the variable's type can't hold.

array or object, the size of one element. Throws ValueError for null.
