packages.name: qr
packages.description: Makes QR codes and Code 128, EAN-13, UPC-A and Code 39 barcodes as images, and reads them back.
packages.about:
A code is an image from std:img, so whatever takes an image takes one:

  *img.Image code = qr.code("https://rotur.dev/link?code=AB12")!
  <image src=${code}/>          shown in a std:ui view
  code.save("code.png")!        written as a file, as any image is

qr.barcode makes the four kinds of barcode, qr.read reads either kind back
from an image, and qr.modules gives a code's grid for drawing it some
other way.

functions.name: barcode
functions.signature: qr.barcode(text: string, options?: object) -> result<*img.Image, error>
functions.doc:
barcode makes text into a barcode image. Options: kind ("code128", the
default, "ean13", "upca" or "code39"), height (in pixels, default 120),
and color and background (default black on white). EAN-13 takes 12 or 13
digits and UPC-A 11 or 12, computing or checking the last (qr.read gives
an EAN-13 that starts with 0 back as its UPC-A, without the 0); Code 39 takes
upper-case letters, digits and - . $ / + % and space. Fails with
ValueError when the text can't be written as that kind.

functions.name: checkDigit
functions.doc:
checkDigit gives the check digit an EAN-13 or UPC-A barcode ends with for
digits, the code without it. Fails with ValueError when digits is empty or
has anything but 0-9.

functions.name: code
functions.signature: qr.code(text: string, options?: object) -> result<*img.Image, error>
functions.doc:
code makes text into a QR code image. Options: size (the image's width
and height in pixels, default 256; it grows to fit a module per pixel),
margin (the blank border, in modules, default 4), color and background
(default black on white), and level ("L", "M", "Q" or "H": how much of the
code may be damaged and still read; default M, or L when the text only
fits there). Fails with ValueError when the text is too long for a QR code.

functions.name: modules
functions.signature: qr.modules(text: string, options?: object) -> result<boolean[][], error>
functions.doc:
modules gives text's code as a grid, true for dark, without its quiet
zone, for drawing it some other way: the rows of a QR code, or one row of
a barcode's bars. Options: kind ("qr", the default, or a barcode kind as
qr.barcode takes) and level (QR only, as qr.code takes). Fails with
ValueError when the text can't be encoded as that kind.

functions.name: read
functions.doc:
read gives the text of the QR code or barcode in picture: a code qr.code
or qr.barcode made, or one in a photo or screenshot, at any angle. It reads
QR codes, Code 128, Code 39, Code 93, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, ITF and
Codabar; a UPC-A barcode reads as its 12 digits, so an EAN-13 that starts
with 0 reads as the UPC-A it is, without that 0. Fails with NotFoundError
when the image holds no code it can read, and StateError when it is
closed.

packages.name: random
packages.description: Fast seedable pseudo-random numbers, items, shuffles and strings; use crypto for secrets.

functions.name: bool
functions.doc:
bool returns true or false with equal odds, or true with the given
probability from 0 to 1, as in random.bool(0.25). Throws ValueError for a
probability outside 0 to 1.

functions.name: gaussian
functions.doc:
gaussian returns a normally distributed number: gaussian() has mean 0
and standard deviation 1, and gaussian(mean, stdDev) uses the given ones.
Throws ValueError for a negative stdDev.

functions.name: int
functions.doc:
int returns a whole number from min to max, including both ends, so
random.int(1, 6) rolls a die. The bounds may come in either order.

functions.name: item
functions.doc:
item returns a random item of items, typed as the array's items are, or
null (the item type's zero value for a typed array) when items is empty.

functions.name: number
functions.doc:
number returns a random number. number() is from 0 up to but not
including 1, as JavaScript's Math.random() is, number(max) from 0 up to
max, and number(min, max) from min up to max.

functions.name: sample
functions.doc:
sample returns count different items of items in random order, typed as
items is, or all of them shuffled when count is larger than items.
Throws ValueError for a negative count.

functions.name: seed
functions.doc:
seed restarts the generator from seed, so the same seed always produces
the same sequence of results from every random function.

functions.name: shuffle
functions.doc:
shuffle returns a shuffled copy of items, typed as items is, and leaves
items unchanged.

functions.name: string
functions.doc:
string returns random characters: string() gives 16 letters and digits,
string(length) gives length of them, and string(length, alphabet) draws
from the characters of alphabet instead. Throws ValueError for a negative
length, one over 16777216, or an empty alphabet, and TypeError for other
argument types.

packages.name: raygui
packages.description: Immediate-mode GUI controls for raylib windows: buttons, toggles, sliders, text fields, lists, dropdowns, color pickers, dialogs and styles

functions.name: button
functions.doc: button draws a button and returns true when it was clicked this frame.

functions.name: buttonGroup
functions.signature: raygui.buttonGroup(bounds: any, items: any, selected: int) -> int
functions.doc:
buttonGroup draws a row of toggle buttons, one per item, and returns the
1-based selected item after this frame's input. Throws ValueError when
selected is out of range.

functions.name: checkBox
functions.signature: raygui.checkBox(bounds: any, text: string, checked: boolean) -> boolean
functions.doc:
checkBox draws a check box and returns whether it is checked after this
frame's input.

functions.name: colorBarAlpha
functions.signature: raygui.colorBarAlpha(bounds: any, text: string, alpha: number) -> number
functions.doc:
colorBarAlpha draws an alpha bar and returns the alpha, 0 to 1, after
this frame's input.

functions.name: colorBarHue
functions.signature: raygui.colorBarHue(bounds: any, text: string, hue: number) -> number
functions.doc:
colorBarHue draws a hue bar and returns the hue, 0 to 360, after this
frame's input.

functions.name: colorPanel
functions.signature: raygui.colorPanel(bounds: any, text: string, color: any) -> {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.returns: {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.doc:
colorPanel draws a saturation/value color square and returns the color
{r, g, b, a} after this frame's input.

functions.name: colorPicker
functions.signature: raygui.colorPicker(bounds: any, text: string, color: any) -> {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.returns: {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.doc:
colorPicker draws a color picker and returns the color {r, g, b, a} after
this frame's input.

functions.name: cycleButton
functions.signature: raygui.cycleButton(bounds: any, items: any, selected: int) -> int
functions.doc:
cycleButton draws a button that steps through items when clicked and
returns the 1-based selected item after this frame's input. Throws
ValueError when selected is out of range.

functions.name: disable
functions.doc: disable greys out controls drawn afterwards and makes them ignore input.

functions.name: disableTooltip
functions.doc: disableTooltip stops showing tooltips.

functions.name: dropdown
functions.signature: raygui.dropdown(bounds: any, items: any, state: object) -> {open: boolean, selected: int}
functions.doc:
dropdown draws a dropdown list of items. state is {selected, open} (the
1-based selected item, default 1, and whether the list is open, default
false); pass the returned state back in next frame. Draw open dropdowns
last so their list covers other controls. Throws ValueError when selected
is out of range.

functions.name: enable
functions.doc: enable makes controls respond to input again after disable.

functions.name: enableTooltip
functions.doc:
enableTooltip shows the text set with setTooltip when the mouse rests on
controls drawn afterwards.

functions.name: getStyle
functions.doc:
getStyle returns a style property, treating unknown names as the default
control's first property.

Deprecated: use raygui.style(control, property) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raygui.style(control, property) instead.

functions.name: gridCell
functions.signature: raygui.gridCell(bounds: any, spacing: number, options?: object) -> {column: int, row: int}?
functions.doc:
gridCell draws a grid of lines spacing apart and returns the 1-based
{column, row} under the mouse, or null when the mouse is outside it.
Options: subdivisions (lines between main lines, default 2) and text.

functions.name: groupBox
functions.doc: groupBox draws a titled frame around a group of controls.

functions.name: icon
functions.signature: raygui.icon(id: int, position: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
icon draws one of raygui's icons (by number) with its top-left corner at a
point {x, y}. Options: scale (pixels per icon pixel, default 1) and color
(default "#000000"). Throws StateError when no window is open.

functions.name: iconText
functions.doc:
iconText returns text prefixed with one of raygui's icons (by number), for
use as a control's label.

functions.name: inputDialog
functions.signature: raygui.inputDialog(bounds: any, state: object, options?: object) -> {button: int?, text: string}
functions.doc:
inputDialog draws a dialog with a text field. state is {text} (the
returned {text, button} works too); it returns {text, button}, where
button is the 1-based button clicked this frame, 0 for the close button,
or null. Options: title, message, buttons (default ["OK"]), maxLength
(default 256) and secret (hide the text, default false).

functions.name: isLocked
functions.doc: isLocked reports whether controls are locked.

functions.name: label
functions.doc: label draws text.

functions.name: labelButton
functions.doc:
labelButton draws text that acts as a button and returns true when it was
clicked this frame.

functions.name: line
functions.doc: line draws a separator line with optional text.

functions.name: list
functions.signature: raygui.list(bounds: any, items: any, state: object) -> {scroll: int, selected: int?}
functions.doc:
list draws a scrollable list of items. state is {selected, scroll} (the
1-based selected item or null for none, and the 1-based first visible
item, default 1); pass the returned state back in next frame. Throws
ValueError when selected or scroll is out of range.

functions.name: loadStyle
functions.doc:
loadStyle loads a raygui style file (.rgs). Fails with StateError when no
window is open and NotFoundError or IOError when the file can't be read.

functions.name: loadStyleDefault
functions.doc:
loadStyleDefault restores raygui's default style. Throws StateError when
no window is open.

functions.name: lock
functions.doc: lock makes controls ignore input while still drawing normally.

functions.name: locked
functions.doc:
locked reports whether controls are locked.

Deprecated: use raygui.isLocked() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raygui.isLocked() instead.

functions.name: messageDialog
functions.signature: raygui.messageDialog(bounds: any, message: string, options?: object) -> int?
functions.doc:
messageDialog draws a message box and returns the 1-based button clicked
this frame, 0 for its close button, or null when nothing was clicked.
Options: title and buttons (an array of labels, default ["OK"]).

functions.name: panel
functions.doc: panel draws a background panel with an optional title.

functions.name: progress
functions.signature: raygui.progress(bounds: any, value: number, options?: object)
functions.doc:
progress draws a progress bar filled up to value. Takes valueSlider's
options.

functions.name: scrollSlider
functions.signature: raygui.scrollSlider(bounds: any, value: int, options?: object) -> int
functions.doc:
scrollSlider draws a scroll bar and returns its value after this frame's
input. Options: min (default 0) and max (default 100).

functions.name: scrollView
functions.signature: raygui.scrollView(bounds: any, content: any, options?: object) -> {scroll: {x: number, y: number}, view: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}}
functions.returns: {scroll: {x: number, y: number}, view: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}}
functions.doc:
scrollView draws a scrollable panel over content {x, y, width, height}
and returns {scroll, view}: the scroll offset {x, y} to pass back in next
frame and draw the content shifted by, and the visible area {x, y, width,
height}, x, y its top-left corner as for bounds. Options: title and
scroll (default {x: 0, y: 0}, a distance rather than a position).

functions.name: setAlpha
functions.doc:
setAlpha sets the opacity controls are drawn with, from 0 to 1. Throws
ValueError outside that range.

functions.name: setIconScale
functions.doc: setIconScale sets how many pixels each icon pixel takes in controls.

functions.name: setState
functions.doc:
setState sets the state controls are drawn in: "normal", "focused",
"pressed" or "disabled" (older scripts passed 0 to 3). Throws ValueError
for anything else.

functions.name: setStyle
functions.signature: raygui.setStyle(control: any, property: any, value: any)
functions.doc:
setStyle sets one style property of a control: control is a name such as
"default" (all controls), "button", "textbox" or "listview", property a
name such as "text_size", "border_width" or "base_color_normal", and value
a number or, for color properties, a color. Throws ValueError for unknown
names and StateError when no window is open.

functions.name: setTooltip
functions.doc: setTooltip sets the tooltip for controls drawn afterwards.

functions.name: spinBox
functions.signature: raygui.spinBox(bounds: any, state: object, options?: object) -> {editing: boolean, value: int}
functions.doc:
spinBox draws a whole-number field with - and + buttons. state is
{value, editing}; pass the returned state back in next frame. Options: min
(default 0), max (default 100) and text (a label beside it).

functions.name: state
functions.doc:
state returns the state controls are drawn in: "normal", "focused",
"pressed" or "disabled".

functions.name: statusBar
functions.doc: statusBar draws a status bar with text.

functions.name: style
functions.doc:
style returns a control's style property as a number, naming them as
setStyle does. Throws ValueError for unknown names and StateError when no
window is open.

functions.name: styleColor
functions.signature: raygui.styleColor(control: any, property: any) -> {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.returns: {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.doc:
styleColor returns a control's color style property as {r, g, b, a}.
Throws ValueError for unknown names and StateError when no window is open.

functions.name: tabs
functions.signature: raygui.tabs(bounds: any, items: any, selected: int) -> {closed: int?, selected: int}
functions.doc:
tabs draws a tab bar of items and returns {selected, closed}: the 1-based
selected tab after this frame's input, and the tab whose close button was
clicked (null for none). Throws ValueError when selected is out of range.

functions.name: textField
functions.signature: raygui.textField(bounds: any, state: object, options?: object) -> {editing: boolean, text: string}
functions.doc:
textField draws a single-line text field. state is {text, editing} (the
text, and whether it has keyboard focus; clicking it starts editing and
Enter or clicking elsewhere stops); pass the returned state back in next
frame. Options: maxLength (characters, default 256).

functions.name: textWidth
functions.doc:
textWidth returns how wide text is in the current style, in pixels.
Throws StateError when no window is open.

functions.name: toggle
functions.signature: raygui.toggle(bounds: any, text: string, active: boolean) -> boolean
functions.doc:
toggle draws a toggle button and returns whether it is on after this
frame's input; pass the result back in next frame.

functions.name: toggleSwitch
functions.signature: raygui.toggleSwitch(bounds: any, items: any, selected: int) -> int
functions.doc:
toggleSwitch draws a sliding switch between items and returns the 1-based
selected item after this frame's input. Throws ValueError when selected is
out of range.

functions.name: unlock
functions.doc: unlock makes controls respond to input again after lock.

functions.name: valueBar
functions.signature: raygui.valueBar(bounds: any, value: number, options?: object) -> number
functions.doc:
valueBar draws a slider that fills up to its value and returns the value
after this frame's input. Takes valueSlider's options.

functions.name: valueField
functions.signature: raygui.valueField(bounds: any, state: object, options?: object) -> {editing: boolean, value: int}
functions.doc:
valueField draws a whole-number field to type into. state is {value,
editing}; pass the returned state back in next frame. Options: min
(default 0), max (default 100) and text (a label beside it).

functions.name: valueSlider
functions.signature: raygui.valueSlider(bounds: any, value: number, options?: object) -> number
functions.doc:
valueSlider draws a slider with a handle and returns its value after this
frame's input. Options: min (default 0), max (default 1), textLeft and
textRight (labels on either side).

functions.name: windowBox
functions.doc:
windowBox draws a window panel with a title bar and returns true when its
close button was clicked.

packages.name: raylib
packages.description: raylib windows with 2D and 3D drawing, keyboard and mouse input, textures, images, shaders and render textures, exchanging pixels with img.Image
packages.about:
raylib draws through SDL2, which a program links from the system. Building
one needs SDL2's development files and pkg-config, and running it needs
SDL2 where it runs: the libSDL2 package on Linux, Homebrew's sdl2 on
macOS, and SDL2.dll beside the program or on PATH on Windows.

functions.name: begin3D
functions.doc:
begin3D starts drawing through a 3D camera.

Deprecated: use camera.use(draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use camera.use(draw) instead.

functions.name: beginBlend
functions.doc:
beginBlend switches the blend mode; unknown modes mean "alpha".

Deprecated: use raylib.blend(mode, draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.blend(mode, draw) instead.

functions.name: beginDrawing
functions.doc:
beginDrawing starts a frame.

Deprecated: use raylib.draw(frame) instead, which ends the frame even when frame throws.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.draw(frame) instead, which ends the frame even when frame throws.

functions.name: beginShader
functions.doc:
beginShader starts drawing through a shader and returns false for an
invalid one.

Deprecated: use shader.use(draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use shader.use(draw) instead.

functions.name: blend
functions.doc:
blend runs draw with a blend mode: "alpha" (normal), "additive",
"multiply", "premultiplied", or "layer" (alpha blending that keeps a
transparent render texture premultiplied, for compositing it later with
"premultiplied"). Throws ValueError for an unknown mode.

functions.name: camera
functions.doc:
camera builds a 3D camera. Options: position and target ({x, y, z}, the
camera's place and what it looks at; default the origin), up (default
{x: 0, y: 1, z: 0}), fovy (vertical field of view in degrees, or the view
height for an orthographic camera; default 60) and projection
("perspective", the default, or "orthographic").

functions.name: camera2D
functions.doc:
camera2D builds a 2D camera. Options: target (the world point {x, y} the
camera looks at; default {x: 1, y: 1}), offset (where on screen that
point appears, {x, y}; default {x: 1, y: 1}, the top-left pixel),
rotation (degrees, default 0) and zoom (default 1). World points count
from 1 like window positions, so the default camera draws everything
where it would be drawn without one.

functions.name: centerRay
functions.doc:
centerRay returns the ray from a camera through the middle of the screen.

Deprecated: use camera.centerRay() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use camera.centerRay() instead.

functions.name: circle
functions.signature: raylib.circle(center: any, radius: number, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
circle draws a circle around a center {x, y}, filled unless lineWidth is
given. Options: lineWidth (draw only the outline, this thick).

functions.name: circlesCollide
functions.signature: raylib.circlesCollide(first: any, firstRadius: any, second: any, secondRadius: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
circlesCollide reports whether two circles overlap.

Deprecated: use raylib.isCircleOverlapping({x, y, radius}, {x, y, radius}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isCircleOverlapping({x, y, radius}, {x, y, radius}) instead.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: clear fills the whole drawing target with a color.

functions.name: closeWindow
functions.doc:
closeWindow closes the window and its graphics context. Closing when no
window is open does nothing.

functions.name: color
functions.signature: raylib.color(value: any) -> {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.returns: {a: int, b: int, g: int, r: int}
functions.doc:
color reads a color and returns it as {r, g, b, a}. It accepts "#rrggbb",
"#rrggbbaa", "#rgb", "#rgba", raylib's color names ("black", "white",
"red", "green", "blue", "yellow", "orange", "purple", "pink", "gray",
"transparent", "raywhite") and {r, g, b, a}; every raylib function that
takes a color accepts the same. Throws ValueError for anything else.

functions.name: compileShader
functions.signature: raylib.compileShader(code: string, options?: object) -> result<*raylib.Shader, error>
functions.doc:
compileShader compiles a fragment shader for drawing. code is GLSL 330 or
OSL-style shader code (see shader.transpile). Options: vertex (vertex
shader code; default raylib's). Fails with StateError when no window is
open and ParseError when the GPU driver rejects the code (raylib logs the
driver's message).

functions.name: compileShaderFile
functions.signature: raylib.compileShaderFile(path: string, options?: object) -> result<*raylib.Shader, error>
functions.doc:
compileShaderFile compiles a fragment shader from a file, like
compileShader. Options: vertex (a vertex shader file; default raylib's).
Fails with StateError when no window is open, NotFoundError or IOError
when a file can't be read, and ParseError when the code doesn't compile.

functions.name: cube
functions.signature: raylib.cube(center: any, size: any, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
cube draws a box around a center {x, y, z} with a size {x, y, z}.
Options: wireframe (draw only the edges).

functions.name: cursorHidden
functions.doc:
cursorHidden reports whether the mouse cursor is hidden.

Deprecated: use raylib.isCursorHidden() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isCursorHidden() instead.

functions.name: cylinder
functions.signature: raylib.cylinder(from: any, to: any, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
cylinder draws a cylinder or cone from one point {x, y, z} to another.
Options: radius (default 1), topRadius (the radius at to; default radius,
0 makes a cone), slices (default 16) and wireframe.

functions.name: disableCursor
functions.doc: disableCursor hides and locks the mouse cursor, for mouse-look controls.

functions.name: dpiScale
functions.doc:
dpiScale returns framebuffer pixels per window unit (2 on most retina
screens). It is measured rather than taken from the platform, which some
backends report incorrectly.

functions.name: draw
functions.doc:
draw runs frame to draw one frame of the window and shows the result.
Everything drawn on screen happens inside it. Throws StateError when no
window is open.

functions.name: draw3D
functions.doc:
draw3D runs frame drawing through a 3D camera.

Deprecated: use camera.use(frame) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use camera.use(frame) instead.

functions.name: drawBillboard
functions.signature: raylib.drawBillboard(camera: *raylib.Camera, texture: *raylib.Texture, position: any, size: any, tint: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
drawBillboard draws a texture facing the camera and returns false for a
missing camera or invalid texture.

Deprecated: use texture.drawBillboard(camera, position, {size, tint}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use texture.drawBillboard(camera, position, {size, tint}) instead.

functions.name: drawCube
functions.signature: raylib.drawCube(center: any, size: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawCube draws a solid box.

Deprecated: use raylib.cube(center, size, color) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.cube(center, size, color) instead.

functions.name: drawCubeWires
functions.signature: raylib.drawCubeWires(center: any, size: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawCubeWires draws a box's edges.

Deprecated: use raylib.cube(center, size, color, {wireframe: true}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.cube(center, size, color, {wireframe: true}) instead.

functions.name: drawCylinder
functions.signature: raylib.drawCylinder(position: any, radiusTop: any, radiusBottom: any, height: any, slices: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawCylinder draws a cylinder standing on position.

Deprecated: use raylib.cylinder(from, to, color, {radius, topRadius, slices}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.cylinder(from, to, color, {radius, topRadius, slices}) instead.

functions.name: drawGrid
functions.doc:
drawGrid draws a ground grid.

Deprecated: use raylib.grid(slices, spacing) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.grid(slices, spacing) instead.

functions.name: drawLine3D
functions.signature: raylib.drawLine3D(start: any, end: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawLine3D draws a 3D line.

Deprecated: use raylib.line3D(from, to, color) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.line3D(from, to, color) instead.

functions.name: drawPlane
functions.signature: raylib.drawPlane(center: any, size: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawPlane draws a ground rectangle.

Deprecated: use raylib.plane(center, {x, z}, color) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.plane(center, {x, z}, color) instead.

functions.name: drawSphere
functions.signature: raylib.drawSphere(center: any, radius: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawSphere draws a solid sphere.

Deprecated: use raylib.sphere(center, radius, color) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.sphere(center, radius, color) instead.

functions.name: drawSphereWires
functions.signature: raylib.drawSphereWires(center: any, radius: any, rings: any, slices: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
drawSphereWires draws a sphere's wireframe.

Deprecated: use raylib.sphere(center, radius, color, {wireframe: true, rings, slices}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.sphere(center, radius, color, {wireframe: true, rings, slices}) instead.

functions.name: drawToTexture
functions.doc:
drawToTexture runs drawFunc drawing into a render texture and returns
false for an invalid one.

Deprecated: use renderTexture.use(draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use renderTexture.use(draw) instead.

functions.name: elapsed
functions.doc: elapsed returns the milliseconds since the window was opened.

functions.name: enableCursor
functions.doc: enableCursor shows and unlocks the mouse cursor.

functions.name: end3D
functions.doc:
end3D stops drawing through a 3D camera.

Deprecated: use camera.use(draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use camera.use(draw) instead.

functions.name: endBlend
functions.doc:
endBlend restores normal alpha blending.

Deprecated: use raylib.blend(mode, draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.blend(mode, draw) instead.

functions.name: endDrawing
functions.doc:
endDrawing ends a frame and shows it.

Deprecated: use raylib.draw(frame) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.draw(frame) instead.

functions.name: endShader
functions.doc:
endShader stops drawing through a shader.

Deprecated: use shader.use(draw) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use shader.use(draw) instead.

functions.name: fps
functions.doc: fps returns the frames drawn in the last second.

functions.name: frameDuration
functions.doc: frameDuration returns how long the last frame took, in milliseconds.

functions.name: frameTime
functions.doc:
frameTime returns how long the last frame took, in seconds.

Deprecated: use raylib.frameDuration() instead; it returns milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.frameDuration() instead; it returns milliseconds.

functions.name: gpuPreference
functions.doc: gpuPreference returns "integrated" or "discrete".

functions.name: grid
functions.doc:
grid draws a ground grid of slices by slices squares, spacing apart,
centred on the origin.

functions.name: initWindow
functions.signature: raylib.initWindow(width: int, height: int, title: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
initWindow opens the program's window, width by height window units, and
its graphics context; most other functions need it open. Options: fps
(frames per second to aim for) and the window flags highdpi, resizable,
vsync, msaa, transparent, undecorated, borderless, topmost, hidden and
alwaysRun (booleans, default false). A hidden window can show for a
moment as it opens, since SDL2 opens every window shown. Throws
ValueError for transparent, which SDL2's windows can't be. Fails with
StateError when a window is already open and RuntimeError when one can't
be opened.

functions.name: isCircleOverlapping
functions.doc: isCircleOverlapping reports whether two circles {x, y, radius} overlap.

functions.name: isCursorHidden
functions.doc: isCursorHidden reports whether the mouse cursor is hidden.

functions.name: isKeyDown
functions.doc:
isKeyDown reports whether key is held down. Keys are named as for
isKeyPressed.

functions.name: isKeyPressed
functions.doc:
isKeyPressed reports whether key went down this frame. Keys are names
("space", "escape", "enter", "tab", "backspace", "insert", "delete",
arrow keys "left"/"right"/"up"/"down", "pageup", "pagedown", "home",
"end", "shift", "ctrl", "alt" and their "left"/"right" forms, "f1" to
"f12") or single characters ("a", "1", "/"). Throws ValueError for an
unknown key.

functions.name: isKeyReleased
functions.doc:
isKeyReleased reports whether key came up this frame. Keys are named as
for isKeyPressed.

functions.name: isMouseDown
functions.doc:
isMouseDown reports whether a mouse button is held down. Buttons are
named as for isMousePressed.

functions.name: isMousePressed
functions.doc:
isMousePressed reports whether a mouse button ("left", "right",
"middle", "side" or "extra") went down this frame. Throws ValueError for
an unknown button.

functions.name: isMouseReleased
functions.doc:
isMouseReleased reports whether a mouse button came up this frame.
Buttons are named as for isMousePressed.

functions.name: isPointInCircle
functions.doc:
isPointInCircle reports whether a point {x, y} is inside a circle
{x, y, radius}.

functions.name: isPointInRect
functions.doc:
isPointInRect reports whether a point {x, y} is inside a rectangle
{x, y, width, height}.

functions.name: isRectOverlapping
functions.doc:
isRectOverlapping reports whether two rectangles {x, y, width, height}
overlap.

functions.name: isWindowReady
functions.doc: isWindowReady reports whether a window is open.

functions.name: keyDown
functions.doc:
keyDown reports whether a key, by name or key code, is held down.

Deprecated: use raylib.isKeyDown(key) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isKeyDown(key) instead.

functions.name: keyPressed
functions.doc:
keyPressed reports whether a key, by name or key code, went down this
frame.

Deprecated: use raylib.isKeyPressed(key) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isKeyPressed(key) instead.

functions.name: keyReleased
functions.doc:
keyReleased reports whether a key, by name or key code, came up this
frame.

Deprecated: use raylib.isKeyReleased(key) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isKeyReleased(key) instead.

functions.name: line
functions.signature: raylib.line(from: any, to: any, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
line draws a straight line between two points {x, y}. Options: thickness
(default 1).

functions.name: line3D
functions.signature: raylib.line3D(from: any, to: any, color: any)
functions.doc: line3D draws a line between two points {x, y, z}.

functions.name: loadFragmentShader
functions.doc:
loadFragmentShader loads a fragment shader from a file or code; check
valid() afterwards.

Deprecated: use raylib.compileShader(code) or raylib.compileShaderFile(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.compileShader(code) or raylib.compileShaderFile(path) instead.

functions.name: loadImage
functions.doc:
loadImage loads an image file (PNG, BMP, TGA, JPEG, GIF, QOI, HDR, PSD,
...) into memory; no window is needed. Fails with NotFoundError or IOError
when the file can't be read and ParseError when it isn't an image raylib
can decode.

functions.name: loadSVG
functions.signature: raylib.loadSVG(path: string, scale: number) -> result<*raylib.Image, error>
functions.doc:
loadSVG rasterises an SVG file at scale, rounding the size up and
stretching the drawing to fill it. Fails with NotFoundError or IOError
when the file can't be read, ParseError when it isn't an SVG with a size,
and ValueError when the image would be over 67 million pixels; throws
ValueError for a scale that isn't positive.

functions.name: loadSVGCanvas
functions.signature: raylib.loadSVGCanvas(path: string, scale: number) -> result<*raylib.Image, error>
functions.doc:
loadSVGCanvas rasterises an SVG the way a browser draws it onto a canvas
that is width * scale by height * scale (sizes truncated, as canvas
dimensions are), with the drawing at exactly that scale. Fails like
loadSVG.

functions.name: loadShader
functions.doc:
loadShader loads a vertex and fragment shader, each from a file when one
exists at that path and as code otherwise; check valid() afterwards.

Deprecated: use raylib.compileShader(code, {vertex}) or raylib.compileShaderFile(path, {vertex}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.compileShader(code, {vertex}) or raylib.compileShaderFile(path, {vertex}) instead.

functions.name: loadTexture
functions.doc:
loadTexture loads an image file (PNG, BMP, TGA, JPEG, GIF, QOI, HDR, PSD,
...) onto the GPU. Fails with StateError when no window is open,
NotFoundError or IOError when the file can't be read, and ParseError when
it isn't an image raylib can decode.

functions.name: measureText
functions.doc: measureText returns how wide text is at an em size, in window units.

functions.name: mouseDelta
functions.doc: mouseDelta returns how far the mouse moved {x, y} since the last frame.

functions.name: mouseDown
functions.doc:
mouseDown reports whether a mouse button is held down.

Deprecated: use raylib.isMouseDown(button) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isMouseDown(button) instead.

functions.name: mousePosition
functions.doc:
mousePosition returns the mouse position {x, y} in window units, 1, 1
over the top-left pixel, the way drawing calls take positions.

functions.name: mousePressed
functions.doc:
mousePressed reports whether a mouse button, by name or number, went down
this frame; unknown names mean the left button.

Deprecated: use raylib.isMousePressed(button) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isMousePressed(button) instead.

functions.name: mouseReleased
functions.doc:
mouseReleased reports whether a mouse button came up this frame.

Deprecated: use raylib.isMouseReleased(button) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isMouseReleased(button) instead.

functions.name: mouseWheel
functions.doc:
mouseWheel returns how far the mouse wheel turned this frame; positive is
away from the user.

functions.name: nextChar
functions.doc:
nextChar returns the next character typed since the last call, with
shift and the keyboard layout applied, or null when the queue is empty.

functions.name: nextKey
functions.doc:
nextKey returns the next key pressed since the last call, named as
isKeyPressed names keys, or null when the queue is empty. Keys without a
name are skipped.

functions.name: off
functions.doc:
off removes a handler added with on. Removing one that isn't registered
does nothing.

functions.name: on
functions.doc:
on adds handler for an event. "resize" runs while the window is being
resized by dragging its edge: on macOS the program's loop is paused until
the drag ends, so the handler is the only chance to redraw (fit the
content, then draw a frame) during it. Throws ValueError for an unknown
event.

functions.name: onResize
functions.doc:
onResize sets the one handler run while the window is being resized,
replacing any earlier one.

Deprecated: use raylib.on("resize", handler) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.on("resize", handler) instead.

functions.name: pixel
functions.doc:
pixel draws one pixel at a point {x, y}; {x: 1, y: 1} is the top-left
pixel.

functions.name: plane
functions.signature: raylib.plane(center: any, size: any, color: any)
functions.doc:
plane draws a flat rectangle on the ground (the x-z plane) around a center
{x, y, z}, size {x, z} across.

functions.name: pointInRectangle
functions.doc:
pointInRectangle reports whether a point is inside a rectangle.

Deprecated: use raylib.isPointInRect(point, rect) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isPointInRect(point, rect) instead.

functions.name: polygon
functions.signature: raylib.polygon(points: array, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
polygon draws a convex polygon through three or more points {x, y}, in
either winding order, filled unless lineWidth is given. Options:
lineWidth (draw only the outline, this thick).

functions.name: pressedChar
functions.doc:
pressedChar returns the next typed character, or "" when there is none.

Deprecated: use raylib.nextChar() instead; it returns null when there is none.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.nextChar() instead; it returns null when there is none.

functions.name: pressedKey
functions.doc:
pressedKey returns the next pressed key's name, or "" when there is none.

Deprecated: use raylib.nextKey() instead; it returns null when there is none.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.nextKey() instead; it returns null when there is none.

functions.name: ray
functions.doc: ray builds a ray from an origin {x, y, z} in a direction {x, y, z}.

functions.name: rect
functions.signature: raylib.rect(x: any, y: any, width: any, height: any) -> object
functions.doc:
rect builds a rectangle {x, y, width, height}.

Deprecated: write the object {x, y, width, height} instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: write the object {x, y, width, height} instead.

functions.name: rectangle
functions.signature: raylib.rectangle(rect: any, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
rectangle draws a rectangle {x, y, width, height}, x, y its top-left
corner, filled unless lineWidth is given. Options: lineWidth (draw only
the outline, this thick) and radius (round the corners by this many
units).

functions.name: rectanglesCollide
functions.doc:
rectanglesCollide reports whether two rectangles overlap.

Deprecated: use raylib.isRectOverlapping(a, b) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isRectOverlapping(a, b) instead.

functions.name: renderTexture
functions.signature: raylib.renderTexture(width: int, height: int) -> result<*raylib.RenderTexture, error>
functions.doc:
renderTexture makes an off-screen texture of width by height pixels to
draw into with use(), then draw on screen with drawAt() or pass to a
shader. Fails with StateError when no window is open and RuntimeError when
the GPU can't make one; throws ValueError for a size that isn't positive.

functions.name: run
functions.signature: raylib.run(options: object, update: any, draw: any)
functions.doc:
run opens a window from an options object and calls update(seconds) and
draw() once a frame until the window closes.

Deprecated: use raylib.runWindow(frame, options) instead; frame gets milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.runWindow(frame, options) instead; frame gets milliseconds.

functions.name: runWindow
functions.signature: raylib.runWindow(frame: any, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
runWindow opens a window, calls frame(ms) once a frame inside draw with
the previous frame's duration in milliseconds until the window is asked
to close, then closes it. Options: width (default 800), height (450),
title ("OSL raylib"), fps (60), background (a color to clear each frame
to), frames (stop after this many; 0, the default, runs until closed) and
the window flags of initWindow. When a window is already open it is used
and left open. Fails with RuntimeError when a window can't be opened.

functions.name: screenSize
functions.doc: screenSize returns the window's {width, height} in window units.

functions.name: screenshot
functions.doc:
screenshot returns what the window shows as a new img.Image from
std:img, at the framebuffer's full resolution on high-DPI screens and
fully opaque. Fails with StateError when no window is open.

functions.name: setConfigFlags
functions.doc:
setConfigFlags sets window flags for the next window from a "a|b" string,
an array of names, or a number; unknown names are ignored.

Deprecated: pass flags as initWindow options instead, such as {highdpi: true, resizable: true}.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: pass flags as initWindow options instead, such as {highdpi: true, resizable: true}.

functions.name: setGPUPreference
functions.doc:
setGPUPreference chooses the GPU for windows opened afterwards:
"integrated" (the default, lower power) or "discrete" ("dedicated" and
"high_performance" mean the same). It returns the preference now in
effect. Throws ValueError for anything else.

functions.name: setLogLevel
functions.doc:
setLogLevel sets which of raylib's own log messages are printed: "all",
"trace", "debug", "info" (raylib's default), "warning", "error", "fatal" or
"none". Throws ValueError for anything else.

functions.name: setMousePosition
functions.doc:
setMousePosition moves the mouse cursor to x, y in window units, 1, 1
being the top-left pixel as for mousePosition.

functions.name: setSVGFont
functions.doc:
setSVGFont registers the font file used for SVG text in a font family and
returns false when it can't be loaded.

Deprecated: use svg.addFont(family, path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use svg.addFont(family, path) instead.

functions.name: setTargetFPS
functions.doc: setTargetFPS caps the frame rate; 0 means no cap.

functions.name: setWindowSize
functions.doc:
setWindowSize resizes the window to width by height window units. Throws
StateError when no window is open.

functions.name: setWindowTitle
functions.doc:
setWindowTitle changes the window's title. Throws StateError when no
window is open.

functions.name: shader
functions.doc:
shader loads a fragment shader from a file or code; check valid()
afterwards.

Deprecated: use raylib.compileShader(code) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.compileShader(code) instead.

functions.name: smoothLine
functions.signature: raylib.smoothLine(from: any, to: any, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
smoothLine draws an antialiased line with round caps between two points
{x, y}; a zero-length line draws a round dot. Options: thickness (default
1). Throws StateError outside raylib.smoothLines.

functions.name: smoothLines
functions.doc:
smoothLines runs draw, in which smoothLine draws antialiased round-capped
lines with premultiplied alpha, all sent to the GPU in one batch at the
end. Fails with StateError when no window is open and RuntimeError when
the line shader doesn't compile.

functions.name: sphere
functions.signature: raylib.sphere(center: any, radius: number, color: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
sphere draws a sphere around a center {x, y, z}. Options: wireframe,
rings (default 16) and slices (default 16).

functions.name: svgSize
functions.doc:
svgSize returns the [width, height] loadSVG gives an SVG at scale, or
[0, 0].

Deprecated: use raylib.loadSVG(path, scale) and the image's width() and height() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.loadSVG(path, scale) and the image's width() and height() instead.

functions.name: svgViewBox
functions.doc:
svgViewBox returns an SVG file's viewBox as [x, y, width, height], or
zeros.

Deprecated: use svg.infoFile(path) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use svg.infoFile(path) instead.

functions.name: takeScreenshot
functions.doc:
takeScreenshot saves what the window shows to an image file (PNG by
extension). Fails with StateError when no window is open and IOError when
the file can't be written.

functions.name: text
functions.signature: raylib.text(text: string, position: any, options?: object)
functions.doc:
text draws text with its top-left corner at a point {x, y}. Options: size
(em size, default 20) and color (default "#000000").

functions.name: textHeight
functions.doc:
textHeight returns the line height text uses for an em size: the font's
ascent plus descent, or the size itself with raylib's default font.

functions.name: textureFromImage
functions.doc:
textureFromImage uploads an img.Image from std:img to the GPU as a
texture, so anything drawn with img can be shown in the window. Later
changes to the image don't reach the texture. Options: premultiplied, as
for Image.toTexture. Fails with StateError when no window is open; throws
StateError when the image is closed and TypeError for null.

functions.name: time
functions.doc:
time returns the seconds since the window was opened.

Deprecated: use raylib.elapsed() instead; it returns milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.elapsed() instead; it returns milliseconds.

functions.name: useFont
functions.signature: raylib.useFont(path: string, baseSize: int) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
useFont makes text and measureText use a TTF or OTF font, rasterised at
baseSize pixels and smoothly scaled; sizes passed to them are em sizes, as
in CSS. Fails with StateError when no window is open, NotFoundError or
IOError when the file can't be read, and ParseError when it isn't a font.

functions.name: vec
functions.signature: raylib.vec(x: number, y: number) -> {x: number, y: number}
functions.doc: vec builds a 2D point {x, y}.

functions.name: vec3
functions.signature: raylib.vec3(x: number, y: number, z: number) -> {x: number, y: number, z: number}
functions.doc: vec3 builds a 3D point {x, y, z}.

functions.name: windowReady
functions.doc:
windowReady reports whether a window is open.

Deprecated: use raylib.isWindowReady() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use raylib.isWindowReady() instead.

functions.name: windowShouldClose
functions.doc:
windowShouldClose reports whether the user asked to close the window
(its close button or Escape). Throws StateError when no window is open.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close frees the texture's GPU memory. A texture from a render texture's
texture() belongs to it and is freed with it; closing that one only stops
it being used. Closing twice does nothing; drawing a closed texture
throws StateError.

methods.name: drawAt
methods.doc:
drawAt draws the texture with its top-left corner at a point {x, y}.
Options: scale (default 1), rotation (degrees around origin, default 0),
tint (a color multiplied in, default "#ffffff"), source (the part of the
texture to draw, {x, y, width, height} in texture pixels with x, y its
top-left pixel, 1, 1 for the texture's corner; default all of it; a
negative width or height flips it), width and height (the drawn size;
default the source size times scale) and origin (how far {x, y} from the
drawn rectangle's top-left corner the point is that position and rotation
refer to; default {x: 0, y: 0}). Throws StateError when the texture is
closed.

methods.name: drawBillboard
methods.doc:
drawBillboard draws the texture in 3D at a point {x, y, z}, always facing
the camera. Call it inside camera.use. Options: size (world units tall,
default 1) and tint (default "#ffffff"). Throws StateError when the
texture is closed.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: height returns the texture's height in pixels.

methods.name: isClosed
methods.doc:
isClosed reports whether the texture has been closed, or belongs to a
render texture that has.

methods.name: setFilter
methods.doc:
setFilter sets how the texture is sampled when scaled: "point" (sharp
pixels, the default), "bilinear" or "trilinear" (smooth, with mipmaps).
Fails with StateError when the texture is closed; throws ValueError for
an unknown mode.

methods.name: setWrap
methods.doc:
setWrap sets how sampling beyond the texture's edges behaves: "repeat"
(the default), "clamp" (edge pixels extend outwards) or "mirror". Fails
with StateError when the texture is closed; throws ValueError for an
unknown mode.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc:
unload frees the texture and returns false when it was already unloaded.

Deprecated: use texture.close() instead.

methods.name: valid
methods.doc:
valid reports whether the texture loaded and hasn't been unloaded.

Deprecated: loaders now fail with a result instead of returning invalid textures; use isClosed() for closed ones.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: loaders now fail with a result instead of returning invalid textures; use isClosed() for closed ones.

methods.name: width
methods.doc: width returns the texture's width in pixels.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close frees the image's memory. Closing twice does nothing; any other use
afterwards throws StateError.

methods.name: height
methods.doc:
height returns the image's height in pixels. Throws StateError when the
image is closed.

methods.name: isClosed
methods.doc: isClosed reports whether the image has been closed.

methods.name: pixels
methods.doc:
pixels returns every pixel row by row from the top left, each packed as
one 0xRRGGBBAA number. Throws StateError when the image is closed.

methods.name: premultipliedTexture
methods.doc:
premultipliedTexture uploads a premultiplied copy of the image, returning
an invalid texture when it can't.

Deprecated: use image.toTexture({premultiplied: true}) instead.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
save writes the image to a file (PNG by extension), alpha included.
Fails with IOError when the file can't be written; throws StateError when
the image is closed.

methods.name: texture
methods.doc:
texture uploads the image to the GPU, returning an invalid texture when it
can't.

Deprecated: use image.toTexture() instead.

methods.name: toImage
methods.doc:
toImage copies the image into a new img.Image from std:img, to draw on,
filter or encode it there; the two don't share pixels. Throws StateError
when the image is closed.

methods.name: toTexture
methods.doc:
toTexture uploads the image to the GPU as a texture. Options:
premultiplied (multiply color by alpha first, for drawing inside
raylib.blend("premultiplied", ...); linear filtering of such a texture
doesn't darken the edges of transparent areas). Fails with StateError
when no window is open; throws StateError when the image is closed.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc:
unload frees the image and returns false when it was already unloaded.

Deprecated: use image.close() instead.

methods.name: valid
methods.doc:
valid reports whether the image loaded and hasn't been unloaded.

Deprecated: loaders now fail with a result instead of returning invalid images; use isClosed() for closed ones.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: loaders now fail with a result instead of returning invalid images; use isClosed() for closed ones.

methods.name: width
methods.doc:
width returns the image's width in pixels. Throws StateError when the
image is closed.

methods.name: centerRay
methods.doc:
centerRay returns the ray from the camera through the middle of the
screen.

methods.name: control
methods.doc:
control moves the camera from this frame's keyboard and mouse input the
way raylib's camera modes do: "free" (fly with WASD and the mouse),
"orbital" (circle the target), "firstPerson" or "thirdPerson". Throws
ValueError for an unknown mode.

methods.name: position
methods.signature: camera.position() -> {x: number, y: number, z: number}
methods.doc: position returns where the camera is, {x, y, z}.

methods.name: screenRay
methods.doc:
screenRay returns the ray from the camera through a point {x, y} on the
screen, such as the mouse position.

methods.name: setPosition
methods.doc: setPosition moves the camera to a point {x, y, z}. It always succeeds.

methods.name: setTarget
methods.doc: setTarget points the camera at a point {x, y, z}. It always succeeds.

methods.name: target
methods.signature: camera.target() -> {x: number, y: number, z: number}
methods.doc: target returns the point {x, y, z} the camera looks at.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
update moves the camera from input in a mode ("free" by default); unknown
modes mean "free".

Deprecated: use camera.control(mode) instead.

methods.name: use
methods.doc:
use runs draw with 3D drawing (cube, sphere, ...) seen through this
camera. Call it inside raylib.draw.

methods.name: offset
methods.doc: offset returns where on screen the target appears, {x, y}.

methods.name: rotation
methods.doc: rotation returns the camera's rotation in degrees.

methods.name: setOffset
methods.doc: setOffset sets where on screen the target appears, {x, y}.

methods.name: setRotation
methods.doc: setRotation sets the camera's rotation in degrees.

methods.name: setTarget
methods.doc: setTarget sets the world point {x, y} the camera looks at.

methods.name: setZoom
methods.doc: setZoom sets the camera's zoom. Throws ValueError unless it is more than 0.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: target returns the world point {x, y} the camera looks at.

methods.name: toScreen
methods.doc: toScreen converts a world point {x, y} to where it appears on screen.

methods.name: toWorld
methods.doc:
toWorld converts a screen point {x, y}, such as the mouse position, to the
world point under it.

methods.name: use
methods.doc:
use runs draw with drawing panned, rotated and zoomed by this camera.
Call it inside raylib.draw.

methods.name: zoom
methods.doc: zoom returns the camera's zoom; 2 draws everything twice as large.

methods.name: box
methods.signature: ray.box(center: any, size: any) -> {distance: number?, hit: boolean, normal: {x: number, y: number, z: number}?, point: {x: number, y: number, z: number}?}
methods.returns: {distance: number?, hit: boolean, normal: {x: number, y: number, z: number}?, point: {x: number, y: number, z: number}?}

methods.name: begin
methods.doc:
begin starts drawing through the shader and returns false for an invalid
one.

Deprecated: use shader.use(draw) instead.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close frees the shader. Closing twice does nothing; any other use
afterwards throws StateError.

methods.name: drawFullscreen
methods.doc:
drawFullscreen fills the whole window with white drawn through this
shader. Fails with StateError when the shader is closed or no window is
open.

methods.name: drawRect
methods.doc:
drawRect fills a rectangle {x, y, width, height} with white drawn through
this shader. Throws StateError when the shader is closed.

methods.name: end
methods.doc:
end stops drawing through the shader.

Deprecated: use shader.use(draw) instead.

methods.name: hasUniform
methods.doc:
hasUniform reports whether the shader has a uniform with this name. GLSL
drops uniforms the code doesn't use.

methods.name: isClosed
methods.doc: isClosed reports whether the shader has been closed.

methods.name: setUniform
methods.signature: shader.setUniform(name: string, value: any) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
setUniform sets a uniform: a number (float), an array of 1 to 4 numbers
or a vector {x, y}, {x, y, z} or {x, y, z, w} (float to vec4), a color
{r, g, b, a} (vec4 of 0-255 channels), or a texture or render texture
(sampler2D). Setting a uniform the shader doesn't have does nothing,
since GLSL drops unused ones (see hasUniform). Fails with StateError when
the shader is closed; throws TypeError for any other value.

methods.name: setValue
methods.doc:
setValue sets a uniform and returns false when the shader is invalid, has
no such uniform, or the value can't be used.

Deprecated: use shader.setUniform(name, value) instead.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc:
unload frees the shader and returns false when it was invalid or already
unloaded.

Deprecated: use shader.close() instead.

methods.name: use
methods.doc:
use runs draw with everything it draws passed through this shader. Call
it inside raylib.draw. Throws StateError when the shader is closed.

methods.name: valid
methods.doc:
valid reports whether the shader compiled and hasn't been unloaded.

Deprecated: raylib.compileShader fails with a result instead of returning invalid shaders; use isClosed() for closed ones.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: raylib.compileShader fails with a result instead of returning invalid shaders; use isClosed() for closed ones.

methods.name: begin
methods.doc:
begin starts drawing into the render texture and returns false for an
invalid one.

Deprecated: use renderTexture.use(draw) instead.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close frees the render texture, and the textures texture() returned with
it. Closing twice does nothing; any other use afterwards throws
StateError.

methods.name: drawAt
methods.doc:
drawAt draws the render texture's contents the right way up with the
top-left corner at a point {x, y}. Takes the options of Texture.drawAt.
Throws StateError when the render texture is closed.

methods.name: end
methods.doc:
end stops drawing into the render texture.

Deprecated: use renderTexture.use(draw) instead.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: height returns the render texture's height in pixels.

methods.name: isClosed
methods.doc: isClosed reports whether the render texture has been closed.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
save writes the render texture's contents to an image file (PNG by
extension), the right way up and fully opaque. Fails with IOError when
the file can't be written; throws StateError when the render texture is
closed.

methods.name: texture
methods.doc:
texture returns the render texture's contents as a texture, for
setUniform or drawing with texture options. It shares the render
texture's GPU memory: it is upside down (OpenGL stores rows bottom-up),
closing it doesn't free anything, and it stops working when the render
texture is closed. Throws StateError when the render texture is closed.

methods.name: toImage
methods.doc:
toImage copies the render texture's contents into a new img.Image from
std:img, the right way up and with the alpha it was drawn with. Throws
StateError when the render texture is closed.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc:
unload frees the render texture and returns false when it was invalid or
already unloaded.

Deprecated: use renderTexture.close() instead.

methods.name: use
methods.doc:
use runs draw with everything it draws going into this texture instead
of the screen. Throws StateError when the render texture is closed.

methods.name: valid
methods.doc:
valid reports whether the render texture was made and hasn't been
unloaded.

Deprecated: raylib.renderTexture fails with a result instead of returning invalid render textures; use isClosed() for closed ones.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: raylib.renderTexture fails with a result instead of returning invalid render textures; use isClosed() for closed ones.

methods.name: width
methods.doc: width returns the render texture's width in pixels.

packages.name: regex
packages.description: Regular expressions from strings (RE2 syntax), compiled patterns, and text validators and extractors built on them.

functions.name: camelize
functions.doc:
camelize turns snake_case text into camelCase, as in "hello_world" to
"helloWorld".

functions.name: charCount
functions.doc:
charCount returns how many characters text has, leaving out spaces
unless includeSpaces is true.

functions.name: compile
functions.signature: regex.compile(pattern: string, options?: object) -> result<*regex.Pattern, error>
functions.doc:
compile compiles a pattern into a *regex.Pattern for repeated use. Use
it for patterns that come from outside the program: an invalid pattern
fails with ValueError instead of throwing. The syntax is RE2, as in Go:
no backreferences or lookaround, and matching always takes linear time.
Options: ignoreCase, multiline (^ and $ match at line breaks) and dotAll
(. matches a line break), all false by default.

functions.name: count
functions.doc:
count returns how many non-overlapping matches of pattern text has.
Throws ValueError for an invalid pattern.

functions.name: escape
functions.doc:
escape returns text with every regular expression metacharacter
escaped, so it matches itself literally inside a pattern.

functions.name: extractEmail
functions.doc:
extractEmail returns the first email address in text, or "".

Deprecated: use regex.extractEmails(text), which returns every address.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use regex.extractEmails(text), which returns every address.

functions.name: extractEmails
functions.doc: extractEmails returns every email address in text, in order.

functions.name: extractHashtags
functions.doc:
extractHashtags returns every #hashtag in text, including the #. A # in
the middle of a word, as in a URL's page#section, starts no hashtag.

functions.name: extractMentions
functions.doc:
extractMentions returns every @mention in text, including the @. An @ in
the middle of a word, as in the email address a@example.com, starts no
mention.

functions.name: extractNumbers
functions.doc: extractNumbers returns every run of digits in text, as strings.

functions.name: extractURLs
functions.doc: extractURLs returns every http and https URL in text, in order.

functions.name: extractWords
functions.doc:
extractWords returns every word in text: a run of letters in any
language, which may contain an apostrophe, as in "don't" or "café".

functions.name: find
functions.doc:
find returns the first match of pattern in text, or "" when there is
none or the pattern is invalid.

Deprecated: use regex.findFirst(pattern, text) instead, which returns
null when nothing matches and throws ValueError for an invalid pattern.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use regex.findFirst(pattern, text) instead, which returns null when nothing matches and throws ValueError for an invalid pattern.

functions.name: findAll
functions.doc:
findAll returns every non-overlapping match of pattern in text, in
order, or an empty array when there is none. Throws ValueError for an
invalid pattern.

functions.name: findFirst
functions.doc:
findFirst returns the first match of pattern in text, or null when
there is none. Throws ValueError for an invalid pattern.

functions.name: findSubmatch
functions.doc:
findSubmatch returns the first match of pattern in text followed by the
text of each capture group, "" for a group that didn't take part, or an
empty array when nothing matches. Throws ValueError for an invalid
pattern.

functions.name: highlight
functions.signature: regex.highlight(text: any, pattern: any, color: any) -> string
functions.doc:
highlight wraps each match of pattern in text with an ANSI color code,
returning text unchanged for an unknown color or invalid pattern.

Deprecated: use regex.replace(pattern, text, "\x1b[31m$0\x1b[0m") with
the color code you want.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use regex.replace(pattern, text, "\x1b[31m$0\x1b[0m") with the color code you want.

functions.name: isAlpha
functions.doc: isAlpha reports whether text is one or more ASCII letters.

functions.name: isAlphanumeric
functions.doc:
isAlphanumeric reports whether text is one or more ASCII letters and
digits.

functions.name: isBase64
functions.doc:
isBase64 reports whether text is standard padded base64, ignoring line
breaks. "" counts as valid.

functions.name: isHexadecimal
functions.doc:
isHexadecimal reports whether text is one or more hex digits, with an
optional 0x prefix.

functions.name: isNumeric
functions.doc:
isNumeric reports whether text is one or more digits 0 to 9, with no
sign or decimal point.

functions.name: isUUID
functions.doc:
isUUID reports whether text is a UUID such as
3b241101-e2bb-4255-8caf-4136c566a962, in either case.

functions.name: isValid
functions.doc: isValid reports whether pattern is a valid regular expression.

functions.name: isValidEmail
functions.doc:
isValidEmail reports whether email looks like name@domain.tld. It is a
shape check, not proof that the address exists.

functions.name: isValidIPv4
functions.doc: isValidIPv4 reports whether ip is an IPv4 address such as 192.168.0.1.

functions.name: isValidIPv6
functions.doc: isValidIPv6 reports whether ip is an IPv6 address such as ::1.

functions.name: isValidPhone
functions.doc:
isValidPhone reports whether phone is 10 to 14 digits with an optional
leading +, ignoring spaces, dashes and parentheses.

functions.name: isValidURL
functions.doc:
isValidURL reports whether url is an http or https URL with a domain
name, such as https://example.com/path.

functions.name: kebabCase
functions.doc:
kebabCase turns camelCase or snake_case text into kebab-case, as in
"helloWorld" to "hello-world".

functions.name: maskEmail
functions.doc:
maskEmail hides an email address's name after its first character, as
in "john@example.com" to "j***@example.com".

functions.name: maskPhoneNumber
functions.doc: maskPhoneNumber replaces every character but the last four with *.

functions.name: match
functions.doc:
match reports whether pattern matches anywhere in text. Throws
ValueError for an invalid pattern; use regex.compile for patterns from
outside the program.

functions.name: replace
functions.signature: regex.replace(pattern: string, text: string, replacement: string) -> string
functions.doc:
replace returns text with every match of pattern replaced by
replacement, in which $1 or ${name} stands for a capture group and $$
for a literal $. Throws ValueError for an invalid pattern.

functions.name: replaceFunc
functions.signature: regex.replaceFunc(pattern: string, text: string, fn: any) -> string
functions.doc:
replaceFunc returns text with every match of pattern replaced by what fn
returns when called with the matched text. Throws ValueError for an
invalid pattern.

functions.name: sentenceCount
functions.doc:
sentenceCount returns how many sentences text has: the pieces between
., ! and ? that contain more than whitespace.

functions.name: slugify
functions.doc:
slugify lowercases text, turns spaces and underscores into dashes, and
drops everything but ASCII letters, digits and single dashes, as in
"Hello World!" to "hello-world".

functions.name: snakeCase
functions.doc:
snakeCase turns camelCase or kebab_case text into snake_case, as in
"helloWorld" to "hello_world".

functions.name: split
functions.doc:
split splits text around every match of pattern; text without a match
comes back whole as the only item. Throws ValueError for an invalid
pattern.

functions.name: stripTags
functions.doc:
stripTags removes everything that looks like an HTML tag from text. It
is not an HTML sanitizer: don't rely on it to make input safe.

functions.name: stripWhitespace
functions.doc:
stripWhitespace trims text and collapses each run of whitespace inside
it to a single space.

functions.name: test
functions.doc:
test reports whether pattern is a valid regular expression.

Deprecated: use regex.isValid(pattern) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use regex.isValid(pattern) instead.

functions.name: truncate
functions.signature: regex.truncate(text: string, length: int, suffix: string) -> string
functions.doc:
truncate shortens text to its first length characters and appends
suffix, or returns text unchanged when it is no longer than length.

functions.name: wordCount
functions.doc: wordCount returns how many words regex.extractWords finds in text.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: count returns how many non-overlapping matches text has.

methods.name: findAll
methods.doc: findAll returns every non-overlapping match in text, in order.

methods.name: findFirst
methods.doc: findFirst returns the first match in text, or null when there is none.

methods.name: findSubmatch
methods.doc:
findSubmatch returns the first match in text followed by the text of
each capture group, or an empty array when nothing matches.

methods.name: groupNames
methods.doc:
groupNames returns the names of the pattern's capture groups in order,
"" for an unnamed group.

methods.name: match
methods.doc: match reports whether the pattern matches anywhere in text.

methods.name: replace
methods.doc:
replace returns text with every match replaced by replacement, in which
$1 or ${name} stands for a capture group and $$ for a literal $.

methods.name: replaceFunc
methods.doc:
replaceFunc returns text with every match replaced by what fn returns

methods.name: source
methods.doc:
source returns the pattern's source text, including any (?flags) the
options added.

methods.name: split
methods.doc:
split splits text around every match; text without a match comes back
