functions.name: request
functions.signature: requests.request(method: string, url: string, options?: object) -> result<{body: string, error: string (deprecated), headers: string[string], ok: boolean, raw: any (deprecated), status: int, statusText: string, success: boolean (deprecated), url: string}, error>
functions.returns: result<{body: string, error: string (deprecated), headers: string[string], ok: boolean, raw: any (deprecated), status: int, statusText: string, success: boolean (deprecated), url: string}, error>
functions.doc:
request sends an HTTP request and reads the whole response as
{status, ok, statusText, url, headers, body}. A 4xx or 5xx response is
not a failure. Options: headers, query, body, json, timeoutMs (default
30000, 0 waits forever), maxBytes (default 16 MiB) and redirects (default
true; false returns a redirect as the response instead of following it).
Deprecated:
timeout (seconds), params and max_bytes. Fails with NetworkError,
NotFoundError, TimeoutError, ParseError, UnsupportedError, or IOError
when the body is larger than maxBytes.

Deprecated option timeout: it is in seconds; pass timeoutMs (milliseconds) instead.
Deprecated option params: pass query instead.
Deprecated option max_bytes: pass maxBytes instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated:

functions.name: stream
functions.signature: requests.stream(method: string, url: string, options?: object) -> result<*requests.Stream, error>
functions.doc:
stream sends a request and returns as soon as the response headers
arrive, so the body can be read line by line or event by event while the
server is still sending it. Close the stream when done. It takes the
options of requests.request except maxBytes; timeoutMs defaults to 0 (no
limit) and covers reading the body too. It fails like requests.request
when no response arrives; an HTTP error status is a stream with ok()
false.

Deprecated option timeout: it is in seconds; pass timeoutMs (milliseconds) instead.
Deprecated option params: pass query instead.
Deprecated option max_bytes: pass maxBytes instead.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close stops reading and releases the connection. Closing twice is a
no-op.

methods.name: events
methods.signature: stream.events() -> iter<{data: string, event: string, id: string}>
methods.returns: iter<{data: string, event: string, id: string}>
methods.doc:
events returns an iterator over the body's server-sent events
(text/event-stream), each as {event, data, id}: event is the event type
("message" unless the server names one), data joins the event's data
lines with "\n", and id is the last event id seen ("" if none). Comments
and retry fields are skipped. A sentinel payload such as "[DONE]" is
yielded like any other event. Iterating fails like lines().

methods.name: headers
methods.doc:
headers returns the response headers, mapping each canonical header name
to its value; repeated headers are joined with ", ".

methods.name: lines
methods.doc:
lines returns an iterator over the body's lines, without their line
endings, ending when the server finishes the body. Several loops and
threads can share one stream; each line goes to one of them. Iterating
throws TimeoutError or NetworkError when reading fails and StateError
once the stream is closed.

methods.name: ok
methods.doc: ok reports whether the status is 2xx.

methods.name: readEvent
methods.doc:
readEvent returns the data of the next server-sent event, or "" at the end
of the body, after a failure and for a "[DONE]" event alike.

Deprecated: use `for event in stream.events()` instead, which yields
{event, data, id} records.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use `for event in stream.events()` instead, which yields {event, data, id} records.

methods.name: readLine
methods.doc:
readLine returns the next line, or "" at the end of the body, after a
failure and for a blank line alike.

Deprecated: use `for line in stream.lines()` instead, which ends at the
end of the body and throws on failures.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use `for line in stream.lines()` instead, which ends at the end of the body and throws on failures.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: status returns the response's HTTP status code, such as 200.

packages.name: result
packages.description: The result<T, E> type: the value of an operation that succeeded, or the error it failed with.
packages.about:
result and its Go type names are built into the compiler, which decides
which methods it answers itself. Make one with result.ok(value) or
result.err(error); using a result as a plain value unwraps it and throws
its error on failure.

functions.name: err
functions.doc:
err returns a failed result holding e, usually an error such as
error("NotFoundError", "no such user").

functions.name: fromGo
functions.doc:
fromGo turns a Go value and error pair into a result: ok(val) when err is
null, otherwise a failed result whose error is typed. A Go error gets the
kind that describes it, a "Kind: message" string keeps its kind, and
anything else is a RuntimeError.

functions.name: ok
functions.doc: ok returns a successful result holding v.

packages.name: retry
packages.description: Call a function again after it fails, waiting longer between attempts.

functions.name: backoff
functions.doc:
backoff returns the delay in seconds after a failed attempt, with options
in seconds (delay, factor, max_delay, jitter) clamped into range.

Deprecated: use retry.delayFor(attempt, options), which works in milliseconds, instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use retry.delayFor(attempt, options), which works in milliseconds, instead.

functions.name: call
functions.signature: retry.call(fn: any, options?: object) -> result<any, error>
functions.doc:
call calls fn until it succeeds or the attempts run out, and returns the
first successful value. fn receives the attempt number, starting at 1;
an attempt fails when fn throws or returns a failed result, and a
successful result is unwrapped. Between attempts it waits delay
milliseconds, multiplied by factor after each failure and capped at
maxDelay. When every attempt fails, the error has the last failure's kind
and a message naming the attempt count and that failure. Options:
attempts (default 3), delay (ms, default 0), factor (default 2), maxDelay
(ms, default 30000), jitter (0 to 1, default 0: randomises each delay by
up to that fraction either way). Throws TypeError when fn isn't a function
and ValueError for an option out of range.

functions.name: delayFor
functions.doc:
delayFor returns how many milliseconds retry.call waits after the given
failed attempt (1 or more) with the same options; a jitter option
randomises it the same way. Throws ValueError when attempt is below 1 or
an option is out of range.

functions.name: run
functions.doc:
run calls callback until it succeeds and returns an object with success,
value, error, attempts and elapsed (seconds) keys; options are in seconds.

Deprecated: use retry.call(fn, options), which returns a result and takes milliseconds, instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use retry.call(fn, options), which returns a result and takes milliseconds, instead.

packages.name: rotur
packages.description: Client for the rotur.dev API: sign in, accounts, posts, groups, economy, signing and encryption, storage and realtime presence.

functions.name: avatarURL
functions.doc:
avatarURL is the profile picture of username on avatars.rotur.dev.
Options: version (string appended as ?v= so a changed picture isn't
served from cache).

functions.name: backgroundURL
functions.doc:
backgroundURL is the profile background video of username. Options as
for avatarURL.

functions.name: bannerURL
functions.doc: bannerURL is the profile banner of username. Options as for avatarURL.

functions.name: canonical
functions.doc:
canonical serialises value as canonical JSON (sorted object keys, numbers
as JavaScript prints them), the bytes rotur signatures are made over.

functions.name: configPath
functions.doc:
configPath is the rotur CLI config file (~/.config/rotur/config.json) that
load, loadToken, logout and client.saveToken share with the rotur CLI.
Fails with IOError when the home directory is unknown.

functions.name: generateKey
functions.signature: rotur.generateKey() -> result<{algorithm: string, private_key_jwk: object, public_key_jwk: object}, error>
functions.returns: result<{algorithm: string, private_key_jwk: object, public_key_jwk: object}, error>
functions.doc:
generateKey makes a new Ed25519 key pair, returned as
{private_key_jwk, public_key_jwk, algorithm}. Fails with RuntimeError when
the system has no randomness.

functions.name: load
functions.doc:
load builds a client from the saved token (see loadToken). Without one the
client is anonymous; check client.hasToken(). Fails like loadToken.

functions.name: loadToken
functions.doc:
loadToken returns the saved token: the ROTUR_TOKEN environment variable,
else the token in the rotur CLI config file, else null. Fails with IOError
or ParseError when the config file exists but can't be read.

functions.name: login
functions.doc:
login runs the device flow and returns the signed-in client, or null.

Deprecated: use client.login(options?) on rotur.new() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.login(options?) on rotur.new() instead.

functions.name: logout
functions.doc:
logout removes the saved token and username from the rotur CLI config
file. Fails with IOError or ParseError when the file can't be updated.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new builds a client: new(token?). Pass a rotur account token, or nothing
(or "") for an anonymous client that can only call public endpoints.

Every API method returns result<T, error> whose message carries the API's
own error text. The kinds are NotFoundError for a missing resource (HTTP
404), PermissionError when the client has no token or the API refuses the
request (401, 402, 403), ValueError for other rejected requests (4xx),
StateError for conflicts and rate limits (409, 429), TimeoutError,
NetworkError when the API can't be reached (and for 502 and 503), and
RuntimeError for anything else. Response objects keep the API's own keys.
Throws TypeError when token isn't a string.

functions.name: overlayURL
functions.doc: overlayURL is the avatar overlay of username. Options as for avatarURL.

functions.name: savedToken
functions.doc:
savedToken returns the saved token, or "" when there is none.

Deprecated: use rotur.loadToken() instead, which returns null when there is no token.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use rotur.loadToken() instead, which returns null when there is no token.

functions.name: signWith
functions.signature: rotur.signWith(seed: string, content: any) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
signWith signs content's canonical JSON with an Ed25519 seed given as
base64url (the private JWK's "d") and returns the base64url signature.
Fails with ValueError when seed isn't a 32-byte base64url seed.

functions.name: verifyWith
functions.signature: rotur.verifyWith(publicKey: string, content: any, signature: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
verifyWith reports whether signature is a valid Ed25519 signature of
content's canonical JSON for publicKey (base64url, the JWK's "x"). A
well-formed signature that doesn't match is false. Fails with ValueError
when publicKey or signature isn't well-formed base64url of the right size.

methods.name: deleteBadge
methods.signature: systems.deleteBadge(system: string, badge: string) -> result<object, error>
methods.doc: deleteBadge deletes badge. Needs a token.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: list returns the registered systems, as an object of name to system. Public.

methods.name: revokeBadge
methods.signature: systems.revokeBadge(system: string, badge: string, username: string) -> result<object, error>
methods.doc: revokeBadge takes badge away from username. Needs a token.

methods.name: setBadgeProgress
methods.signature: systems.setBadgeProgress(system: string, badge: string, username: string, ...progress: any) -> result
methods.doc:
setBadgeProgress sets one user's badge progress: setBadgeProgress(system, badge, username, progress).

Deprecated: use client.systems().updateBadgeProgress(system, badge, {username: progress}) instead.

methods.name: update
methods.signature: systems.update(system: string, key: string, value: any) -> result<object, error>
methods.doc: update sets one field of the system you own. Needs a token.

methods.name: updateBadge
methods.signature: systems.updateBadge(system: string, badge: string, definition: object) -> result<object, error>
methods.doc: updateBadge replaces the definition of badge. Needs a token.

methods.name: updateBadgeProgress
methods.signature: systems.updateBadgeProgress(system: string, badge: string, progress: object) -> result<object, error>
methods.doc:
updateBadgeProgress sets users' progress on badge of system. progress is
an object of username to a number of 0 or more; tiers unlock at the
thresholds the badge defines. Returns an object of username to the API's
{grant, badge}. Stops at the first failure. Throws TypeError for a
progress value that isn't a number. Needs a token.

methods.name: users
methods.doc: users returns the usernames registered on system. Needs a token.

methods.name: addActivity
methods.doc:
addActivity shows an activity on the profile. activity needs an id and
may have title, application, status, image and media (the API's fields).
Fails with StateError when the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: broadcast
methods.signature: socket.broadcast(room: string, value: any, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
broadcast sends value to everyone in room, delivered as a "gmsg" message.
Options: listener (string echoed back to match replies). Fails with
StateError when the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: connect
methods.doc:
connect opens the socket and reports whether it became ready within 10
seconds; without a token it prints why and returns false.

Deprecated: use socket.start(options?) instead, which fails with a typed error.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use socket.start(options?) instead, which fails with a typed error.

methods.name: connected
methods.doc:
connected reports whether the socket is connected and ready.

Deprecated: use socket.isConnected() instead.

methods.name: disconnect
methods.doc:
disconnect closes the socket.

Deprecated: use socket.stop() instead.

methods.name: getKey
methods.doc:
getKey returns one live account key.

Deprecated: use socket.key(key) instead.

methods.name: isConnected
methods.doc: isConnected reports whether the socket is connected and authenticated.

methods.name: join
methods.doc:
join joins one or more rooms by name (strings, or arrays of strings).
The server answers with a join_ok message per room. Fails with StateError
when the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: key
methods.doc:
key returns the live value of one account key, kept current by
key_update messages, or null when it isn't set.

methods.name: keys
methods.doc: keys returns every live account key as an object.

methods.name: leave
methods.doc: leave leaves one or more rooms; see join.

methods.name: listRooms
methods.doc:
listRooms asks the server for the joined rooms; the answer arrives as a
"rooms" message. Fails with StateError when the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: off
methods.doc: off removes a handler added with on(event, handler).

methods.name: on
methods.doc:
on adds handler for event: a server command such as "ready", "join_ok",
"gmsg", "pmsg" or "key_update", "close" when the connection drops, or "*"
for every message. The handler receives the message object. Handlers run
on background threads; a throw is printed and the socket keeps running.

methods.name: removeActivity
methods.doc:
removeActivity removes the activity id. Fails with StateError when the
socket isn't connected.

methods.name: roomState
methods.doc:
roomState asks for the members of room; the answer arrives as a
"room_state" message. Fails with StateError when the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: rooms
methods.doc: rooms lists the rooms the socket has joined.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
send sends a raw message object to the server. Fails with StateError when
the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: sendGroupMessage
methods.signature: socket.sendGroupMessage(room: string, val: any, ...listener: any) -> boolean
methods.doc:
sendGroupMessage broadcasts to a room and reports whether it was sent.

Deprecated: use socket.broadcast(room, value, {listener}) instead.

methods.name: sendPrivate
methods.signature: socket.sendPrivate(room: string, to: string, value: any, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
sendPrivate sends value to one member of room (username or user id),
delivered as a "pmsg" message. Options as for broadcast.

methods.name: sendPrivateMessage
methods.signature: socket.sendPrivateMessage(room: string, to: string, val: any, ...listener: any) -> boolean
methods.doc:
sendPrivateMessage messages one room member and reports whether it was sent.

Deprecated: use socket.sendPrivate(room, to, value, {listener}) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use socket.sendPrivate(room, to, value, {listener}) instead.

methods.name: setListening
methods.signature: socket.setListening(application: string, media: object, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
setListening shows music from application on the profile. media has
title, artist, album, start and end (unix ms). Options: title (string,
default "Listening to <application>"). Fails with StateError when the
socket isn't connected.

methods.name: setMusic
methods.signature: socket.setMusic(application: string, media: object, ...title: any) -> boolean
methods.doc:
setMusic shows music on the profile and reports whether it was sent.

Deprecated: use socket.setListening(application, media, {title}) instead.

methods.name: setPlaying
methods.signature: socket.setPlaying(application: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
setPlaying shows "playing application" on the profile. Options: title
(string, default application), status (string), url (string), image
(string). Fails with StateError when the socket isn't connected.

methods.name: setStatus
methods.doc:
setStatus sets the status text and reports whether it was sent.

Deprecated: use socket.updateStatus(status, {presence}) instead.

methods.name: setURL
methods.doc: setURL changes the websocket address used by the next start().

methods.name: socketUrl
methods.doc:
socketUrl sets the websocket address and returns the socket.

Deprecated: use socket.setURL(url) instead.

methods.name: start
methods.doc:
start opens the socket, authenticates with the client's token and waits
until the server says it is ready. Joined rooms are rejoined after a
reconnect. Already connected is a no-op. Options: timeout (ms, default
10000). Fails with PermissionError when the client has no token or the
server refuses it, NetworkError when the server can't be reached and
TimeoutError when it doesn't answer in time.

methods.name: stop
methods.doc:
stop closes the socket and forgets joined rooms and keys. start() can
open it again. Stopping twice is a no-op.

methods.name: updateStatus
methods.signature: socket.updateStatus(status: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
updateStatus sets the account's status text. Options: presence (string
such as "online", "idle" or "dnd"). Fails with StateError when the socket
isn't connected.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: url is the websocket address the socket connects to.

methods.name: userID
methods.doc: userID is the signed-in account's id, or null before the socket is ready.

methods.name: username
methods.doc: username is the signed-in account's name, or null before the socket is ready.

packages.name: s3
packages.description: Uploads, downloads and deletes objects in Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage such as R2 and MinIO, and signs presigned URLs.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new returns a client for one bucket. Options: endpoint (required, the
service URL such as "https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com" or
"https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com"), bucket (required), region
(default "us-east-1"; R2 uses "auto"), accessKeyId, secretAccessKey,
sessionToken (for temporary credentials), publicURL (base URL that
client.public builds on) and timeout (milliseconds per request, default
30000). Objects are addressed path-style, as endpoint/bucket/key. Throws
ValueError when endpoint or bucket is missing or endpoint isn't an http or
https URL.

methods.name: bucket
methods.doc: bucket returns the bucket name.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
delete removes the object key. Deleting a key that doesn't exist
succeeds, as it does in S3. Fails with PermissionError, NetworkError,
TimeoutError or RuntimeError like download.

methods.name: download
methods.doc:
download returns the contents of the object key. Fails with NotFoundError
when there is no such object, PermissionError when access is denied,
NetworkError or TimeoutError when the service can't be reached, and
RuntimeError for any other error response. Throws ValueError for an empty
key.

methods.name: downloadFile
methods.signature: client.downloadFile(key: string, path: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
downloadFile saves the object key to path, replacing the file. Fails like
download, and with an IOError or PermissionError when path can't be
written; a partly written file is removed.

methods.name: endpoint
methods.doc: endpoint returns the service URL the client was created with.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get fetches input.key and returns {ok, status, body, headers}, or
{ok: false, error} when the request couldn't be made.

Deprecated: use client.download(key) instead, which fails with
NotFoundError for a missing object.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.download(key) instead, which fails with NotFoundError for a missing object.

methods.name: presign
methods.doc:
presign returns {ok: true, url} for input.key, with input.expires in
seconds, input.method and input.content_length, or {ok: false, error}.

Deprecated: use client.presignURL(key, options?) instead, which takes
expires in milliseconds.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.presignURL(key, options?) instead, which takes expires in milliseconds.

methods.name: presignURL
methods.doc:
presignURL returns a URL that grants whoever holds it one kind of access
to key without credentials. Options: method (default "GET"; "PUT" lets the
holder upload), expires (milliseconds the URL stays valid, default 3600000,
whole seconds from 1 second to 7 days) and contentLength (bytes; the
upload must then be exactly that size). Throws ValueError for an empty key
or an out-of-range option.

methods.name: public
methods.doc:
public returns the public URL of key: publicURL/key when the client has a
publicURL option, otherwise endpoint/bucket/key. The URL is only useful
when the bucket allows public reads; use presignURL for private objects.

methods.name: put
methods.doc:
put uploads input.body as input.key and returns {ok, status, body,
headers}, or {ok: false, error} when the request couldn't be made.

Deprecated: use client.upload(key, data, options?) instead, which fails
with a typed error.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.upload(key, data, options?) instead, which fails with a typed error.

methods.name: region
methods.doc: region returns the signing region, "us-east-1" unless set.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
remove deletes input.key and returns {ok, status, body, headers}, or
{ok: false, error} when the request couldn't be made.

Deprecated: use client.delete(key) instead.

methods.name: upload
methods.signature: client.upload(key: string, data: any, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
upload stores data, a string or byte[], as the object key, replacing any
object already there. Options: contentType (default
"application/octet-stream"), contentEncoding (such as "gzip") and
cacheControl. Fails with PermissionError when the credentials are refused,
NetworkError or TimeoutError when the service can't be reached, and
RuntimeError for any other error response. Throws ValueError for an empty
key and TypeError for other data types.

methods.name: uploadFile
methods.signature: client.uploadFile(key: string, path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
uploadFile stores the file at path as the object key. It takes the same
options as upload, except that contentType defaults to the type its
extension suggests. Fails like upload, and with NotFoundError or
PermissionError when the local file can't be read.

packages.name: save
packages.description: Persistent per-app storage of named text items under ~/.osl/apps.

functions.name: all
functions.doc:
all lists the shared store's file names.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.keys() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.keys() instead.

functions.name: create
functions.doc:
create returns a new, uninitialised store.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use save.open(appName) instead.

functions.name: exists
functions.doc:
exists reports whether the shared store has an item.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.has(name) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.has(name) instead.

functions.name: getItem
functions.doc:
getItem returns {app, filename, exists, data, size} from the shared
store.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.get(name) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.get(name) instead.

functions.name: init
functions.doc:
init points the package's shared store at an app and reports whether it
worked.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use save.open(appName) instead.

functions.name: open
functions.doc:
open returns the store for an app, creating its directory
~/.osl/apps/<appName> if needed. Throws ValueError when appName isn't a
plain file name; fails with NotFoundError when the home directory isn't
known, PermissionError or IOError.

functions.name: setItem
functions.doc:
setItem stores a value in the shared store and returns its path, or "".

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.set(name, text) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use save.open(appName) and store.set(name, text) instead.

methods.name: dir
methods.doc: dir returns the store's directory.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get returns the text stored under name. Fails with NotFoundError when
there is no such item. Throws ValueError for an invalid name.

methods.name: has
methods.doc:
has reports whether an item is stored under name. Invalid names have no
item.

methods.name: keys
methods.doc:
keys lists the stored items' file names (such as "score.txt"), sorted.
Fails with NotFoundError when the store's directory has been deleted.

methods.name: path
methods.doc:
path returns the file an item is stored in. A name without an extension
is stored as name.txt, so "score" and "score.txt" are the same item.
Throws ValueError for a name with slashes or a trailing ".".

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
remove deletes an item. Fails with NotFoundError when there is no such
item. Throws ValueError for an invalid name.

methods.name: set
methods.signature: store.set(name: string, text: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
set stores text under name, replacing any earlier value atomically.
Throws ValueError for an invalid name; fails with PermissionError or
IOError.

methods.name: all
methods.doc:
all lists stored file names, or [] when they can't be read.

Deprecated: use store.keys() instead.

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
create returns a new, uninitialised store.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) instead.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc:
exists reports whether an item is stored.

Deprecated: use store.has(name) instead.

methods.name: getItem
methods.doc:
getItem returns {app, filename, exists, data, size} for an item.

Deprecated: use store.get(name) and store.has(name) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use store.get(name) and store.has(name) instead.

methods.name: init
methods.doc:
init points the store at an app's directory and reports whether it
worked.

Deprecated: use save.open(appName) instead.

methods.name: setItem
methods.doc:
setItem stores a value and returns its path, or "".

Deprecated: use store.set(name, text) instead.

packages.name: schema
packages.description: Validate and normalise OSL values against composable schemas.

functions.name: any
functions.doc: any accepts every value, null included, and returns it unchanged.

functions.name: array
functions.doc:
array accepts arrays whose every item matches item, and returns the
items as item normalises them.

functions.name: boolean
functions.doc: boolean accepts true and false.

functions.name: enum
functions.doc: enum accepts any one of values. Throws ValueError for an empty array.

functions.name: integer
functions.doc: integer accepts finite whole numbers.

functions.name: literal
functions.doc: literal accepts only value itself.

functions.name: number
functions.doc: number accepts finite numbers.

functions.name: object
functions.doc:
object accepts objects whose keys match the schemas in shape; a key
whose schema isn't optional is required. Keys not in shape pass through
unless .strict() is used. Throws TypeError when a shape value is not a
schema.

functions.name: oneOrMany
functions.doc:
oneOrMany accepts an array of item values or a single item value, and
always returns an array.

functions.name: record
functions.doc: record accepts objects whose every value matches item, whatever the keys.

functions.name: string
functions.doc: string accepts strings.

functions.name: union
functions.doc:
union accepts a value matching any of schemas, tried in order, and
returns it as the first matching schema normalises it. Throws TypeError
when an item is not a schema and ValueError for an empty array.

methods.name: defaultValue
methods.doc:
defaultValue returns a copy of the schema that uses value in place of
null or a missing key.

methods.name: extend
methods.doc:
extend returns a copy of an object schema with the fields of shape added
or replaced, keeping its other modifiers. Throws TypeError on other
schemas or when a shape value is not a schema.

methods.name: gt
methods.doc:
gt returns a copy of a number or integer schema that requires values
> value. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: isValid
methods.doc: isValid reports whether s.parse would accept value.

methods.name: issues
methods.doc:
issues validates value and lists every problem as records {path,
message}, where path holds the object keys and 1-based array indexes
leading to the bad value ([] for the value itself). [] means the value
is valid.

methods.name: length
methods.doc:
length returns a copy of a string, array or object schema that requires
exactly value characters, items or keys. Throws TypeError on other
schemas and ValueError unless value is a whole number >= 0.

methods.name: lt
methods.doc:
lt returns a copy of a number or integer schema that requires values
< value. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: max
methods.doc:
max returns a copy of a number or integer schema that requires values
<= value. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: maxLen
methods.doc:
maxLen returns a copy of a string, array or object schema that allows at
most value characters, items or keys. Throws TypeError on other schemas
and ValueError unless value is a whole number >= 0.

methods.name: min
methods.doc:
min returns a copy of a number or integer schema that requires values
>= value. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: minLen
methods.doc:
minLen returns a copy of a string, array or object schema that requires
at least value characters, items or keys. Throws TypeError on other
schemas and ValueError unless value is a whole number >= 0.

methods.name: nullable
methods.doc: nullable returns a copy of the schema that also accepts null.

methods.name: optional
methods.doc:
optional returns a copy of the schema that also accepts null or a
missing key.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
parse validates value and returns it normalised: strings trimmed where
.trim() is used, defaults filled in, a oneOrMany value as an array, and
keys outside a strict object's shape removed. Throws ValueError naming
the path of the first problem, such as "schema.Schema.parse:
users[2].name: Expected string, received number"; use try(s.parse(value))
for a result, and s.issues(value) to list every problem.

methods.name: partial
methods.doc:
partial returns a copy of an object schema with every field optional.
Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: requireAny
methods.doc:
requireAny returns a copy of an object schema that requires at least one
of fields to be present, even as null. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: requireAnyValue
methods.doc:
requireAnyValue returns a copy of an object schema that requires at
least one of fields to hold a non-null value. Throws TypeError on other
schemas.

methods.name: strict
methods.doc:
strict returns a copy of an object schema that rejects keys not in its
shape. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

methods.name: trim
methods.doc:
trim returns a copy of a string schema that trims surrounding whitespace
before checking. Throws TypeError on other schemas.

packages.name: semver
packages.description: Parse, compare and range-match semantic versions such as "1.4.0-rc.1".

functions.name: compare
functions.signature: semver.compare(a: string, b: string) -> result<int, error>
functions.doc:
compare returns -1, 0 or 1 as a is lower than, equal to or higher than b
in semantic version precedence; build metadata is ignored. Fails with
ParseError when either is not a semantic version.

functions.name: eq
functions.signature: semver.eq(a: string, b: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
eq reports whether versions a and b have equal precedence (build
metadata is ignored). Fails with ParseError when either is not a
semantic version.

functions.name: gt
functions.signature: semver.gt(a: string, b: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
gt reports whether version a is higher than b. Fails with ParseError
when either is not a semantic version.

functions.name: gte
functions.signature: semver.gte(a: string, b: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
gte reports whether version a is higher than or equal to b. Fails with
ParseError when either is not a semantic version.

functions.name: inc
functions.signature: semver.inc(version: string, part: string) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
inc returns version with part ("major", "minor" or "patch") increased
and the lower parts, prerelease and build cleared. Fails with ParseError
when version is not a semantic version; throws ValueError for any other
part.

functions.name: isValid
functions.doc: isValid reports whether text is a semantic version semver.parse accepts.

functions.name: lt
functions.signature: semver.lt(a: string, b: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
lt reports whether version a is lower than b. Fails with ParseError when
either is not a semantic version.

functions.name: lte
functions.signature: semver.lte(a: string, b: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
lte reports whether version a is lower than or equal to b. Fails with
ParseError when either is not a semantic version.

functions.name: max
functions.doc:
max returns the highest of an array of version strings, as written. Fails with ParseError
when any item is not a semantic version and ValueError when versions is
empty.

functions.name: min
functions.doc:
min returns the lowest of an array of version strings, as written. Fails with ParseError
when any item is not a semantic version and ValueError when versions is
empty.

functions.name: neq
functions.signature: semver.neq(a: string, b: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
neq reports whether versions a and b have different precedence. Fails
with ParseError when either is not a semantic version.

functions.name: parse
functions.signature: semver.parse(text: string) -> result<{build: string?, major: int, minor: int, patch: int, prerelease: string?, valid: boolean (deprecated)}, error>
functions.returns: result<{build: string?, major: int, minor: int, patch: int, prerelease: string?, valid: boolean (deprecated)}, error>
functions.doc:
parse reads a semantic version such as "1.4.0-rc.1+build.5"; a leading
"v" is allowed. Returns a record {major, minor, patch, prerelease, build}
where prerelease and build are strings, or null when absent; the
deprecated key valid is always true. Fails with ParseError when text is
not a semantic version.

functions.name: satisfies
functions.signature: semver.satisfies(version: string, constraint: string) -> result<boolean, error>
functions.doc:
satisfies reports whether version is in the npm-style range: comparators
(">=1.2.0 <2"), caret and tilde ranges ("^1.2", "~1.2.3"), x-ranges
("1.x"), hyphen ranges ("1.2 - 1.5") and alternatives joined by "||".
Prereleases only match comparators on the same major.minor.patch. Fails
with ParseError when version is not a semantic version or the range is
malformed.

functions.name: sort
functions.doc:
sort returns an array of version strings in ascending precedence as a
new array; equal versions keep their order. Throws TypeError when
versions is not an array of strings. Fails with ParseError when any item is not a
semantic version.

packages.name: serve
packages.description: Runs HTTP servers with routes, middleware, templates, static files and WebSocket endpoints.

functions.name: basicAuth
functions.doc:
basicAuth returns middleware that answers 401 with a Basic challenge
unless the request carries the given username and password, which are
compared in constant time. An empty password, such as an unset
environment variable, refuses every request, and a warning says so when
the middleware is made.

functions.name: cors
functions.signature: serve.cors(allowOrigin: string, allowMethods: string, allowHeaders: string) -> serve.Handler
functions.doc:
cors returns middleware that sets the CORS headers allowing allowOrigin
to call with allowMethods and allowHeaders (comma-separated lists), with
credentials unless the origin is "*", and answers preflight OPTIONS
requests with 204.

functions.name: corsOpen
functions.doc:
corsOpen returns cors middleware allowing any origin, every common
method and any header.

functions.name: logger
functions.doc:
logger returns middleware that prints one line per request: time,
method, path, status, response bytes and duration.

functions.name: maxBodySize
functions.doc:
maxBodySize returns middleware that limits the request body of the
routes it guards to maxBytes; larger bodies answer 413.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new creates a router. Add routes with app.get(path, handler) and the
other method functions, then serve it with app.run(address). Option:
trustProxy, the reverse proxies in front of the server as IP addresses
or CIDR ranges, such as ["10.0.0.0/8"]. Only a request whose direct peer
is one of them has its X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto headers read
by c.ip(), c.scheme() and c.fullURL(), and so by serve.rateLimit; any
client can send those headers, so from anyone else they are ignored.

The default is this machine (127.0.0.0/8 and ::1), so a Cloudflare Tunnel
or a local nginx works with no options: cloudflared connects from
loopback and passes the visitor's IP in X-Forwarded-For. A proxy on
another host (a separate container, a load balancer) must be listed;
giving trustProxy replaces the default, so list loopback too if a local
proxy is still in use, and pass [] to trust no proxy at all. X-Real-IP
and CF-Connecting-IP are never read: configure the proxy to append to
X-Forwarded-For (nginx: proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For
$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for). Throws ValueError for an entry that isn't
an IP address or CIDR range.

functions.name: noCache
functions.doc: noCache returns middleware that tells clients not to cache responses.

functions.name: rateLimit
functions.doc:
rateLimit returns middleware that lets each visitor make at most
requests requests per window milliseconds, and answers 429 Too Many
Requests after that until the window resets. Both options are required,
so a route says exactly what it allows:

	app.get("/api", serve.rateLimit({requests: 60, window: date.minute}), handler)

A visitor is a client IP, c.ip(): a Cloudflare Tunnel or proxy on this
machine works as is, and one on another host must be listed in
serve.new's trustProxy. Throws ValueError when an option is missing,
requests is less than 1 or window isn't more than 0.

functions.name: recover
functions.doc:
recover returns middleware that turns a throwing handler into a 500
response carrying the error text.

Deprecated: handlers that throw already answer 500 and have their error
printed; drop this middleware.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: handlers that throw already answer 500 and have their error printed; drop this middleware.

functions.name: requestID
functions.doc:
requestID returns middleware that gives every request an id, reusing
the client's X-Request-ID when present, and sets it as the X-Request-ID
response header and as c.get("requestID").

functions.name: requireBearer
functions.doc:
requireBearer returns middleware that answers 401 unless the request has
"Authorization: Bearer <token>". The token is compared in constant time.
An empty token, such as an unset environment variable, refuses every
request, and a warning says so when the middleware is made.

functions.name: requireHeader
functions.doc:
requireHeader returns middleware that answers 400 unless header name
equals value, ignoring case.

functions.name: secureHeaders
functions.doc:
secureHeaders returns middleware that sets common security headers
(nosniff, frame denial, no referrer).

functions.name: setKey
functions.doc:
setKey returns middleware that stores value under key on every request
(see c.get).

functions.name: timeLimit
functions.doc:
timeLimit returns middleware that answers 503 when the rest of the chain
takes longer than timeout milliseconds; a late response is discarded.

functions.name: timeout
functions.doc:
timeout answers 503 when the chain takes longer than seconds.

Deprecated: use serve.timeLimit(milliseconds) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use serve.timeLimit(milliseconds) instead.

methods.name: abort
methods.doc:
abort stops the handler chain after the current handler. abort(status)
also sends an empty response with that status, and abort(status, message)
sends {"error": message} as JSON. Nothing is sent if a response was
already written.

methods.name: accepts
methods.doc:
accepts reports whether the Accept header allows mediaType; true when
the header is missing or accepts */*.

methods.name: addHeader
methods.doc: addHeader adds a response header value, keeping earlier ones.

methods.name: attachment
methods.doc: attachment sends the file at path as a download named filename.

methods.name: badRequest
methods.doc: badRequest aborts with 400 and {"error": message}.

methods.name: basicAuth
methods.doc:
basicAuth returns {ok, username, password} for HTTP Basic credentials.

Deprecated: use c.credentials() instead, which returns null when there
are none.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.credentials() instead, which returns null when there are none.

methods.name: bearer
methods.doc:
bearer returns the token of an "Authorization: Bearer <token>" header,
or null when there is none.

methods.name: bindJSON
body
methods.doc:
body returns the request body as a string; it can be read any number of
times. When the body is larger than the router's bodyLimit or can't be
read, the client gets 413 or 400 and body throws IOError, which ends the
handler without a 500.

methods.name: bodyBytes
methods.doc: bodyBytes returns the request body as byte[]; it fails like body.

methods.name: bodyJSON
methods.doc:
bodyJSON parses the request body as a JSON object. Fails with ParseError
when it isn't valid JSON or isn't an object, and like body when it can't
be read; left uncaught, a ParseError answers the client 400.

methods.name: bodyJSONArray
methods.doc:
bodyJSONArray parses the request body as a JSON array and fails like
bodyJSON.

methods.name: clearCookie
methods.doc: clearCookie tells the client to delete a cookie set with path "/".

methods.name: contentType
methods.doc:
contentType returns the request's media type without parameters, such
as "application/json", or "" when it has none.

methods.name: cookie
methods.doc: cookie returns a request cookie's value, or null when it wasn't sent.

methods.name: cookies
methods.doc: cookies returns every request cookie by name.

methods.name: created
methods.doc:
created sends value as JSON with status 201.

Deprecated: use c.json(201, value) instead.

methods.name: credentials
methods.doc:
credentials returns the HTTP Basic {username, password} the client sent,
or null when the request has no Basic Authorization header.

methods.name: data
methods.signature: context.data(code: int, contentType: string, body: byte[])
methods.doc:
data sends bytes with a content type.

Deprecated: use c.send(status, contentType, body) instead, which takes a
string or byte[].
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.send(status, contentType, body) instead, which takes a string or byte[].

methods.name: file
methods.doc:
file sends the file at path, with its Content-Type, range and caching
support; a missing file answers 404.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc:
flush sends what has been written so far to the client, for streaming
responses.

methods.name: forbidden
methods.doc: forbidden aborts with 403 and {"error": message}.

methods.name: formFile
methods.signature: context.formFile(key: string) -> result<{contentType: string, data: byte[], filename: string, size: int}, error>
methods.returns: result<{contentType: string, data: byte[], filename: string, size: int}, error>
methods.doc:
formFile reads an uploaded file from a multipart form and returns
{filename, size, contentType, data}, with size in bytes and data as
byte[]. Fails with NotFoundError when the form has no such file and
IOError when the body is too large (the client then gets 413) or
malformed.

methods.name: formValue
methods.doc:
formValue returns a field of a URL-encoded or multipart form body, or of
the query string, or null when it is absent.

methods.name: formValueDefault
methods.doc:
formValueDefault returns a form field, or def when it is absent or empty.

Deprecated: use c.formValue(key) ?? def instead.

methods.name: fullURL
methods.doc:
fullURL returns the absolute URL of the request, from scheme(), the Host
header and the request path and query.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: get returns a value stored with set, or null.

methods.name: getBool
methods.doc:
getBool returns a stored boolean, or false.

Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.

methods.name: getFloat
methods.doc:
getFloat returns a stored number, or 0.

Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.

methods.name: getInt
methods.doc:
getInt returns a stored integer, or 0.

Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.

methods.name: getString
methods.doc:
getString returns a stored string, or "".

Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.get(key) with a typed declaration instead.

methods.name: hasHeader
methods.doc: hasHeader reports whether header name equals value, ignoring case.

methods.name: header
methods.doc:
header returns a request header (case-insensitive name), or null when it
wasn't sent. Repeated headers give their first value.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc:
headers returns the request headers by canonical name; repeated headers
are joined with ", ".

methods.name: host
methods.doc: host returns the Host the request was sent to.

methods.name: html
methods.doc:
html sends html as a text/html response with the given status. Passing
data runs the template named html from the deprecated loadHTMLGlob
instead; use render for templates. Throws StateError when data is given
and no templates are loaded, and RuntimeError when the template fails.

methods.name: internalError
methods.doc: internalError aborts with 500 and {"error": message}.

methods.name: ip
methods.doc:
ip returns the client's IP address: the address of the connection's
peer. Only when that peer is a trusted proxy (see serve.new's trustProxy)
is it the right-most X-Forwarded-For address that isn't a trusted proxy.
Any client can send that header, so from anyone else it is ignored.

methods.name: isAborted
methods.doc: isAborted reports whether abort was called.

methods.name: isAjax
methods.doc:
isAjax reports whether the request carries X-Requested-With:
XMLHttpRequest.

methods.name: isForm
methods.doc:
isForm reports whether the request body is a URL-encoded or multipart
form.

methods.name: isJSON
methods.doc: isJSON reports whether the request body is JSON.

methods.name: isWebSocket
methods.doc: isWebSocket reports whether the request asks to upgrade to a WebSocket.

methods.name: isWritten
methods.doc: isWritten reports whether a response status has been sent.

methods.name: json
methods.doc:
json sends value encoded as JSON with the given status. Throws TypeError
when value can't be encoded (a function, say).

methods.name: method
methods.doc: method returns the request method, such as "GET".

methods.name: next
methods.doc:
next runs the rest of the handler chain; middleware calls it to pass the
request on and can act after it returns.

methods.name: noContent
methods.doc: noContent sends an empty 204 response.

methods.name: notFound
methods.doc: notFound aborts with 404 and {"error": message}.

methods.name: ok
methods.doc:
ok sends value as JSON with status 200.

Deprecated: use c.json(200, value) instead.

methods.name: param
methods.doc:
param returns a path parameter of the matched route: for "/users/:id",
param("id") is "42" on /users/42. Throws ValueError when the route has no
such parameter.

methods.name: paramInt
methods.signature: context.paramInt(key: string, def: int) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
paramInt returns a path parameter as an integer, or def when it is
empty. Fails with ValueError when it isn't an integer; left uncaught,
that answers the client 400 instead of 500.

methods.name: path
methods.doc: path returns the request path, such as "/users/42".

methods.name: query
methods.doc:
query returns the first value of a query parameter, or null when the
request has none.

methods.name: queryAll
methods.doc: queryAll returns every query parameter with its first value.

methods.name: queryArray
methods.doc:
queryArray returns every value of a repeated query parameter, such as
["1", "2"] for ?x=1&x=2; empty when absent.

methods.name: queryBool
methods.signature: context.queryBool(key: string, def: boolean) -> result<boolean, error>
methods.doc:
queryBool returns a query parameter as a boolean ("true", "false", "1",
"0", ...), or def when it is absent or empty. Fails with ValueError when
it isn't a boolean; left uncaught, that answers the client 400.

methods.name: queryDefault
methods.doc:
queryDefault returns a query parameter, or def when it is absent or
empty.

Deprecated: use c.query(key) ?? def instead.

methods.name: queryInt
methods.signature: context.queryInt(key: string, def: int) -> result<int, error>
methods.doc:
queryInt returns a query parameter as an integer, or def when it is
absent or empty. Fails with ValueError when it isn't an integer; left
uncaught, that answers the client 400 instead of 500.

methods.name: redirect
methods.doc:
redirect sends a redirect to url with the given status (301, 302, 303,
307 or 308).

methods.name: redirectPermanent
methods.doc:
redirectPermanent redirects with status 301.

Deprecated: use c.redirect(301, url) instead.

methods.name: referer
methods.doc: referer returns the Referer header, or null when it wasn't sent.

methods.name: remoteAddr
methods.doc: remoteAddr returns the client's address as host:port.

methods.name: render
methods.signature: context.render(name: string, data: object, options?: object)
methods.doc:
render renders the view views/<name>.html (see app.views) with std:template
syntax, HTML-escaping values, merges in the router's locals, wraps the
result in the layout view if one is set (it receives the page as body)
and sends it as text/html. Options: status (default 200). Throws
NotFoundError when a view file is missing and ParseError when a view is
malformed.

methods.name: responseSize
methods.doc: responseSize returns the number of body bytes written so far.

methods.name: scheme
methods.doc:
scheme returns "https" or "http": "https" for a TLS connection, or the
X-Forwarded-Proto a trusted proxy (see serve.new's trustProxy) set.

methods.name: send
methods.signature: context.send(status: int, contentType: string, body: any)
methods.doc:
send sends body, a string or byte[], with the given status and
Content-Type. Throws TypeError for other body types.

methods.name: set
methods.doc:
set stores a value on the request for later handlers, such as the user
an auth middleware found.

methods.name: setCookie
methods.signature: context.setCookie(name: string, value: string, options?: object)
methods.doc:
setCookie sets a response cookie. Options: maxAge (milliseconds; 0, the
default, makes a session cookie), path (default "/"), domain, httpOnly
(default true, so page scripts can't read it), secure (default true, so
browsers send it only over HTTPS; they also keep a Secure cookie from
plain http://localhost, so local development works too) and sameSite
("lax", the default, "strict" or "none"). Throws ValueError for another sameSite, and for
sameSite "none" without secure, which browsers reject.

methods.name: setHeader
methods.doc: setHeader sets a response header, replacing earlier values.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: status sets the response status code, such as 201, without a body.

methods.name: statusCode
methods.doc: statusCode returns the response status sent so far, or 200 before any.

methods.name: string
methods.doc:
string sends a text response, formatting format with values like Go's
fmt.Sprintf when values are given.

Deprecated: use c.text(status, body) instead, with a string template for
formatting.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use c.text(status, body) instead, with a string template for formatting.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: text sends body as a text/plain response with the given status.

methods.name: unauthorized
methods.doc: unauthorized aborts with 401 and {"error": message}.

methods.name: upgrade
methods.doc:
upgrade hands the request to a std:ws server, which takes over the
connection. Fails with ValueError, after answering 400, when the request
isn't a WebSocket upgrade. Throws StateError when a response was already
written.

methods.name: userAgent
methods.doc: userAgent returns the User-Agent header, or null when it wasn't sent.

methods.name: written
methods.doc:
written reports whether a response status has been sent.

Deprecated: use c.isWritten() instead.

methods.name: any
methods.doc:
any routes every common method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS,
HEAD) for pattern to handlers; see get.

methods.name: bodyLimit
methods.doc:
bodyLimit sets the largest request body, in bytes, a handler can read
(default 32 MiB); larger bodies answer 413. 0 removes the limit. Returns
the router.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: delete routes DELETE requests for pattern; see get.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get routes GET requests for pattern to handlers, which run in order;
each takes a *serve.Context and middleware calls c.next() to continue.
":name" segments match one path segment (read with c.param("name")) and
a final "{name...}" matches the rest of the path. A handler that throws
answers 500 and has its error printed; the server keeps running.
Registering the same method and pattern again replaces the handlers.
Throws ValueError without handlers and TypeError for a non-function.

methods.name: group
methods.doc:
group returns a router whose routes all start with prefix and share this
router's middleware; middleware added to the group stays in the group.
The group renders with this router's views, layout and locals unless it
sets its own. If
setup is given it is called with the group, so routes can be declared in
a block.

methods.name: head
methods.doc: head routes HEAD requests for pattern; see get.

methods.name: layout
methods.doc:
layout sets the view every c.render wraps its page in; the layout
receives the rendered page as body (write {{& body}}). Returns the
router.

methods.name: loadHTMLGlob
methods.doc:
loadHTMLGlob parses the Go html/template files matching pattern for
c.html(status, name, data).

Deprecated: use app.views(dir) and c.render(name, data), which use
std:template syntax.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use app.views(dir) and c.render(name, data), which use std:template syntax.

methods.name: locals
methods.doc:
locals sets values every render merges into its data. Returns the
router.

methods.name: options
methods.doc:
options routes OPTIONS requests for pattern; see get. Without one, an
OPTIONS request runs the middleware and answers 204 with an Allow header.

methods.name: patch
methods.doc: patch routes PATCH requests for pattern; see get.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: post routes POST requests for pattern; see get.

methods.name: put
methods.doc: put routes PUT requests for pattern; see get.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
run serves the router on address, such as ":8080" or "127.0.0.1:3000",
and blocks until stop() is called; run it in a thread to keep going.
Fails with NetworkError when the address can't be bound. Throws
StateError when the router is already running.

methods.name: runTLS
methods.signature: router.runTLS(address: string, certFile: string, keyFile: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
runTLS is run over HTTPS with the certificate and key in the given PEM
files. Fails with NotFoundError or IOError when they can't be read.

methods.name: serve
methods.doc:
serve serves the router on addr until stopped.

Deprecated: use app.run(address) instead.

methods.name: serveTLS
methods.signature: router.serveTLS(addr: string, certFile: string, keyFile: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
serveTLS serves the router over HTTPS until stopped.

Deprecated: use app.runTLS(address, certFile, keyFile) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use app.runTLS(address, certFile, keyFile) instead.

methods.name: setFuncMap
methods.doc:
setFuncMap sets the functions Go html/templates can call.

Deprecated: use app.views(dir) and c.render(name, data) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use app.views(dir) and c.render(name, data) instead.

methods.name: start
methods.doc:
start serves the router on address like run, but returns as soon as it
is listening, so the program goes on, for example to open a window. The
server stops with stop(), or when the program ends. Fails with
NetworkError when the address can't be bound. Throws StateError when the
router is already running.

methods.name: static
methods.signature: router.static(prefix: string, dir: string, options?: object)
methods.doc:
static serves the files under dir at prefix, so prefix/a.css serves
dir/a.css and prefix/docs/ serves dir/docs/index.html. Paths that escape
dir, including through ".." or symlinks, answer 404. So, unless opted
in, do dotfiles (any path segment starting with ".", such as .env or
.git/config) and directories without an index.html. Options: dotfiles
(default false) serves dotfiles, and listing (default false) lists the
files of a directory that has no index.html.

methods.name: staticFile
methods.doc: staticFile serves the single file at path for pattern.

methods.name: stop
methods.doc:
stop closes the server and its mounted WebSocket servers' connections;
run() then returns. Stopping a router that isn't running does nothing.

methods.name: ui
methods.signature: router.ui(pattern: string, target: any, options?: object)
methods.doc:
UI shows a std:ui interface at pattern, as a web page that updates live
over a WebSocket and still works without JavaScript. target's type
decides how it behaves: a function returning ui.node is a view, rendered
fresh on every update; a function returning an object with view() is a
factory, called once per visitor to make that visitor's state, and may
take the request's *serve.Context; an object with view() is shared by
everyone it is given to. After any action every page updates, sending
only what changed. Options: title, the page's title ("OSL" by default);
maxConnections, how many pages may be live at once (1000), and
maxConnectionsPerAddress, how many from one address as c.ip() sees it,
an IPv6 address counting by its /64 (100), with at most 16 in one
visitor's session, past which a page still
works by posting its form; and messagesPerSecond, how many messages a
live page may send a second (20, with bursts of twice that), past which
they are dropped.

The compiler checks target's type, so a function whose result has no
type is an error that asks for its return type.

	app.UI("/", def(*serve.Context c) -> TodoList(user = c.get("user")))

methods.name: use
methods.doc:
use adds middleware that runs before the handlers of every route
registered after it, in order. Returns the router.

methods.name: views
methods.doc:
views sets the directory c.render reads <name>.html views from. Returns
the router.

methods.name: ws
methods.doc:
ws mounts a std:ws server (from ws.new()) on pattern: WebSocket upgrade
requests go to it after the middleware, and other requests reach any
regular route on the same pattern. stop() also stops the server's
connections.

packages.name: shader
packages.description: Transpile OSL-style shader code into GLSL for raylib, with example shaders

functions.name: eval
functions.doc:
eval was meant to evaluate a shader expression, but it returned sin(t),
cos(t) or t depending on words in the text. It now fails with
UnsupportedError.

Deprecated: shader expressions can't be evaluated on the CPU.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: shader expressions can't be evaluated on the CPU.

functions.name: gradient
functions.doc:
gradient returns an example fragment shader in OSL style: a colour
gradient that cycles with iTime.

functions.name: plasma
functions.doc:
plasma returns an example fragment shader in OSL style: animated plasma
bands driven by iTime.

functions.name: renderImage
functions.signature: shader.renderImage(code: any, width: any, height: any, ...args: any) -> result<*img.Image, error>
functions.doc:
renderImage was meant to run a shader on the CPU, but it drew one of three
built-in effects chosen by words in the code instead. It now fails with
UnsupportedError; run shaders on the GPU with raylib.compileShader.

Deprecated: shaders only run on the GPU; use raylib.compileShader(code) and draw into a raylib.renderTexture.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: shaders only run on the GPU; use raylib.compileShader(code) and draw into a raylib.renderTexture.

functions.name: toGLSL
functions.doc:
toGLSL turns OSL-style shader code into GLSL; a second argument of "vert"
or "vertex" makes a vertex shader.

Deprecated: use shader.transpile(code, {stage: "vertex"}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use shader.transpile(code, {stage: "vertex"}) instead.

functions.name: transpile
functions.doc:
transpile turns OSL-style shader code into GLSL 330 for raylib. GLSL that
already has #version and main is returned unchanged. Options: stage
("fragment" or "vertex"). Defines mainImage or plain statements with
fragCoord, uv and fragColor, and declares the usual Shadertoy uniforms.
Throws ValueError for an unknown stage.

functions.name: vertexDefault
functions.doc:
vertexDefault returns raylib's standard vertex shader as GLSL 330, which
passes fragTexCoord and fragColor to the fragment shader.

packages.name: sound
packages.description: Play WAV, MP3, OGG Vorbis and QOA audio with per-sound volume, pitch, pan, pause and seeking

functions.name: clear
functions.doc:
clear frees the sound with this ID.

Deprecated: use snd.close() on a *sound.Sound instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use snd.close() on a *sound.Sound instead.

functions.name: close
functions.doc:
close stops every sound and releases the audio device until a sound plays
again. Sounds stay loaded.

functions.name: currentTime
functions.doc:
currentTime returns the playback position of the sound with this ID in
seconds, or 0.

Deprecated: use snd.position() on a *sound.Sound instead; it returns milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use snd.position() on a *sound.Sound instead; it returns milliseconds.

functions.name: decode
functions.doc:
decode reads a WAV, MP3, OGG Vorbis or QOA sound from bytes, recognising
the format from the data rather than a file name. Fails with ParseError
when the bytes aren't a sound it can decode.

functions.name: decodeFile
functions.doc:
decodeFile reads a sound file (WAV, MP3, OGG Vorbis or QOA, up to 64 MiB).
Fails with NotFoundError or IOError when the file can't be read,
UnsupportedError when it is too large, and ParseError when it isn't a
sound it can decode.

functions.name: duration
functions.doc:
duration returns the length of the sound with this ID in seconds, or 0.

Deprecated: use snd.duration() on a *sound.Sound instead; it returns milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use snd.duration() on a *sound.Sound instead; it returns milliseconds.

functions.name: fetch
functions.signature: sound.fetch(url: string, options?: object) -> result<*sound.Sound, error>
functions.doc:
fetch downloads a sound from an http or https URL and decodes it. Options:
timeout (milliseconds, default 10000). Fails with NetworkError,
TimeoutError, NotFoundError (404 or 410), PermissionError (401 or 403),
UnsupportedError for more than 64 MiB, and ParseError when the response
isn't a sound it can decode.

functions.name: globalVolume
functions.doc: globalVolume returns the volume applied to every sound, from 0 to 1.

functions.name: info
functions.doc:
info returns one numeric field of the sound with this ID ("loaded",
"playing", "volume", "pitch", "pan", "duration" or "current_time"), or 0.

Deprecated: use the *sound.Sound methods instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use the *sound.Sound methods instead.

functions.name: isReady
functions.doc:
isReady reports whether an audio output device is available, opening it
if needed. Playing a sound opens it too.

functions.name: load
functions.doc:
load loads a sound and returns its ID, or "" when it can't be loaded.

Deprecated: use sound.decodeFile(path) or sound.fetch(url) instead; they return a *sound.Sound.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use sound.decodeFile(path) or sound.fetch(url) instead; they return a *sound.Sound.

functions.name: loaded
functions.doc:
loaded reports whether a sound with this ID is loaded.

Deprecated: use snd.isClosed() on a *sound.Sound instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use snd.isClosed() on a *sound.Sound instead.

functions.name: masterVolume
functions.doc:
masterVolume sets the volume of every sound, clamped to 0 to 1.

Deprecated: use sound.setGlobalVolume(volume) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use sound.setGlobalVolume(volume) instead.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new loads a sound from a path, file:// URL or http(s) URL and returns its
ID, or "" when it can't be loaded.

Deprecated: use sound.decodeFile(path) or sound.fetch(url) instead; they return a *sound.Sound.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use sound.decodeFile(path) or sound.fetch(url) instead; they return a *sound.Sound.

functions.name: pan
functions.doc:
pan sets the stereo position of the sound with this ID, clamped to -1 to 1.

Deprecated: use snd.setPan(pan) on a *sound.Sound instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use snd.setPan(pan) on a *sound.Sound instead.

functions.name: pause
functions.doc:
pause pauses the sound with this ID and returns false when it wasn't
playing.

Deprecated: use snd.pause() on a *sound.Sound instead.

methods.name: pitch

methods.name: setPan
