packages.name: ssh
packages.description: Connects to SSH servers with host-key verification to run commands, read, write and manage files over SFTP and forward ports, and manages SSH keys.

functions.name: connect
functions.doc:
connect opens and signs in to an SSH server. address is "host" or
"host:port". Options: username (required), password, privateKey,
passphrase, knownHosts, hostKey, insecureIgnoreHostKey and timeout
(milliseconds, default 10000). Fails with NetworkError, PermissionError,
NotFoundError, ParseError or TimeoutError. The deprecated five-argument
form returns a disconnected client instead of failing.

functions.name: execRemote
functions.signature: ssh.execRemote(host: any, port: any, user: any, ...rest: any) -> object
functions.doc:
execRemote(host, port, user, password, privateKey, command) connects,
runs one command like exec and disconnects.

Deprecated: use ssh.connect(address, options) and client.run(command)
instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use ssh.connect(address, options) and client.run(command) instead.

functions.name: fingerprint
functions.doc:
fingerprint returns the SHA256 fingerprint of a public key in
authorized_keys format, such as "SHA256:uNiVztksCsDhcc0u9e8BujQXVUpKZIDTMczCvj3tD2s".
Fails with ParseError when publicKey isn't one.

functions.name: generateKeyPair
functions.signature: ssh.generateKeyPair(keyType: string, options?: object) -> {private: string, public: string, type: string}
functions.doc:
generateKeyPair creates a new key pair of keyType, "ed25519" or "rsa"
("" means rsa). It returns an object with private (a PEM private key,
unencrypted; save it with savePrivateKey), public (one authorized_keys
line) and type. Options: bits (RSA key size, default 2048, from 2048 to
8192). Throws ValueError for another keyType or bits.

functions.name: loadPrivateKey
functions.doc:
loadPrivateKey reads a private key file, for the privateKey option of
connect. Fails with NotFoundError or PermissionError when it can't be
read.

functions.name: savePrivateKey
functions.signature: ssh.savePrivateKey(path: string, key: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
savePrivateKey writes key to path readable only by its owner (mode
0600), as SSH requires. Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or
IOError when path can't be written.

functions.name: savePublicKey
functions.signature: ssh.savePublicKey(path: string, key: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc: savePublicKey writes key to path. Fails like savePrivateKey.

functions.name: scpDownload
functions.signature: ssh.scpDownload(client: *ssh.Client, remotePath: any, localPath: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
scpDownload copies a remote file to a local path over SFTP, returning
false on failure.

Deprecated: use client.download(remotePath, localPath) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.download(remotePath, localPath) instead.

functions.name: scpUpload
functions.signature: ssh.scpUpload(client: *ssh.Client, localPath: any, remotePath: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
scpUpload copies a local file to the server over SFTP, returning false
on failure.

Deprecated: use client.upload(localPath, remotePath) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.upload(localPath, remotePath) instead.

functions.name: tunnel
functions.signature: ssh.tunnel(localPort: any, remoteHost: any, remotePort: any, ...rest: any) -> *ssh.Client
functions.doc:
tunnel(localPort, remoteHost, remotePort, sshHost, sshPort) connects with
the SSH_USER, SSH_PASSWORD and SSH_PRIVATE_KEY (a key file path)
environment variables and forwards 127.0.0.1:localPort to
remoteHost:remotePort, returning the client or null on failure.

Deprecated: use ssh.connect(address, options) and
client.forward(localAddress, remoteAddress) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use ssh.connect(address, options) and client.forward(localAddress, remoteAddress) instead.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close closes the connection, its tunnels and any session started with
the deprecated startCommand. Closing twice is a no-op.

methods.name: download
methods.signature: client.download(remotePath: string, localPath: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
download copies the remote file at remotePath to localPath over SFTP,
creating missing local directories; a partly written file is removed.
Fails like upload.

methods.name: exec
methods.doc:
exec runs a command with a 30-second limit and returns {success, output
(stdout and stderr mixed), error, timeout, truncated}.

Deprecated: use client.run(command, options?) instead, which returns
{ok, code, stdout, stderr, truncated}.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.run(command, options?) instead, which returns {ok, code, stdout, stderr, truncated}.

methods.name: execLimited
methods.doc:
execLimited is exec keeping at most maxBytes of output.

Deprecated: use client.run(command, {maxOutput: bytes}) instead.

methods.name: execTimeout
methods.doc:
execTimeout is exec with a limit in seconds (at most 300).

Deprecated: use client.run(command, {timeout: milliseconds}) instead.

methods.name: execTimeoutLimited
methods.signature: client.execTimeoutLimited(command: any, timeout: any, maxBytes: any) -> object
methods.doc:
execTimeoutLimited is exec with a limit in seconds and at most maxBytes
of output.

Deprecated: use client.run(command, {timeout: milliseconds, maxOutput:
bytes}) instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.run(command, {timeout: milliseconds, maxOutput: bytes}) instead.

methods.name: forward
methods.signature: client.forward(localAddress: string, remoteAddress: string) -> result<*ssh.Tunnel, error>
methods.doc:
forward listens on localAddress (such as "127.0.0.1:8080", or port 0
for any free port) and forwards every connection to it through the SSH
server to remoteAddress (such as "db.internal:5432"). It returns a Tunnel;
tunnel.localAddr() tells the address it listens on. Connections the
server can't make are closed. The tunnel closes with the client. Fails
with NetworkError or PermissionError when localAddress can't be used.
Throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: isConnected
methods.doc:
isConnected reports whether the client is connected and not closed. It
does not contact the server.

methods.name: readOutput
methods.doc:
readOutput returns the next chunk of the startCommand command's output,
waiting up to timeout seconds, or "" on timeout or at the end.

Deprecated: use session.read({timeout: milliseconds}) instead, which
fails with TimeoutError or StateError instead of returning "".
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use session.read({timeout: milliseconds}) instead, which fails with TimeoutError or StateError instead of returning "".

methods.name: run
methods.signature: client.run(command: string, options?: object) -> result<{code: int, ok: boolean, stderr: string, stdout: string, truncated: boolean}, error>
methods.returns: result<{code: int, ok: boolean, stderr: string, stdout: string, truncated: boolean}, error>
methods.doc:
run runs command through the remote user's shell and returns
{ok, code, stdout, stderr, truncated}. Options: timeout (milliseconds),
maxOutput (bytes per stream, default 16 MiB), input and check. Fails with
TimeoutError or NetworkError; throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: sendInput
methods.doc:
sendInput writes to the startCommand command's stdin, returning false
on failure.

Deprecated: use session.write(data) instead.

methods.name: sftp
methods.doc:
sftp opens an SFTP session on the connection and returns an SFTP handle
to read, write, list and manage remote files, named like the std:fs
functions. Close it when done; it also closes with the client. Fails
with UnsupportedError when the server has no SFTP and NetworkError when
the connection breaks. Throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: start
methods.doc:
start starts command on the server and returns a Session to talk to it:
write sends input, read returns output as it arrives (stdout and stderr
together), wait waits for the exit code. Fails with NetworkError when the
connection breaks. Throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: startCommand
methods.doc:
startCommand starts one interactive command on the client, returning
false when one is already running or it can't start.

Deprecated: use client.start(command) instead, which returns a Session.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use client.start(command) instead, which returns a Session.

methods.name: upload
methods.signature: client.upload(localPath: string, remotePath: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
upload copies the local file at localPath to remotePath over SFTP,
replacing it. Fails with NotFoundError or PermissionError for either
side, IOError when localPath isn't a regular file, and UnsupportedError
when the server has no SFTP. Throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close ends the session, killing the command if it is still running.
Closing twice is a no-op.

methods.name: closeInput
methods.doc:
closeInput closes the command's stdin, so a command reading it sees the
end of its input. Closing twice is a no-op.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
read waits for output and returns the next chunk (stdout and stderr
together, as they arrive). Once the command has exited and all of its
output has been read, it fails with StateError, so a read loop ends with
`string chunk = session.read() catch (err) ( break )`. Options: timeout
(milliseconds to wait; by default it waits indefinitely). Fails with
TimeoutError when the timeout passes. Throws StateError on a closed
session.

methods.name: wait
methods.doc:
wait waits for the command to exit and returns its exit code (-1 when it
was killed by a signal). Unread output stays readable. Fails with
NetworkError when the connection breaks.

methods.name: write
methods.doc:
write sends data to the command's stdin: a string (its UTF-8 bytes), a
byte[] or an array of whole numbers from 0 to 255. Fails with
NetworkError when the connection breaks or StateError once input is
closed. Throws StateError on a closed session.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: close stops accepting connections. Closing twice is a no-op.

methods.name: localAddr
methods.doc:
localAddr returns the address the tunnel listens on, such as
"127.0.0.1:41234".

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close ends the SFTP session; the client stays connected. Closing twice
is a no-op.

methods.name: entries
methods.signature: sFTP.entries(path: string) -> result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}[], error>
methods.returns: result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}[], error>
methods.doc:
entries lists a remote directory's entries, sorted by name, with the
keys of an fs.entries entry: name, path (path joined with name), ext,
isDir, isSymlink, size (bytes), modTime (unix milliseconds) and mode
(such as "-rw-r--r--"). A symlink reports itself, not its target.
Fails like readDir.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc:
exists reports whether something exists at the remote path. It is false
when the path can't be checked. Throws StateError once the SFTP session
is closed.

methods.name: mkdir
methods.signature: sFTP.mkdir(path: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
mkdir creates a remote directory. Options: recursive (boolean, default
false) also creates missing parents and succeeds when the directory
already exists. Fails with NotFoundError when a parent is missing
(without recursive), IOError when path already exists, or
PermissionError. Throws StateError once the SFTP session is closed.

methods.name: readDir
methods.doc:
readDir lists the names of the entries in a remote directory, sorted by
name. Fails with NotFoundError when the directory doesn't exist,
PermissionError, or IOError when path isn't a directory. Throws
StateError once the SFTP session is closed.

methods.name: readFile
methods.doc:
readFile reads a whole remote file as text. Fails with NotFoundError when
the file doesn't exist, PermissionError when it can't be read, and
IOError or NetworkError for anything else. Throws StateError once the
SFTP session is closed.

methods.name: readFileBytes
methods.doc: readFileBytes reads a whole remote file as bytes. Fails like readFile.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
remove deletes a remote file, or a directory and everything in it, like
fs.remove. A symlink is removed, not its target. Removing a path that
doesn't exist does nothing. Fails with PermissionError or IOError when
something can't be deleted. Throws StateError once the SFTP session is
closed.

methods.name: rename
methods.signature: sFTP.rename(from: string, to: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
rename moves or renames a remote file or directory, replacing an
existing file at to when the server supports it (OpenSSH does). Fails
with NotFoundError when from doesn't exist, PermissionError, or IOError.
Throws StateError once the SFTP session is closed.

methods.name: stat
methods.signature: sFTP.stat(path: string) -> result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}, error>
methods.returns: result<{ext: string, isDir: boolean, isSymlink: boolean, modTime: int, mode: string, name: string, path: string, size: int}, error>
methods.doc:
stat describes the remote file, directory or symlink at path, with the
same keys as an entries entry. A symlink describes its target, with
isSymlink true. Fails with NotFoundError when nothing exists at path.
Throws StateError once the SFTP session is closed.

methods.name: writeFile
methods.signature: sFTP.writeFile(path: string, text: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
writeFile replaces a remote file's contents with text, creating it if
needed. Fails with NotFoundError when the parent directory doesn't
exist, PermissionError, or IOError. Throws StateError once the SFTP
session is closed.

methods.name: writeFileBytes
methods.signature: sFTP.writeFileBytes(path: string, data: byte[]) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
writeFileBytes replaces a remote file's contents with bytes, creating it
if needed. data is a byte[], a string (its UTF-8 bytes) or an array of
whole numbers from 0 to 255. Fails like writeFile.

packages.name: svg
packages.description: Render SVG documents into img.Image values, read their size and viewBox, and register fonts for SVG text

functions.name: addFont
functions.signature: svg.addFont(family: string, path: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
addFont registers the TTF or OTF font file at path as family, so SVG text
in that family renders with it wherever SVGs are drawn (such as
raylib.loadSVG). Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when
the file can't be read, and ParseError when it isn't a font.

functions.name: info
functions.signature: svg.info(text: string) -> result<{height: number, viewBox: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}?, width: number}, error>
functions.returns: result<{height: number, viewBox: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}?, width: number}, error>
functions.doc:
info reads an SVG document's intrinsic size and viewBox without rendering
it. The record's keys: width and height, the size in CSS pixels that a
browser gives the image, resolved from the root's width, height and
viewBox; and viewBox, the root's {x, y, width, height} in user units, or
null when it has none. Fails with ParseError when text isn't an SVG
document.

functions.name: infoFile
functions.signature: svg.infoFile(path: string) -> result<{height: number, viewBox: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}?, width: number}, error>
functions.returns: result<{height: number, viewBox: {height: number, width: number, x: number, y: number}?, width: number}, error>
functions.doc:
infoFile reads the size and viewBox of the SVG file at path, as svg.info
does. Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file
can't be read, and ParseError when it isn't an SVG document.

functions.name: render
functions.signature: svg.render(text: string, options?: object) -> result<*img.Image, error>
functions.doc:
render draws SVG text into a new img.Image, transparent where the
drawing is. By default the image is the document's intrinsic size in CSS
pixels (as svg.info reports it), rounded up. Options: scale (multiplies
that size, default 1), or width and height in pixels (give one to keep
the aspect ratio, or both to stretch the drawing to exactly that size).
Fails with ParseError when text isn't an SVG document or has no size,
and ValueError when the image would be over 100000 pixels a side or 100
megapixels; throws ValueError for an option that isn't more than 0, or
scale given with width or height.

functions.name: renderFile
functions.signature: svg.renderFile(path: string, options?: object) -> result<*img.Image, error>
functions.doc:
renderFile draws the SVG file at path into a new img.Image, as
svg.render does. Fails with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError
when the file can't be read, and otherwise as svg.render.

functions.name: size
functions.doc:
size returns an SVG file's intrinsic [width, height], or [0, 0] if it
can't be read.

Deprecated: use svg.infoFile(path) instead, which reports failures.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use svg.infoFile(path) instead, which reports failures.

functions.name: viewBox
functions.doc:
viewBox returns the root element's viewBox as [x, y, width, height], or

packages.name: sync
packages.description: Lock values, one-time initialisation and wait groups for coordinating threads.
packages.about:
Locks are values owned by the code or data they protect. A lock's name is
only for diagnostics. Relocking a held lock throws DeadlockError instead
of waiting, and unlocking one the thread doesn't hold throws LockError.

functions.name: lock
functions.doc:
lock takes the global lock called name, waiting while another thread holds
it. Release it with sync.unlock(name), often with defer.

functions.name: newLock
functions.doc: newLock returns an unnamed lock value.

functions.name: newNamedLock
functions.doc: newNamedLock returns a lock value whose name labels it in errors.

functions.name: once
functions.doc:
once calls fn the first time it is called with name and returns its
value; every later call with name returns null without calling its fn,
so `sync.once(name, fn) == null` tells a later call from the first.
Callers wait until the first call has finished, so code after once can
rely on its effects. If the first call throws, every call with name
throws that error. Throws TypeError when fn isn't a function.

functions.name: rlock
functions.doc:
rlock takes a shared read lock on name. Release it with
sync.runlock(name). Throws DeadlockError when this thread already holds
name, because read locks cannot be upgraded or taken twice.

functions.name: runlock
functions.doc:
runlock releases this thread's read lock on name. Throws LockError when
name isn't read-locked or this thread holds no read lock on it.

functions.name: tryLock
functions.doc:
tryLock takes the global lock called name if it is free and reports
whether it did. It never waits.

functions.name: unlock
functions.doc:
unlock releases the global lock called name. Throws LockError when name
isn't locked or another thread holds it.

functions.name: waitGroup
functions.doc: waitGroup returns a new WaitGroup with a count of 0.

functions.name: withLock
functions.doc:
withLock takes the global lock called name, calls fn, and releases the
lock even if fn throws.

functions.name: withRLock
functions.doc: withRLock is withLock, using a read lock.

methods.name: lock
methods.doc:
lock takes this lock exclusively. Throws DeadlockError when this thread
already holds it.

methods.name: rlock
methods.doc:
rlock takes a shared read lock. Throws DeadlockError when this thread
already holds the lock, because read locks cannot be upgraded.

methods.name: runlock
methods.doc: runlock releases this thread's read hold.

methods.name: tryLock
methods.doc: tryLock takes the lock if it is free and reports whether it did.

methods.name: unlock
methods.doc: unlock releases this thread's exclusive hold.

methods.name: with
methods.doc:
with takes the lock, calls fn, releases the lock even if fn throws, and
returns what fn returned.

methods.name: withRLock
methods.doc: withRLock is with, using a read lock.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
add raises the count by delta, a whole number that defaults to 1; a
negative delta lowers it. Throws TypeError when delta isn't a whole
number and ValueError when the count would drop below 0.

methods.name: count
methods.doc: count returns the current count.

methods.name: done
methods.doc:
done lowers the count by 1, waking threads in wait when it reaches 0.
Throws StateError when the count is already 0.

methods.name: wait
methods.doc: wait blocks until the count is 0.

packages.name: thread
packages.description: Run functions on threads, wait for their results, and pass values between them over channels.
packages.about:
When the main program finishes, running threads stop where they are. A
thread's failure is rethrown with its stack only when wait, waitAll or
race waits on it, so keep and wait on the threads you start.

A thread is typed by the return type written on its function:
thread.new(def() int -> 1) is a *thread.Thread<int>, its wait gives an
int, and its then's callback takes an int. A function whose return type
is left to be inferred, as def() -> 1, makes a bare *thread.Thread, whose
wait gives any, as do waitAll and race. Write the type where a thread is
declared or returned to keep it, as in
def load() *thread.Thread<result<string, error>>. A *thread.Thread<T>
holds a thread whose function returns a T or a type that already is one:
a subclass of T, an int for a number, or a member of a union.

An async function is written for one that returns a thread:

	async load(string url) string ( ... )

is def load(string url) *thread.Thread<string> returning
thread.new(def() string ( ... )), so load(url) starts the body and
load(url).wait() waits for its value. An async lambda is the same for a
lambda, with async in def's place:

	auto load = async(string url) string -> fetch(url)

is def(string url) *thread.Thread<string> returning
thread.new(def() string -> fetch(url)). A file with an async function or
lambda has std:thread's names without importing it. There is no await:
call .wait().

functions.name: channel
functions.doc:
channel returns a Channel that holds up to capacity values (default 0)
before send waits for a receiver. Throws ValueError when capacity isn't a
whole number of 0 or more.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new starts fn on a new thread, calling it with args, and returns the
Thread. Throws TypeError when fn isn't a function or accepts fewer
parameters than there are args.

functions.name: parallel
functions.signature: thread.parallel(items: array, fn: any, ...limit: any) -> array
functions.doc:
parallel calls fn(item, index) for every item on separate threads, at
most limit at a time when limit is given, and returns the results in item
order. index is 1-based. If any call throws, parallel rethrows the first
failure after every call has finished. Throws TypeError when fn isn't a
function and ValueError when limit isn't a whole number of 1 or more.

functions.name: race
functions.doc:
race waits for the first of threads to finish and returns its value, or
rethrows its error. The others keep running. Throws ValueError for an
empty array and TypeError when an item isn't a thread.

functions.name: sleep
functions.doc:
sleep pauses the current thread for ms milliseconds. Other threads keep
running. Zero, negative and NaN return at once; a longer time than Go
can count (about 292 years) waits that long.

	thread.sleep(250)

functions.name: waitAll
functions.doc:
waitAll waits for every thread and returns their values in the same
order. If any thread threw, it rethrows the first failure, listing the
others, after all have finished. Throws TypeError when an item isn't a
thread.

methods.name: age
methods.doc: age returns how many milliseconds ago the thread was started.

methods.name: isDone
methods.doc: isDone reports whether the thread has finished, successfully or not.

methods.name: then
methods.doc:
then calls fn with what the thread's function returned once it finishes,
and returns a Thread that finishes with what fn returns. On a
*thread.Thread<T>, an untyped parameter of fn is a T, and the Thread
then returns is typed by fn's declared return. In a program showing a
std:ui interface, fn runs on the UI's thread, like an action,
and every screen updates after it; otherwise it runs on a thread of its
own. When the thread threw, fn doesn't run and the returned Thread
carries the error, which its wait rethrows. Throws TypeError when fn
isn't a function.

	thread.new(def() -> load(url)).then(def(data) -> (
	  self.items = data
	))

methods.name: timeout
methods.doc:
timeout waits at most ms milliseconds for the thread to finish and
returns what its function returned, or null when the thread is still
running (it keeps running and can be waited on again). Like wait, it
rethrows the thread's own error. A negative ms doesn't wait.

Deprecated: use t.wait({timeout: ms}) instead, which throws TimeoutError
rather than returning null, so a thread that returned null can't be
mistaken for one that timed out.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use t.wait({timeout: ms}) instead, which throws TimeoutError rather than returning null, so a thread that returned null can't be mistaken for one that timed out.

methods.name: wait
methods.doc:
wait blocks until the thread finishes and returns what its function
returned, as a T for a *thread.Thread<T>. If the function threw, wait
rethrows that error with the thread's stack. Option: timeout, the most
milliseconds to wait; when the
thread is still running after it, wait throws TimeoutError (catch it, or
use try(t.wait({timeout: ms})) for a result) and the thread keeps running,
so it can be waited on again. The timeout is a throw rather than a result
so that wait keeps returning the thread's plain value. Throws ValueError
for a negative timeout.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close stops new sends, makes waiting senders fail, and lets receivers
drain the values already buffered. Closing twice does nothing.

methods.name: isClosed
methods.doc: isClosed reports whether close has been called.

methods.name: len
methods.doc: len returns how many values are buffered and waiting to be received.

methods.name: recv
methods.doc:
recv waits for the next value and returns it, or returns null once the
channel is closed and empty. Use values() when null itself is sent.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
send delivers value, waiting for a receiver or a free buffer slot. Fails
with StateError when the channel is closed, or is closed while send
waits; in a condition the result reads as "was it delivered".

methods.name: tryRecv
methods.doc:
tryRecv returns the next value if one is ready, or null without waiting
when none is or the channel is closed and empty.

methods.name: values
methods.doc:
values iterates over received values, waiting for each, and ends once the
channel is closed and empty, so for x in ch.values() drains a channel.
