methods.name: save
methods.doc:
save writes the .torrent file to path. Fails with NotFoundError,
PermissionError or IOError when path can't be written.

methods.name: seed
methods.signature: torrent.seed(torrentPath: any, port: any) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
seed only ever returned true and seeded nothing; it now fails with
UnsupportedError.

Deprecated: use torrent.seedFrom(dir, options?) instead, which really
seeds.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use torrent.seedFrom(dir, options?) instead, which really seeds.

methods.name: seedFrom
methods.signature: torrent.seedFrom(dir: string, options?: object) -> result<*torrent.Download, error>
methods.doc:
seedFrom starts uploading the torrent to peers from its data in dir: the
file of a single-file torrent or the directory of a multi-file one, under
the torrent's name, as torrent.fromPath(dir + "/" + name) made it. It
verifies the data first, then seeds in the background until the returned
download is closed; its client() tells the port peers connect to.
Options are the torrent.newClient options other than dir and seed, such
as listenPort and uploadRateLimit. Fails with NotFoundError when a file
is missing, ValueError when the data doesn't match the torrent, and
NetworkError when the client can't listen.

methods.name: setFiles
methods.doc:
setFiles replaces the file list without rehashing the pieces.

Deprecated: build a new torrent with torrent.fromPath instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: build a new torrent with torrent.fromPath instead.

methods.name: size
methods.doc: size returns the total size of the torrent's files in bytes.

methods.name: strip
methods.doc:
strip removes a stored metadata key and returns the torrent.

Deprecated: keep extra data in your own object instead.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: keep extra data in your own object instead.

methods.name: trackers
methods.doc: trackers returns the announce URLs, the first being the primary one.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
validate reports whether the torrent has a name, files, and one valid
hash per piece.

Deprecated: torrents from torrent.fromPath and torrent.decode are always
valid.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: torrents from torrent.fromPath and torrent.decode are always valid.

methods.name: addMagnet
methods.signature: client.addMagnet(uri: string, options?: object) -> result<*torrent.Download, error>
methods.doc:
addMagnet starts downloading the torrent a magnet URI names: it fetches
the torrent's metadata from peers (see Download.waitForInfo), then its
data, into the client's dir (or the dir option), and returns the
download, which runs in the background. Peers come from the URI's
trackers and x.pe addresses, the DHT, and the peers option (an array of
"host:port" addresses). Adding a torrent the client already has returns
its existing download. Fails with ParseError for an invalid magnet URI or
peer address and NetworkError when a peer's host can't be resolved.
Throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: addTorrent
methods.doc:
addTorrent starts downloading t into the client's dir (or the dir
option), first verifying any of its data already there, and returns the
download, which runs in the background. Options: dir (a directory for
this download instead of the client's) and peers (an array of
"host:port" addresses to connect to, besides those found through
trackers and the DHT). Adding a torrent the client already has returns
its existing download. Fails with ParseError for a malformed peer
address and NetworkError when a peer's host can't be resolved. Throws
StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: close
dir
methods.doc:
dir returns the absolute path of the directory downloads are stored in
unless added with their own dir option.

methods.name: downloads
methods.doc:
downloads returns the client's open downloads, in the order they were
added. Throws StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: port
methods.doc:
port returns the port the client listens on for peers, which is the
listenPort option or, when that was 0, the port the system chose. Throws
StateError on a closed client.

methods.name: addPeers
methods.doc:
addPeers connects to more peers, given as an array of "host:port"
strings. Fails with ParseError for a malformed address and NetworkError
when a host can't be resolved, adding none of them. Throws TypeError for
an element that isn't a string, and StateError on a closed download.

methods.name: client
methods.doc:
client returns the client the download belongs to; for a download from
Torrent.seedFrom, that is the client seeding it, whose port() peers
connect to.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close stops the download and removes it from its client; files already
written stay on disk. For a download from Torrent.seedFrom this stops
seeding. Closing twice is a no-op; using the download afterwards throws
StateError.

methods.name: files
methods.signature: download.files() -> {bytesCompleted: int, length: int, path: string}[]
methods.doc:
files returns the torrent's files, each with path (relative to the
torrent's directory, with "/" separators; the name for a single-file
torrent), length (bytes) and bytesCompleted. Throws StateError on a
closed download, or while a magnet download's metadata hasn't arrived.

methods.name: infoHash
methods.doc:
infoHash returns the torrent's info hash as 40 lowercase hex digits.
Throws StateError on a closed download.

methods.name: isComplete
methods.doc:
isComplete reports whether all of the torrent's data is downloaded and
verified. It is false on a closed download.

methods.name: metainfo
methods.doc:
metainfo returns the torrent's metainfo, the contents of its .torrent
file, which for a magnet download is only known once its metadata has
arrived. Throws StateError on a closed download, or before then.

methods.name: name
methods.doc:
name returns the torrent's name. For a magnet download whose metadata
hasn't arrived, it is the URI's display name (dn), or "" when it has
none. Throws StateError on a closed download.

methods.name: path
methods.doc:
path returns where the torrent's data goes: the file of a single-file
torrent or the directory of a multi-file one, as an absolute path. Throws
StateError on a closed download, or while a magnet download's metadata
hasn't arrived.

methods.name: pause
methods.doc:
pause stops downloading and uploading the torrent, keeping its peers and
data, until resume. Throws StateError on a closed download.

methods.name: progress
methods.signature: download.progress() -> {bytesCompleted: int, bytesTotal: int?, downloadRate: int, fraction: number, peers: int, seeders: int, uploadRate: int}
methods.returns: {bytesCompleted: int, bytesTotal: int?, downloadRate: int, fraction: number, peers: int, seeders: int, uploadRate: int}
methods.doc:
progress returns the download's state: bytesCompleted and bytesTotal
(bytes; bytesTotal is null until a magnet download has its metadata),
fraction (0 to 1), peers (connected peers), seeders (connected peers
that have the whole torrent), and downloadRate and uploadRate (bytes per
second, averaged since the previous call at least half a second earlier).
Throws StateError on a closed download.

methods.name: resume
methods.doc:
resume restarts a paused download. Throws StateError on a closed
download.

methods.name: wait
methods.doc:
wait blocks until the whole torrent is downloaded and verified (at once
for a complete one). Options: timeout (milliseconds, default 0 for no
limit). Fails with TimeoutError when the timeout passes; IOError (or
PermissionError) when the data can't be written to disk, which also stops
the download; and StateError when the download is closed meanwhile.
Throws StateError on a closed download.

methods.name: waitForInfo
methods.doc:
waitForInfo blocks until a magnet download has the torrent's metadata
from a peer; a download added from a torrent has it from the start.
Options: timeout (milliseconds, default 0 for no limit). Fails with
TimeoutError when the timeout passes and StateError when the download is
closed meanwhile. Throws StateError on a closed download.

packages.name: tui
packages.description: Builds terminal interfaces: colours and styles, boxes, tables and charts as strings, cursor control, prompts, key input and a redrawable screen buffer.

functions.name: Select
functions.doc:
Select clears the screen, lists options with numbers and returns the one
whose number is typed, asking again after anything else; "" when options
is empty. Throws IOError when standard input is closed first.

Deprecated: use tui.choose(prompt, choices) instead, which returns null
when the user cancels and a result that fails with IOError.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.choose(prompt, choices) instead, which returns null when the user cancels and a result that fails with IOError.

functions.name: barChart
functions.signature: tui.barChart(data: array, width: int, colored: boolean) -> string
functions.doc:
barChart returns a horizontal bar chart of data, whose items are
{label, value} objects or [label, value] arrays: a scale line width
columns long, then one line per item with its label, a bar scaled so the
largest value fills width, and the value. colored draws the bars in
green. Throws TypeError for any other item.

functions.name: bgColor
functions.doc:
bgColor returns text on a background of color, which is a name or an OSL
colour as for tui.color. Throws ValueError for an unknown name or an
invalid colour.

functions.name: box
functions.doc:
box returns content, which may have several lines, inside a box drawn
with line characters, with title in the top border when it isn't empty.

functions.name: center
functions.doc:
center returns text, line by line, with spaces before each line to centre
it. Options: width (whole number, default the terminal's width, or 80
when output isn't a terminal) is the width to centre in. Before this
release it always centred in 80 columns, whatever the terminal's width;
pass {width: 80} to keep that.

functions.name: choose
functions.signature: tui.choose(prompt: string, choices: string[]) -> result<string?, error>
functions.doc:
choose asks the user to pick one of choices and returns the one picked,
or null when they cancel. In a terminal it shows a menu moved with the
arrow keys (or number keys), picked with Enter and cancelled with Esc or
Ctrl+C; otherwise, such as when input is piped, it lists the choices with
numbers and reads the number of the one picked, where 0 cancels. Fails
with IOError when standard input is closed first. Throws ValueError when
choices is empty.

functions.name: clear
functions.doc: clear clears the terminal and moves the cursor to the top-left corner.

functions.name: clearLine
functions.doc: clearLine clears the line the cursor is on.

functions.name: clearLines
functions.doc:
clearLines clears the count lines above the cursor, such as the last count
lines printed, and leaves the cursor at the start of the first of them.
Throws ValueError for a negative count.

functions.name: color
functions.doc:
color returns text coloured with color: a name (black, red, green,
yellow, blue, magenta or purple, cyan, white, gray or grey, and each with
a "bright" prefix such as "brightBlue"; any case) or an OSL colour such as
"#ff8800" or {r, g, b}, drawn in 24-bit colour. Throws ValueError for an
unknown name or an invalid colour.

functions.name: confirm
functions.doc:
confirm asks a yes-or-no question: it prints prompt (adding "?" when it
doesn't end with one) and " [y/N]: ", and returns true for y or yes and
false for n, no or an empty line, in any case, asking again after any
other answer. Fails with IOError when standard input is closed first.

functions.name: divider
functions.signature: tui.divider(char: string, width: int, title: string) -> string
functions.doc:
divider returns a line of char width columns long with title centred in
it when title isn't empty. char "" means "─" and a width of 0 or less
means 80. Throws ValueError when char isn't a single one-column
character.

functions.name: drawPanel
functions.doc:
drawPanel draws a box filling rect {x, y, width, height}, in terminal
cells with x and y its top-left cell counted from 1, 1, and blanks its
inside. The cursor stays where it was. Options: title (string) is shown
centred in the top border, cut to fit. Throws ValueError for a position
under 1, a width or height under 2, or a malformed rectangle.

functions.name: frame
functions.doc:
frame returns text, which may have several lines, inside a double-line
frame at least width columns wide inside.

functions.name: grid
functions.doc:
grid returns items laid out in columns columns (2 when columns is 0 or
less), each cell as wide as the widest item.

functions.name: height
functions.doc:
height returns the terminal's height in rows, or 24 when output isn't a
terminal.

functions.name: hideCursor
functions.doc: hideCursor hides the cursor until showCursor.

functions.name: horizontal
functions.doc:
horizontal returns a horizontal line "───" width columns long; a width of
0 or less gives 80.

functions.name: input
functions.doc:
input prints prompt and returns the line typed after it, without
surrounding whitespace. Fails with IOError when standard input is closed
before a line arrives.

functions.name: interactiveSelect
functions.doc:
interactiveSelect asks the user to pick one of options like tui.choose and
returns it, or null when they cancel; "" when options is empty. Throws
IOError when standard input is closed first.

Deprecated: use tui.choose(prompt, choices) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.choose(prompt, choices) instead.

functions.name: keyPressed
functions.doc:
keyPressed reports whether a key press is waiting to be read with
readKey, without waiting for one. When standard input isn't a terminal it
reports whether input is already buffered. Throws UnsupportedError on
terminals that can't be checked without waiting (Windows consoles).

functions.name: menu
functions.doc:
menu clears the screen, shows title and items numbered from 1 with
"[0] Exit", and returns the item whose number is typed, or null for 0 or
when standard input is closed; "" when items is empty.

Deprecated: use tui.choose(title, items) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.choose(title, items) instead.

functions.name: moveDown
functions.doc:
moveDown moves the cursor down n rows; 0 doesn't move it. Throws
ValueError for a negative n.

functions.name: moveLeft
functions.doc:
moveLeft moves the cursor left n columns; 0 doesn't move it. Throws
ValueError for a negative n.

functions.name: moveRight
functions.doc:
moveRight moves the cursor right n columns; 0 doesn't move it. Throws
ValueError for a negative n.

functions.name: moveTo
functions.doc:
moveTo moves the cursor to column x and row y, counted from 1, 1 at the
top-left cell. Throws ValueError for a position under 1.

functions.name: moveUp
functions.doc:
moveUp moves the cursor up n rows; 0 doesn't move it. Throws ValueError
for a negative n.

functions.name: newScreen
functions.doc:
newScreen returns an empty screen buffer the size of the terminal (80 x
24 when output isn't a terminal). Options: width and height (whole
numbers of 1 or more) set its size instead. Throws ValueError for a size
under 1.

functions.name: pad
functions.signature: tui.pad(text: string, width: int, align: string) -> string
functions.doc:
pad returns text padded with spaces to width columns, aligned "left"
(also ""), "right" or "center"; text already that wide is returned as it
is. Throws ValueError for another align.

functions.name: password
functions.doc:
password prints prompt and reads a line without showing what is typed
when standard input is a terminal; otherwise it reads the next line.
Returns the text without its line ending. Fails with IOError when
standard input is closed first.

functions.name: progress
functions.signature: tui.progress(current: number, total: number, width: int) -> string
functions.doc:
progress returns a progress bar such as "[█████░░░░░] 50%" for current out
of total, with a bar width columns wide. current is clamped to 0..total,
and a total of 0 or less shows 0%. Throws ValueError for a negative width.

functions.name: readKey
functions.doc:
readKey waits for one key press and returns its name: a character such
as "a", "A", "?" or "é" (" " for space), "enter", "tab", "backspace",
"escape", "up", "down", "left", "right", "home", "end", "insert",
"delete", "pageup", "pagedown", "f1" to "f12", "ctrl+a" to "ctrl+z"
(Ctrl+C is read as a key, not an interrupt), modified keys such as
"ctrl+up", "shift+tab" or "alt+x", or "unknown" for any other sequence.
When standard input isn't a terminal it reads the next key from it. Fails
with IOError when standard input is closed.

functions.name: restoreCursor
functions.doc: restoreCursor moves the cursor back to where saveCursor remembered.

functions.name: rgbBg
functions.signature: tui.rgbBg(r: any, g: any, b: any, text: any) -> string
functions.doc:
rgbBg returns text on the 24-bit background colour r, g, b.

Deprecated: use tui.bgColor({r: r, g: g, b: b}, text) or tui.bgColor("#rrggbb", text) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.bgColor({r: r, g: g, b: b}, text) or tui.bgColor("#rrggbb", text) instead.

functions.name: rgbColor
functions.signature: tui.rgbColor(r: any, g: any, b: any, text: any) -> string
functions.doc:
rgbColor returns text in the 24-bit colour r, g, b.

Deprecated: use tui.color({r: r, g: g, b: b}, text) or tui.color("#rrggbb", text) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.color({r: r, g: g, b: b}, text) or tui.color("#rrggbb", text) instead.

functions.name: saveCursor
functions.doc: saveCursor remembers the cursor position for restoreCursor.

functions.name: showCursor
functions.doc: showCursor shows the cursor again after hideCursor.

functions.name: size
functions.doc:
size returns [width, height] of the terminal, or [80, 24] when output
isn't a terminal.

Deprecated: use tui.width() and tui.height() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.width() and tui.height() instead.

functions.name: spinner
functions.doc:
spinner returns the current frame of a spinner, which changes every 100
ms, or "✓" when finished is true. Print it over itself to animate it.

functions.name: status
functions.doc:
status returns message after a coloured symbol for status: "success",
"ok" or "done" (✓), "error", "fail" or "failed" (✗), "warning" or "warn"
(⚠), "info" (ℹ) and "loading" or "pending" (⏳), in any case; any other
status gets a plain "•".

functions.name: style
functions.doc:
style returns text in a style: "bold", "dim", "underline", "blink",
"reverse" (or "invert"), "hidden" or "strikethrough", in any case. Throws
ValueError for an unknown style.

functions.name: table
functions.signature: tui.table(headers: array, rows: array, options?: object) -> string
functions.doc:
table returns headers and rows (an array of arrays of cells) as a table
drawn with +, - and |, each column as wide as its widest cell; cells past
the last header are left out. Options: cellColor (function) is called with
each body cell and returns its colour as for tui.color, and turns on cyan
borders and bold headers. Throws TypeError when a row isn't an array.

functions.name: tableColored
functions.signature: tui.tableColored(headers: array, rows: array, colorFn: any) -> string
functions.doc:
tableColored returns a table with cyan borders, bold headers and each
cell coloured with the colour name colorFn(cell) returns; an unknown name
leaves the cell uncoloured.

Deprecated: use tui.table(headers, rows, {cellColor: colorFn}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use tui.table(headers, rows, {cellColor: colorFn}) instead.

functions.name: tree
functions.doc:
tree returns items drawn as a tree with ├── and └── connectors, each line
starting with prefix. An item is a value shown as text, or an object
{name, children} whose children array is drawn nested under it.

functions.name: vertical
functions.doc:
vertical returns height copies of "│", one per row; a height of 0 or less
gives 10.

functions.name: width
functions.doc:
width returns the terminal's width in columns, or 80 when output isn't a
terminal.

functions.name: write
functions.doc: write prints value to standard output as text, without a newline.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: clear blanks every cell of the buffer.

methods.name: height
methods.doc: height returns the screen's height in cells.

methods.name: render
methods.doc:
render draws the whole buffer on the terminal from the top-left corner in
one write.

methods.name: set
methods.signature: screen.set(x: int, y: int, text: string)
methods.doc:
set writes text into the buffer starting at column x of row y, both
counted from 1, 1 at the top-left cell, one character per cell; the parts
that fall outside the screen, such as at column 0 or below, are cut off.
Call render to show it.

methods.name: width
methods.doc: width returns the screen's width in cells.

methods.name: writeCenter
methods.doc:
writeCenter writes text centred on row y (counted from 1); a row outside
the screen writes nothing.

packages.name: ui
packages.description: Build interfaces from tags written in OSL, shown as live web pages by std:serve's app.UI and as native windows by std:window.
packages.about:
A component is anything that makes a ui.node. A function component is a
def that returns ui.node: it takes plain inputs and has no state of its
own, and it runs again on every update. A class component is a class with
a def view() ui.node: its fields are its state and its methods are its
actions. Tags such as <column gap=8> ... </column> are written straight
into OSL. <Badge label="hi"/> calls a function component, and <Counter/>
makes the class the first time it appears in that place and keeps it.

A UI is shown by the module that owns the screen: std:serve's app.UI for a
web page and std:window's w.show for a window. Both take the same target,
and its type decides how it behaves:

  def() ui.node -> Badge("hi")     a view, rendered fresh on every update
  def() -> TodoList()              a factory, called once per visitor or window
  counter                          an object, shared by everyone it's given to

A factory for a web page may take the request's *serve.Context.

After any action runs (a click, a submit, a change to a bound input) every
screen showing a UI updates. Web pages update live over std:ws, sending
only what changed, and still work without JavaScript: the page is a form
that posts, and the server answers with a redirect. The server only runs
actions on elements it rendered for that viewer, so a permission is a
plain if around the button in the view.

Layout follows three sizing rules on each axis: hug (the default, as big as
the content), fill (the space left in the parent) and a fixed number of
pixels. A parent places its children with gap, pad and align, where align
names one of nine points: top-left, top-center, top-right, center-left,
center, center-right, bottom-left, bottom-center and bottom-right. A single
word sets that edge and leaves the other axis at its start, except center,
which centres both.

A theme is an object read with ordinary paths:

  *ui.Theme theme = ui.newTheme({accent: "#7c3aed", radius: 8})
  <column bg=theme.accent radius=theme.radius>

On the web its values are CSS variables, so setting a theme field, as in
theme.accent = "#0969da", updates every view.

functions.name: bind
functions.doc: bind ties an input to field of target, which must be a class instance.

functions.name: el
functions.signature: ui.el(tag: string, props: object, ...content: any) -> ui.Node
functions.doc:
el builds the element tag with props. content is the element's text, or
a function filling its children with add, which runs straight away.

functions.name: font
handler
functions.doc: handler wraps fn, a method or function, with the arguments it is called

functions.name: html
functions.doc:
html renders target, with fresh state, as a whole HTML page, for a test
or a static file. target is shown by the same rule as app.UI's. opts.title
is the page's title, "OSL" by default.

functions.name: newTheme
functions.doc:
newTheme makes a theme holding values, such as {accent: "#7c3aed",
radius: 8, font: ui.font("fonts/Inter.ttf")}. Read a value with
theme.accent and use it in a tag as bg=theme.accent.

functions.name: part
functions.signature: ui.part(name: string, factory: any, props: object) -> ui.Node
functions.doc:
part builds the component a capitalised tag mounts outside a container,
such as a component's root.

functions.name: path
functions.signature: ui.path(value: any, base: any, key: string) -> any
functions.doc:
path is what an attribute set to a dotted path, such as bg=theme.accent,
holds: the value the path reads, or, when base is a theme, the theme's
field itself, so a page shows its current value.

functions.name: refresh
functions.doc:
refresh draws every screen again from the state it reads. Setting a
global and a handler's changes draw by themselves; refresh is for a change
the UI can't see, such as an item added to a list a global holds. Call it
from threads and callbacks, not from a view, which would draw forever.
Calls within one frame draw once.

methods.name: with
methods.doc:
with returns a copy of the node with props set on top of its own, as
attributes would be: a function under on:click becomes its handler. The
copy keeps the node's children. On a class component the props set its
fields when it renders; a function component's inputs are fixed when its
tag runs.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
add appends nodes, each a ui.node, to the container being built. Throws
TypeError for anything else.

packages.name: url
packages.description: Parses, builds, resolves and escapes URLs and query strings.

functions.name: build
functions.doc:
build assembles a URL from the parts url.parse returns. Accepted keys:
scheme, host, or hostname with port, path, rawPath, query (an object whose
array values repeat the key) or queryString, fragment, and user with
password. Every key is optional; an unknown key throws ValueError. The
valid key of url.parse's result is ignored, so a parsed URL builds back.

functions.name: decode
functions.doc:
decode reads a query string into an object, or {} when it is malformed.

Deprecated: use url.parseQuery(text) instead, which fails with ParseError
for malformed input.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use url.parseQuery(text) instead, which fails with ParseError for malformed input.

functions.name: encode
functions.doc:
encode encodes an object as a query string.

Deprecated: use url.stringifyQuery(params) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use url.stringifyQuery(params) instead.

functions.name: escape
functions.doc:
escape percent-encodes text for use as a query key or value, writing
spaces as "+".

functions.name: isValid
functions.doc:
isValid reports whether text is an absolute URL with a scheme and a host,
such as "https://example.com".

functions.name: join
functions.signature: url.join(base: string, ref: string) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
join resolves a relative reference against a base URL, as a browser
resolves a link: join("https://x.com/a/", "b") is "https://x.com/a/b".
The result always stays on base's origin, so a ref that names its own
scheme or host (such as "https://other.example" or "//other.example")
fails with ValueError. Fails with ParseError when either URL is malformed.

functions.name: param
functions.signature: url.param(url: string, key: string) -> result<string?, error>
functions.doc:
param returns the first value of a query parameter in url, or null when
the parameter is absent. Fails with ParseError when url is malformed.

functions.name: parse
functions.signature: url.parse(text: string) -> result<{fragment: string, host: string, hostname: string, password: string, path: string, port: string, query: object, queryString: string, rawPath: string, scheme: string, user: string, valid: boolean (deprecated)}, error>
functions.returns: result<{fragment: string, host: string, hostname: string, password: string, path: string, port: string, query: object, queryString: string, rawPath: string, scheme: string, user: string, valid: boolean (deprecated)}, error>
functions.doc:
parse splits a URL into its components. It returns {scheme, host,
hostname, port, path, rawPath, query, queryString, fragment, user,
password}: every key is a string ("" when the URL has no such part) except
query, an object mapping each query key to its value, or to an array of
values when the key repeats. path is decoded and rawPath keeps its escapes.
The deprecated key valid is always true.
Relative references such as "../a" parse too. Fails with ParseError for
malformed input such as a bad percent-escape or port.

functions.name: parseQuery
functions.doc:
parseQuery reads a query string such as "a=1&b=two+words" (a leading "?"
is allowed) into an object mapping each key to its decoded value, or to an
array of values when the key repeats. Fails with ParseError for a bad
percent-escape or a ";" separator.

functions.name: stringifyQuery
functions.doc:
stringifyQuery encodes an object as a query string with sorted keys:
{a: "1", b: "two words"} becomes "a=1&b=two+words". An array value
repeats the key once per element; other values are converted to strings.

functions.name: unescape
functions.doc:
unescape decodes a percent-encoded query component, turning "+" into a
space. Fails with ParseError for a malformed escape such as "%zz".

functions.name: withParams
functions.signature: url.withParams(url: string, params: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
withParams returns url with the given query parameters set, replacing
existing values for those keys and keeping the others. An array value
repeats the key. Fails with ParseError when url is malformed.

packages.name: webpush
packages.description: Sends Web Push notifications to browser subscriptions, with VAPID keys, signing and RFC 8291 payload encryption.

functions.name: derivePublicKey
functions.doc:
derivePublicKey returns the base64url VAPID public key that belongs to a
PEM-encoded P-256 private key. Fails with ParseError when privateKey isn't
one.

functions.name: ensureKeys
functions.signature: webpush.ensureKeys(path: string) -> result<{privateKey: string, publicKey: string}, error>
functions.doc:
ensureKeys returns the VAPID key pair whose private key is stored at
path, creating the key and saving it there (readable only by the owner)
when the file doesn't exist yet. Use it to keep the same keys across
restarts, since browsers' subscriptions are tied to the public key. Fails
with ParseError when the file isn't a PEM-encoded P-256 private key (it is
never overwritten), and PermissionError or IOError when it can't be read
or written.

functions.name: ensureVAPIDKeys
functions.doc:
ensureVAPIDKeys(configPath, privateKeyPath) loads the keys saved by an
earlier call, or generates new ones, writes the private key and a
{public_key, claims_email} config (claims_email is the package author's
address, as before), and returns the config, or {error} on failure.
Malformed files are replaced.

Deprecated: use webpush.ensureKeys(path) instead, which keeps everything
in the private key file and never overwrites a file it can't read.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use webpush.ensureKeys(path) instead, which keeps everything in the private key file and never overwrites a file it can't read.

functions.name: generateKeys
functions.doc:
generateKeys creates a new VAPID key pair: privateKey is a PEM-encoded
P-256 key to keep secret on the server, and publicKey is the base64url
key to give browsers as applicationServerKey when they subscribe.

functions.name: generateVAPIDKeys
functions.doc:
generateVAPIDKeys returns {private_key, public_key}, or {error} when no
key could be generated.

Deprecated: use webpush.generateKeys() instead, which returns
{privateKey, publicKey}.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use webpush.generateKeys() instead, which returns {privateKey, publicKey}.

functions.name: send
functions.signature: webpush.send(subscription: object, payload: any, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
send encrypts payload (at most 3993 bytes) and delivers it to a browser
subscription. Options: privateKey and subject (required), ttl
(milliseconds, default 86400000), urgency, topic, timeout and
allowPrivate. The endpoint comes from the browser, so send only goes
where a push service can be: an https URL whose host resolves to a
public address, without following redirects. allowPrivate (default
false) also allows loopback, private and link-local addresses, for a
push service on your own network such as a self-hosted UnifiedPush
server; it lets any client make the server post to those addresses.
Fails with NotFoundError, ValueError (also for an endpoint that isn't
https or resolves to an address that isn't allowed), PermissionError,
NetworkError, TimeoutError or RuntimeError.

functions.name: sendWebPush
functions.signature: webpush.sendWebPush(endpoint: any, p256dh: any, auth: any, ...rest: any) -> object
functions.doc:
sendWebPush(endpoint, p256dh, auth, data, vapidPrivateKey,
vapidClaimsEmail, ttl) sends one message with ttl in seconds and returns
{success, status, error}.

Deprecated: use webpush.send(subscription, payload, {privateKey, subject,
ttl}) instead, which takes ttl in milliseconds and fails with a typed
error.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use webpush.send(subscription, payload, {privateKey, subject, ttl}) instead, which takes ttl in milliseconds and fails with a typed error.

functions.name: signJWT
functions.signature: webpush.signJWT(audience: string, privateKey: string, options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
signJWT returns a VAPID token (an ES256 JSON Web Token) for audience, the
origin of a push service such as "https://fcm.googleapis.com". send makes
these itself; signJWT is for code that talks to a push service directly.
Options: subject (required, a "mailto:" or "https:" contact the push
service can reach you at) and expires (milliseconds the token stays
valid, default 43200000, at most 86400000). Fails with ParseError when
privateKey isn't a PEM-encoded P-256 private key. Throws ValueError for a
missing subject or an expires out of range.

functions.name: signVapidJWT
functions.signature: webpush.signVapidJWT(audience: any, expiresIn: any, privateKeyPEM: any, ...claimsEmail: any) -> string
functions.doc:
signVapidJWT(audience, expiresIn, privateKeyPEM, claimsEmail) signs a
VAPID token valid for expiresIn seconds (default and maximum 86400), or
returns "" when the key is invalid.

Deprecated: use webpush.signJWT(audience, privateKey, {subject, expires})
instead, which takes expires in milliseconds.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use webpush.signJWT(audience, privateKey, {subject, expires}) instead, which takes expires in milliseconds.

functions.name: verifyJWT
functions.doc:
verifyJWT reports whether token is a VAPID token signed by the private
key that belongs to publicKey (base64url) and has not expired.

functions.name: verifySubscription
functions.signature: webpush.verifySubscription(endpoint: string, p256dh: string, auth: string) -> boolean
functions.doc:
verifySubscription reports whether endpoint is an https URL, p256dh
a base64url P-256 public key and auth a base64url 16-byte secret: the
parts of a browser's PushSubscription that send needs.

functions.name: verifyVapidJWT
functions.doc:
verifyVapidJWT reports whether token's signature matches publicKey,
without checking its expiry.

Deprecated: use webpush.verifyJWT(token, publicKey) instead, which also
rejects expired tokens.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use webpush.verifyJWT(token, publicKey) instead, which also rejects expired tokens.

packages.name: window
packages.description: Open native windows that show std:ui interfaces, drawn with SDL2, with menus, dialogs, shortcuts and the clipboard.
packages.about:
osl:go img_draw

Windows are drawn through SDL2, which a program links from the system.
Building one needs SDL2's development files and pkg-config, and running it
needs SDL2 where it runs: the libSDL2 package on Linux, Homebrew's sdl2 on
macOS, and SDL2.dll beside the program or on PATH on Windows.

A window shows a UI by the same rule as std:serve's app.UI: a function
returning ui.node is a view, a function returning an object with view()
is a factory called once for the window, and an object is shared with
everything else it is given to, web pages included.

  *window.Window main = window.create({title: "Todo", width: 520, height: 560})
  main.show(def() -> TodoList())
  window.run()

window.run() keeps every window drawn and answering until none is open.
A program with its own loop calls window.update() once a frame instead.
Windows run on the program's main thread; a window's methods called from
another thread, such as a web page's action, wait for the main thread to
run them.

Positions count from 1, like everything in OSL: a window at 1, 1 has its
top-left corner at the screen's.

SDL2 has no native menu bars or file dialogs. window.menu draws a menu
bar inside the window on every platform. openFile, saveFile and
pickFolder use zenity or kdialog on Linux, AppleScript on macOS and
PowerShell on Windows, and fail with a result when none is there. ask
uses SDL's native message box everywhere.

functions.name: all
functions.doc: all lists the open windows, in the order they were opened.

functions.name: clipboard
functions.doc:
clipboard is the text on the system clipboard, or "" when there is none
or no display.

functions.name: create
functions.doc:
create opens a window. Options: title ("OSL"), width and height (800 by
600), x and y (centred when left out), resizable (true), borderless,
fullscreen, hidden, alwaysOnTop (all false), minWidth and minHeight,
parent (a *window.Window the new one is centred over and closes with)
and closesWith (a *window.Window whose closing closes this one). Fails
with RuntimeError when no window can be opened, such as on a machine
without a display. Throws StateError off the main thread.

functions.name: displays
functions.signature: window.displays() -> {height: int, name: string, scale: number, width: int, x: int, y: int}[]
functions.returns: {height: int, name: string, scale: number, width: int, x: int, y: int}[]
functions.doc:
displays lists the screens: each one's name, its area, counted from 1,
and its scale. It is empty when there is no display.

functions.name: focused
functions.doc: focused is the open window that has the keyboard, or null.

functions.name: run
functions.doc:
run keeps every window drawn and answering until none is left open.
Throws StateError off the main thread.

functions.name: setClipboard
functions.doc:
setClipboard puts text on the system clipboard. Fails with RuntimeError
when there is no display to hold it.

functions.name: update
functions.doc:
update draws every open window and answers the clicks, typing and other
events that arrived since the last call, then returns how many
milliseconds passed since it last returned. It waits for the next frame
when nothing is happening, so a loop calling it runs at about 60 frames
a second without using the processor while idle. Throws StateError off
the main thread.

methods.name: ask
methods.signature: window.ask(message: string, buttons: array) -> result<string, error>
methods.doc:
ask shows message in a dialog with buttons, such as ["Save", "Cancel"],
and returns the label of the one pressed, or "" when the dialog was
closed another way. An empty array shows one OK button. It waits for the
answer. The dialog is SDL's native message box on every platform. Fails
with RuntimeError when no dialog can open.

While the dialog waits, other actions can run, such as a web page's
click or a thread's then, as other code runs during a JavaScript await.
Read the state you need again after it returns: in
seen = self.count; w.ask(...); self.count = seen + 1, a click made while
the dialog was open is lost.

methods.name: bounds
methods.signature: window.bounds() -> {height: int, width: int, x: int, y: int}
methods.returns: {height: int, width: int, x: int, y: int}
methods.doc: bounds is the window's position, counted from 1, and size together.

methods.name: center
methods.doc: center puts the window in the middle of its screen.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close closes the window straight away, and every window that closes with
it. Closing a closed window does nothing.

methods.name: content
methods.doc: content is what the window shows: the target given to show, or null.

methods.name: duplicate
methods.doc:
duplicate opens another window with this one's options, a little below
and to the right, showing the same target: a shared object stays shared
and a factory makes the new window its own. Fails like window.create.

methods.name: focus
methods.doc: focus brings the window to the front and gives it the keyboard.

methods.name: held
methods.doc:
held reports whether a key, by the names key takes, or a mouse button,
"mouseLeft", "mouseRight" or "mouseMiddle", is held down now.

methods.name: hide
methods.doc: hide hides the window without closing it.

methods.name: isFocused
methods.doc: isFocused reports whether the window has the keyboard.

methods.name: isOpen
methods.doc: isOpen reports whether the window is still open.

methods.name: isVisible
methods.doc: isVisible reports whether the window is open and not hidden.

methods.name: key
methods.doc:
key runs fn when the key combination keys is pressed while the window
has the keyboard, such as "mod+s", "ctrl+shift+z" or "f5". mod is Cmd on
macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. fn runs like an action, so the window updates
after it. Throws ValueError for a combination it doesn't know.

methods.name: maximize
methods.doc: maximize makes the window as big as its screen allows.

methods.name: menu
methods.doc:
menu sets the window's menu bar: an array of menus, each {label, items},
where an item is {label, action, keys} or {separator: true}. keys is a
shortcut, as key takes, that runs the item's action and shows beside it.
SDL2 has no native menus, so the bar is drawn at the top of the window
on every platform. An empty array removes it. Throws TypeError for a
menu or item of the wrong shape.

methods.name: minimize
methods.doc: minimize shrinks the window to the taskbar or dock.

methods.name: move
methods.doc:
move puts the window's top-left corner at x, y on the screen, counted
from 1.

methods.name: onClose
methods.doc:
onClose adds fn, which runs when the window is asked to close, by its
close button or requestClose. The window closes unless a handler returns
false.

methods.name: openFile
methods.doc:
openFile asks the user to pick a file to open and returns its path, or
null when they cancel. Option: types, the extensions to offer, such as
["png", "jpg"]. The dialog is zenity or kdialog on Linux, AppleScript on
macOS and PowerShell on Windows; fails with NotFoundError when none of
them is there.

While the dialog waits, other actions can run, such as a web page's
click or a thread's then, as other code runs during a JavaScript await.
Read the state you need again after it returns: in
seen = self.count; w.openFile(); self.count = seen + 1, a click made while
the dialog was open is lost.

methods.name: pickFolder
methods.doc:
pickFolder asks the user to pick a folder and returns its path, or null
when they cancel. Dialogs are as for openFile.

While the dialog waits, other actions can run, such as a web page's
click or a thread's then, as other code runs during a JavaScript await.
Read the state you need again after it returns: in
seen = self.count; w.pickFolder(); self.count = seen + 1, a click made while
the dialog was open is lost.

methods.name: position
methods.doc:
position is where the window's top-left corner is on the screen,
counted from 1.

methods.name: requestClose
methods.doc:
requestClose asks the window to close, as its close button does: it
closes unless an onClose handler returns false.

methods.name: resize
methods.doc: resize sets the window's size. Throws ValueError below 1 by 1.

methods.name: restore
methods.doc: restore undoes minimize and maximize.

methods.name: saveFile
methods.doc:
saveFile asks the user where to save a file and returns the path, or
null when they cancel. Options: types, as openFile takes, and name, the
file name to suggest. Dialogs are as for openFile.

While the dialog waits, other actions can run, such as a web page's
click or a thread's then, as other code runs during a JavaScript await.
Read the state you need again after it returns: in
seen = self.count; w.saveFile(); self.count = seen + 1, a click made while
the dialog was open is lost.

methods.name: scale
methods.doc:
scale is how many pixels the window draws per unit: 2 on a typical
high-density screen, 1 elsewhere.

methods.name: screenshot
methods.doc:
screenshot saves what the window shows as a PNG file at path, at its
full pixel size. Fails with IOError when the file can't be written.

methods.name: setFullscreen
methods.doc: setFullscreen makes the window fill its screen, or not.

methods.name: setMinSize
methods.doc: setMinSize sets the smallest size the user can resize the window to.

methods.name: setTitle
methods.doc: setTitle sets the window's title.

methods.name: shouldClose
methods.doc:
shouldClose reports whether the window has been asked to close, by its
close button or requestClose, whatever its onClose handlers decided.

methods.name: show
methods.doc:
show makes the window show target, by the same rule as app.UI: a
function returning ui.node is a view, a function returning an object
with view() is a factory called once for this window, and an object is
shared; the compiler checks target's type. Throws TypeError for a
factory that takes a request, which a window doesn't have.

methods.name: size
methods.doc: size is the window's size, in units, not pixels; see scale.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: title is the window's title.

methods.name: unhide
methods.doc: unhide shows a hidden window again.

packages.name: ws
packages.description: Runs WebSocket servers and opens WebSocket client connections that exchange text, binary and JSON messages.

functions.name: closeConn
functions.doc:
closeConn closes conn and reports whether it was a connection.

Deprecated: use conn.close() instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use conn.close() instead.

functions.name: connect
functions.doc:
connect opens a WebSocket connection and starts receiving messages;
register handlers with conn.on. Options: protocols, headers, timeout
(milliseconds, default 10000), maxMessageBytes (default 1 MiB), sendQueue
(default 256) and compression. Fails with ParseError, UnsupportedError,
NotFoundError, TimeoutError or NetworkError. Deprecated positional
protocols from argument 2 are still accepted.

Deprecated positional arguments from 2: pass {protocols: [...]} instead.

functions.name: new
functions.doc:
new creates a WebSocket server for app.ws(path, server) or standalone
server.run(). Options: address (default ":8080"), path (default "/"),
maxMessageBytes (default 1 MiB), sendQueue (default 256) and compression.
Deprecated positional address/path arguments are still accepted.

Deprecated positional arguments from 1: pass {address, path} instead.

functions.name: newServer
functions.doc:
newServer creates a standalone server on addr and path.

Deprecated: use ws.new({address: addr, path: path}) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use ws.new({address: addr, path: path}) instead.

functions.name: send
functions.doc:
send queues a message on conn and reports whether it was queued; false
for anything that isn't a connection.

Deprecated: use conn.send(message) instead, which reports why sending
failed.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use conn.send(message) instead, which reports why sending failed.

methods.name: close
methods.doc:
close closes the connection for good and cancels reconnecting, and
returns at once: from then on send fails and no more messages arrive.
In the background, messages already passed to send go first, then a
close message with code (default 1000, a normal closure) and reason
(default ""), and the socket stays open until the peer answers with its
own close message, so the peer sees a clean close and every message sent
before it. Options: code (1000-1003, 1007-1014 or 3000-4999), reason (at
most 123 bytes), timeout, the most milliseconds to wait for the peer
before closing the socket anyway (default 2000; 0 closes it as soon as
the close message is out), and wait, true to return only once the socket
is closed. The queued messages and the close message get the same 10 s
write limit as any send. "close" fires after. Closing again, even while
the first close is still running, is a no-op that returns at once, or
with wait, once the socket is closed. Throws ValueError for an invalid code or reason.

methods.name: connected
methods.doc:
connected reports whether the connection is open.

Deprecated: use conn.isConnected() instead.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: data returns every stored value as a new object.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: delete removes the value stored under key.

methods.name: enableReconnect
methods.doc:
enableReconnect makes a client connection reopen itself after it drops,
retrying with a delay that doubles from 1 s up to 30 s, and firing "open"
each time it reconnects. close() stops it.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: get returns the value stored under key, or null.

methods.name: getAll
methods.doc:
getAll returns every stored value.

Deprecated: use conn.data() instead.

methods.name: getHeader
methods.doc:
getHeader returns an upgrade request header, or "" when it wasn't sent.

Deprecated: use conn.header(name) instead, which returns null for a
missing header.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use conn.header(name) instead, which returns null for a missing header.

methods.name: getHeaders
methods.doc:
getHeaders returns the upgrade request's headers.

Deprecated: use conn.headers() instead.

methods.name: header
methods.doc:
header returns a header of the upgrade request that opened a server-side
connection, matched case-insensitively, or null when it wasn't sent. The
"Remote-Addr" entry holds the client's address. Client connections have
no request headers.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc:
headers returns the upgrade request's headers as an object, with the
first value of each; empty for client connections.

methods.name: isConnected
methods.doc: isConnected reports whether the connection is currently open.

methods.name: off
methods.doc:
off removes a handler added with on and reports whether it was
registered.

methods.name: on
methods.doc:
on adds a handler for a connection event: "message" calls
fn(conn, message) for every message received (binary messages arrive as
strings), "close" calls fn(conn) when the connection closes from either
side, and "open" calls fn(conn) after a reconnect. Handlers run on the
connection's own thread; one that throws has its error printed and the
connection keeps running. Throws ValueError for an unknown event.

methods.name: onClose
methods.doc:
onClose replaces the connection's close handler.

Deprecated: use conn.on("close", fn) instead, which adds a handler.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use conn.on("close", fn) instead, which adds a handler.

methods.name: onMessage
methods.doc:
onMessage replaces the connection's message handler.

Deprecated: use conn.on("message", fn) instead, which adds a handler.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use conn.on("message", fn) instead, which adds a handler.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
send queues message for delivery: a string is sent as a text message,
byte[] as a binary message, and an object or array as JSON text. Fails
with StateError when the connection is closed and IOError when its send
queue is full because the peer isn't reading. Throws TypeError for other
message types.

methods.name: set
methods.doc:
set stores a value on the connection under key, for the program's own
bookkeeping (a user name, a room). broadcastWhere matches on it.

methods.name: shutdown
methods.doc:
shutdown closes the connection and cancels reconnecting.

Deprecated: use conn.close() instead, which now also cancels
reconnecting.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use conn.close() instead, which now also cancels reconnecting.

methods.name: allowAllOrigins
methods.doc:
allowAllOrigins accepts upgrades from pages on any origin. By default
only same-origin browser pages may connect.

methods.name: broadcast
methods.doc:
broadcast sends message to every connected client, skipping any whose
connection has closed or whose send queue is full. message is a string
(text), byte[] (binary) or an object or array (JSON text). Throws
TypeError for other message types.

methods.name: broadcastWhere
methods.signature: server.broadcastWhere(key: string, value: any, message: any)
methods.doc:
broadcastWhere sends message to every client whose stored value for key
(see conn.set) equals value, skipping closed connections. message takes
the same types as broadcast.

methods.name: connections
methods.doc: connections returns the currently connected clients.

methods.name: getConnections
methods.doc:
getConnections returns the connected clients.

Deprecated: use server.connections() instead.

methods.name: off
methods.doc:
off removes a handler added with on and reports whether it was
registered.

methods.name: on
methods.doc:
on adds a handler for a server event: "connect" and "disconnect" call
fn(conn), and "message" calls fn(conn, message) for every message from
any client. Handlers run on the connection's own thread; one that throws
has its error printed and the server keeps running. Throws ValueError for
an unknown event.

methods.name: onConnect
methods.doc:
onConnect replaces the server's connect handler.

Deprecated: use server.on("connect", fn) instead, which adds a handler.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use server.on("connect", fn) instead, which adds a handler.

methods.name: onDisconnect
methods.doc:
onDisconnect replaces the server's disconnect handler.

Deprecated: use server.on("disconnect", fn) instead, which adds a
handler.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use server.on("disconnect", fn) instead, which adds a handler.

methods.name: onMessage
methods.doc:
onMessage replaces the server's message handler.

Deprecated: use server.on("message", fn) instead, which adds a handler.
methods.deprecated: Deprecated: use server.on("message", fn) instead, which adds a handler.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
run serves WebSocket upgrades on the server's address and path and
blocks until stop() is called; run it in a thread to keep going. Fails
with NetworkError when the address can't be bound. Throws StateError when
the server is already running.

methods.name: runTLS
methods.signature: server.runTLS(certFile: string, keyFile: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
runTLS is run over TLS (wss://) with the certificate and key in the given
PEM files. Fails with NotFoundError or IOError when they can't be read.

methods.name: start
methods.doc:
start serves until stopped.

Deprecated: use server.run() instead.

methods.name: startTLS
methods.signature: server.startTLS(certFile: string, keyFile: string) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
startTLS serves over TLS until stopped.

Deprecated: use server.runTLS(certFile, keyFile) instead.

methods.name: stop
methods.doc:
stop closes the server and every connection, firing "disconnect" for
each. A run() call then returns. Stopping a server that isn't running
only closes its connections.

packages.name: xml
packages.description: Parse, query, edit and write XML documents.

functions.name: isValid
functions.doc: isValid reports whether xml.parse would accept text.

functions.name: parse
functions.doc:
parse reads an XML document from text. Query it with doc.find, doc.text
and doc.attr using paths such as "feed>entry>title": each name matches an
element at any depth below the previous one. Fails with ParseError,
naming the line, for malformed XML.

functions.name: parseFile
functions.doc:
parseFile reads and parses the XML file at path like xml.parse. Fails
with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be
read and ParseError when it isn't valid XML.

methods.name: attr
methods.doc:
attr returns the attribute name of the first element matching path, or
null when nothing matches or the element has no such attribute.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc:
clear deletes the text and children of the first element matching path,
in place, keeping the element and its attributes. Fails with
NotFoundError when nothing matches.

methods.name: count
methods.doc:
count returns how many child elements the first element matching path
has, or 0 when nothing matches. To count the elements matching a path,
use doc.findAll(path).len.

methods.name: find
methods.signature: document.find(path: string) -> {attrs: string[string], children: object[], name: string, text: string}?
methods.returns: {attrs: string[string], children: object[], name: string, text: string}?
methods.doc:
find returns the first element matching path as a record {name, text,
attrs, children}, or null when nothing matches. text is the element's
own text, joined and trimmed; attrs maps attribute names, prefixes
included ("xlink:href"), to values; children are records too.

methods.name: findAll
methods.signature: document.findAll(path: string) -> {attrs: string[string], children: object[], name: string, text: string}[]
methods.returns: {attrs: string[string], children: object[], name: string, text: string}[]
methods.doc:
findAll returns every element matching path as records (see doc.find),
in document order; [] when nothing matches.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
get returns the first element matching path as an object, or null.

Deprecated: use doc.find(path) instead.

methods.name: getAll
methods.doc:
getAll returns every element matching path as objects.

Deprecated: use doc.findAll(path) instead.

methods.name: getAttr

getAttr returns an attribute of the first element matching path, or
null.

Deprecated: use doc.attr(path, name) instead.

methods.name: getText
methods.doc:
getText returns the text of the first element matching path, or null.

Deprecated: use doc.text(path) instead.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: has reports whether any element matches path.

methods.name: hasAttr
methods.doc:
hasAttr reports whether the first element matching path has the
attribute name.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
remove deletes the first element matching path, and its children, in
place; text around it stays. Fails with NotFoundError when nothing
matches.

methods.name: root
methods.signature: document.root() -> {attrs: string[string], children: object[], name: string, text: string}?
methods.returns: {attrs: string[string], children: object[], name: string, text: string}?
methods.doc:
root returns the document's root element as a record with its whole
tree (see doc.find), or null for an empty document.

methods.name: setAttr
methods.signature: document.setAttr(path: string, name: string, value: any) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
setAttr sets the attribute name of the first element matching path, in
place. Fails with NotFoundError when nothing matches.

methods.name: setText
methods.signature: document.setText(path: string, value: any) -> result<unit, error>
methods.doc:
setText replaces the text of the first element matching path, in place,
keeping its child elements. Fails with NotFoundError when nothing
matches.

methods.name: text
methods.doc:
text returns the own text of the first element matching path, joined and
trimmed, or null when nothing matches.

methods.name: toArr
methods.doc:
toArr lists the top-level elements as objects.

Deprecated: use doc.root() instead.

methods.name: toStr
methods.doc:
toStr writes the document as XML text. Attributes are written in sorted
order and text is escaped; an empty document gives "".

functions.name: parse
functions.doc:
parse reads a YAML document from text into OSL values: mappings become
objects (keys as strings), sequences arrays, and scalars strings,
numbers, booleans or null; timestamps stay strings as written. An empty document is null. Fails with
ParseError, naming the line, for malformed YAML, duplicate keys and
recursive aliases.

functions.name: parseFile
functions.doc:
parseFile reads and parses the YAML file at path like yaml.parse. Fails
with NotFoundError, PermissionError or IOError when the file can't be
read and ParseError when it isn't valid YAML.

stringify encodes value as YAML text, with object keys in sorted order
and a trailing newline. Options: indent (spaces per nesting level, 2 to
16, default 4). Throws TypeError for values YAML can't represent, such
as functions, and ValueError for a value that contains itself.

packages.name: zip
packages.description: Create, inspect and extract ZIP and tar archives, and gzip files and strings.

functions.name: addFile
functions.signature: zip.addFile(path: string, file: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
addFile adds the file or directory at file to the existing ZIP archive at
path, replacing entries with the same names. Fails with NotFoundError when
the archive or file doesn't exist and ParseError when path isn't a ZIP
archive; on failure the archive is unchanged.

functions.name: compress
functions.signature: zip.compress(path: string, output: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
compress writes the file or directory at path to a new ZIP archive at
output, named after path's last element, replacing any file there. Fails
with NotFoundError when path doesn't exist and PermissionError or IOError
when something can't be read or written; a failed write leaves no archive
behind.

functions.name: compressString
functions.doc:
compressString gzips text and returns the result as standard base64, for
storing or sending compressed text as a string. Undo it with
zip.decompressString.

functions.name: copyFile
functions.doc:
copyFile copies the file src to dst, returning false on failure.

Deprecated: use fs.copy(from, to) instead.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use fs.copy(from, to) instead.

functions.name: create
functions.doc:
create writes an empty ZIP archive to path, replacing any file there, so
zip.addFile can fill it. Fails with NotFoundError when the directory
doesn't exist and PermissionError or IOError when it can't be written.

functions.name: decompress
functions.signature: zip.decompress(path: string, output: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
decompress extracts the ZIP archive at path into the directory output,
creating it if needed. Every entry is checked before anything is written.
Options: maxBytes (most bytes to write in total) and maxFiles (most
entries), both unlimited by default. Fails with NotFoundError when path
doesn't exist, ParseError for corrupt data or an entry that would land
outside output, UnsupportedError for symbolic link entries or an unknown
compression method, ValueError when the archive passes a limit and
PermissionError when a symbolic link already in output would redirect an
entry. A file that fails part way is removed, but files written before it
stay. Throws ValueError for a limit below 1.

functions.name: decompressLimited
functions.signature: zip.decompressLimited(zipPath: any, outputPath: any, ...limits: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
decompressLimited(zipPath, outputPath, maxBytes, maxFiles) extracts like
decompress, returning false when the archive has more than maxFiles
entries or expands past maxBytes.

Deprecated: use zip.decompress(path, output, {maxBytes: n, maxFiles: n})
instead, which reports why it failed.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use zip.decompress(path, output, {maxBytes: n, maxFiles: n}) instead, which reports why it failed.

functions.name: decompressString
functions.signature: zip.decompressString(text: string, options?: object) -> result<string, error>
functions.doc:
decompressString reverses zip.compressString: it decodes base64 text and
gunzips it. Option: maxBytes, the most bytes the result may have
(unlimited by default). Fails with ParseError when text isn't base64 or
the bytes aren't gzip data, and ValueError when the result passes
maxBytes. Throws ValueError for a maxBytes below 1.

functions.name: entries
functions.signature: zip.entries(path: string) -> result<{comment: string, compressedSize: int64, isDir: boolean, modified: int64, name: string, size: int64}[], error>
functions.returns: result<{comment: string, compressedSize: int64, isDir: boolean, modified: int64, name: string, size: int64}[], error>
functions.doc:
entries lists the members of the ZIP archive at path as records with the
keys name, isDir, size and compressedSize (bytes), modified (unix
milliseconds) and comment. Fails with NotFoundError when path doesn't
exist and ParseError when it isn't a ZIP archive.

functions.name: extractFile
functions.signature: zip.extractFile(path: string, name: string, output: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
extractFile writes the archive entry named name to the file output,
replacing any file there. Option: maxBytes, the most bytes to write.
Fails with NotFoundError when the archive or entry doesn't exist,
ValueError when the entry is a directory or larger than maxBytes and
ParseError for corrupt data; a failed write leaves no file behind. Throws
ValueError for a maxBytes below 1.

functions.name: fileInfo
functions.doc:
fileInfo describes one entry, or returns null when the archive or entry
can't be found.

Deprecated: use zip.entries(path) instead and pick the entry by name.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use zip.entries(path) instead and pick the entry by name.

functions.name: gunzip
functions.signature: zip.gunzip(path: string, output: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
gunzip decompresses the gzip file at path into the file output, replacing
any file there. Option: maxBytes, the most bytes to write (unlimited by
default). Fails with NotFoundError when path doesn't exist, ParseError
when it isn't valid gzip data, ValueError when it expands past maxBytes
and PermissionError or IOError for other file errors; a failed write
leaves no file behind. Throws ValueError for a maxBytes below 1.

functions.name: gunzipLimited
functions.signature: zip.gunzipLimited(sourcePath: any, outputPath: any, maxOutputBytes: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
gunzipLimited gunzips like gunzip, returning false when the output would
pass maxOutputBytes.

Deprecated: use zip.gunzip(path, output, {maxBytes: n}) instead, which
reports why it failed.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use zip.gunzip(path, output, {maxBytes: n}) instead, which reports why it failed.

functions.name: gzip
functions.signature: zip.gzip(path: string, output: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
gzip compresses the file at path into a gzip file at output, replacing any
file there. Options: maxInputBytes (most bytes to read from path) and
maxBytes (most bytes to write), both unlimited by default. Fails with
NotFoundError when path doesn't exist, ValueError when a limit is passed
and PermissionError or IOError for other file errors; a failed write
leaves no file behind. Throws ValueError for a limit below 1.

functions.name: gzipLimited
functions.signature: zip.gzipLimited(sourcePath: any, outputPath: any, ...limits: any) -> boolean
functions.doc:
gzipLimited(sourcePath, outputPath, maxInputBytes, maxOutputBytes) gzips
like gzip, returning false when the input or output passes its limit.

Deprecated: use zip.gzip(path, output, {maxInputBytes: n, maxBytes: n})
instead, which reports why it failed.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use zip.gzip(path, output, {maxInputBytes: n, maxBytes: n}) instead, which reports why it failed.

functions.name: list
functions.doc:
list returns the archive's entries as objects, or [] when it can't be
read.

Deprecated: use zip.entries(path) instead, which reports why it failed.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use zip.entries(path) instead, which reports why it failed.

functions.name: removeFile
functions.signature: zip.removeFile(path: string, name: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
removeFile removes the entry named name from the ZIP archive at path.
Removing an entry the archive doesn't have does nothing, like fs.remove.
Fails with NotFoundError when the archive doesn't exist and ParseError
when path isn't a ZIP archive; on failure the archive is unchanged.

functions.name: statistics
functions.doc:
statistics totals the archive's entries, or returns null when it can't be
read.

Deprecated: use zip.entries(path) instead and total the sizes.
functions.deprecated: Deprecated: use zip.entries(path) instead and total the sizes.

functions.name: tar
functions.signature: zip.tar(path: string, output: string) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
tar writes the file or directory at path to a new tar archive at output,
named after path's last element, replacing any file there. Only regular
files and directories are stored. Fails like zip.compress; a failed write
leaves no archive behind.

functions.name: untar
functions.signature: zip.untar(path: string, output: string, options?: object) -> result<unit, error>
functions.doc:
untar extracts the tar archive at path into the directory output, like
zip.decompress, and takes the same maxBytes and maxFiles options. Only
regular files and directories are supported; other entry types such as
links fail with UnsupportedError before anything is written.
